source.runId: soak walk seed 1786446166374 (200 actions, no category weights) — wedged at the final save/reload oracle checkpoint

violation.message: THE APP DEADLOCKS WHEN A FILE IS OPENED WHILE THE BACKGROUND GATHER-REFRESH RECALCULATION IS RUNNING. Measured: the walk stopped printing at `[oracle checkpoint] after step 200`; the PAGE stayed alive (DOM answered, window title read `oracle-save-13232-1.cala`, no native dialogs open) but every Tauri invoke timed out. Two out-of-process stack dumps a minute apart were byte-identical. Main thread: `open_file` -> `restamp_workbook_name_casing` HOLDING `named_ranges` + `tables` + `table_names`, WAITING for `sheet_names`. Gather worker (`calp_commands::queue_gather_refresh` -> `calculation::recalculate_sheet_values`): HOLDING `grid` + `grids` + `sheet_names` + `style_registry`, WAITING for `tables`. Each holds what the other waits for. No panic, no crash, nothing in the app log after the checkpoint's own DIGEST line -- the message pump stops with the main thread and the window goes Not Responding. Third instance of this class in the programme and the SECOND on this seed. THE GUARD THAT EXISTS FOR THIS SHAPE WAS GREEN: `no_lock_is_held_while_a_grid_lock_is_acquired` treated `.ok()` as consuming the guard, but `LockResult::ok()` MOVES the guard into an `Option` -- so all three of restamp's held guards read as temporaries that had already died.

repro.description: RACE, so a trace reproduces it probabilistically rather than deterministically: `E2E_MANUAL=1 SOAK_SEED=1786446166374 SOAK_ACTIONS=200 SOAK_ORACLE_EVERY=25 npx playwright test --project=soak --grep "random walk"` -- the walk creates 14 tables and 8 charts, and the save/reload oracle's `open_file` at the final checkpoint lands while the gather-refresh worker is recalculating. DETERMINISTIC unit-level reproduction, which is what the fix is validated against: `state_digest_lock_order_tests::restamping_name_casing_does_not_hold_tables_while_it_waits_for_sheet_names` holds `sheet_names` (playing the pass), runs `restamp_workbook_name_casing` on another thread, and probes whether `tables` is still reachable -- with a deadline, so it FAILS rather than hangs. Its non-vacuity partner `the_tables_probe_itself_can_fail_the_way_the_defect_did` plants the pre-fix body and asserts the probe says no.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: A lock-order inversion between the load path and the background recalculation pass, on a PAIR no census asked about. The crate already had one canonical order (`grid` before `grids`, and no lock held while a grid lock is acquired) enforced crate-wide; nothing enforced the order of the four NAMING authorities relative to `sheet_names`, and the pass takes `sheet_names` FIRST while seven functions took one of `tables` / `table_names` / `named_ranges` / `style_registry` before it. `restamp_workbook_name_casing` was additionally inverted against the grid pair and escaped the existing census only because of the `.ok()` hole.
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/src-tauri/src/persistence.rs (restamp_workbook_name_casing) + the ten other inverted call sites + app/src-tauri/src/state_digest_lock_order_tests.rs (CONSUMING, and a census for the new pair)

fix.diffSummary: ONE ORDER, TAKEN FROM THE THREAD THAT CANNOT CHANGE IT. `recalculate_sheet_values` runs on a background thread and takes `grid`, `grids`, `sheet_names`, `style_registry`, ... `tables`, `table_names`, `named_ranges`; everything else now agrees with it. `restamp_workbook_name_casing` takes the two grid locks FIRST and then the four authorities in the pass's order (it used to take the authorities first and the grid locks last). Ten other functions that held one of the four and then asked for `sheet_names` hoist a clone of `sheet_names` above it: `tables::{delete_table, set_totals_row_function, toggle_totals_row, convert_to_range, set_calculated_column}`, `calp_commands::apply_override_value_to_grid`, `named_ranges::{get_named_range_for_selection, resolve_named_range_coords}`, `tracing::{trace_precedents, trace_dependents}`, `commands::print::get_print_data`, `commands::data::remove_duplicates`, and the four `commands::structure::{insert,delete}_{rows,columns}_impl`. `.ok()` is out of `CONSUMING` (it moves the guard into an Option, it does not release it) with a planted-body tooth that fails if it returns. New crate-wide census `no_function_holds_a_name_authority_while_acquiring_sheet_names` over all four pairs, its direction pinned to the pass by `the_recalculation_pass_still_takes_sheet_names_first`, plus a live deadlock probe and its non-vacuity partner.

source.runId: sheet-surface sweep, 2026-08-13 — found by reading `hide_sheet` against its three callers while adding sheet actions to the walker

violation.message: HIDING THE ACTIVE SHEET LEAVES THE BACKEND ON THE HIDDEN SHEET, SO EDITS GO TO THE WRONG SHEET. `hide_sheet` set the visibility flag and RETURNED a recommended new active index without touching `state.active_sheet` or any per-sheet mirror -- its own doc comment said "frontend should call set_active_sheet if it changed". None of the three callers did: `SheetTabs.handleHide` passes `backendHandledSwitch: true` ("Backend already swapped - just sync frontend state"), `ScriptNotebook/lib/deferredActionHost.setSheetVisibility` comments "Hiding the active sheet makes the backend switch", and the broker's `api.setSheetVisibility` goes through `announceSheetsChanged`, which dispatches `setActiveSheet` into the frontend store. All three therefore moved the FRONTEND onto the recommended sheet while the backend still had the hidden sheet active -- and every cell read and every cell write goes to the active sheet. The tab strip highlights Sheet1, the canvas paints Sheet2's data, and typing writes into the sheet the user just hid. Excel's rule settles it: a hidden sheet cannot be the active sheet (no tab to select; `Activate` raises in VBA).

repro.description: TWO ACTIONS. (1) Add a sheet (which makes it active). (2) Right-click its tab and choose Hide. Before: the tab strip and the grid claim to be on Sheet1 while `get_active_sheet` still answers with the hidden sheet, so `get_cell_value`/`update_cell` operate on it -- typing appears to edit Sheet1 and edits the hidden sheet. After: the backend performs the switch through `activate_sheet`, so the index, the grid mirror, the column widths, the row heights, the merged regions and the user-hidden sets all move together. Unit-level: `sheets::hidden_active_sheet_tests::{hiding_the_active_sheet_activates_a_visible_one, the_grid_mirror_moves_with_it, the_sheet_it_lands_on_is_visible}`. NOTE: `TestRunner`'s "Hide and unhide a sheet" hides the sheet it has just added -- i.e. the ACTIVE sheet -- every time it runs, and asserted only `visibility == "hidden"`, so the defect sat underneath a passing test.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: A command that returns a RECOMMENDATION into a codebase where every caller reads it as a report of what happened. The four other sheet-structure commands (`add`, `delete`, `move`, `copy`) all write `active_sheet` and swap the mirrors themselves; `hide_sheet` was the only one that did not, and the asymmetry was invisible because the return type is identical.

fix.diffSummary: `hide_sheet` splits into a `hide_sheet_inner(&AppState, &FileState, ..)` body (so the switch has a unit tier) that computes the target with every guard scoped to a block, releases them, and then calls `activate_sheet` -- the ONE implementation of the swap, the same one BUG-0043 extracted. A source census fails the build if it ever assigns `active_sheet` itself instead. SECOND DEFECT, found by the test fixture: `ensure_vec_len(&mut sheet_visibility, n)` pads with `String::default()`, i.e. the EMPTY STRING, while every reader compares against the literal "visible" -- `SheetTabs` renders `sheets.filter(s => s.visibility === "visible")`, `hide_sheet` counts the visible sheets that way, and `next_sheet`/`previous_sheet` skip anything else. A padded slot is therefore a sheet with no tab that the workbook believes is neither hidden nor visible, and `build_sheet_list`'s `.unwrap_or("visible")` cannot repair it because the slot is `Some("")` rather than `None`. All four padding sites go through a new `ensure_visibility_len`. INSTRUMENT: the walker snapshot now carries `backendActiveSheet` and `sheetVisibility`, and a new cheap invariant `active-sheet-agrees` fails the walk when the two halves of the app name different active sheets, or when the active sheet is not visible -- a class no digest oracle can see, because the digest is assembled entirely from AppState and a backend that is wrong in a self-consistent way passes all three. `sheet.hide` is now a walker action.

source.runId: soak walk seed 1786446166374 (200 actions, no weights); reproduced independently on 90070001 (sheet:10) and 90070002 (sheet:8,chart:4)

violation.message: TABLES DO NOT FOLLOW THEIR SHEET THROUGH A MOVE OR A COPY. `state.tables` is keyed by sheet INDEX, and it is the one sheet-index-keyed store that is NOT in `remap_sheet_keyed_stores` -- `delete_sheet` re-keys it inline, because the same pass has to drop the deleted sheet's table NAMES out of `table_names` and a generic remap cannot do that half. `move_sheet` and `copy_sheet` therefore re-keyed every OTHER per-sheet store (comments, scenarios, outlines, conditional formats, data validations, cell types, controls, protection, AUTOFILTERS, spill tracking, reports, and the floating slicer/timeline/chart/sparkline stores) and left this one where it was. The measured symptom is the AutoFilter link, because `auto_filters` DID move: on reload `relink_autofilter_owner` looks for the owning table under the filter's sheet index, finds none, and the link is gone (`tables.<id>.autoFilterId: <id> -> <absent>`) -- or worse, finds a DIFFERENT sheet's table and hands it the filter (`<A> -> <B>`, seed 90070001; `<absent> -> <id>`, seed 90070002). The lost link is only the visible half. The table itself is now registered against another sheet, and that registry is what every structured reference (`=SUM(Table1[Amount])`) resolves through, what the save path writes per sheet, and what the AutoFilter, totals-row and calculated-column commands look the table up in.

repro.description: NINE ACTIONS, confirmed by the shrinker (30 replays, 20 clean passes, verdict=confirmed): `sheet.add` -> (noise) -> `table.create` -> `sheet.hide {tabIndex:1}` -> `sheet.move {from:0,to:1}`, then save and reload. Replay: E2E_MANUAL=1 SOAK_TRACE=tests/regression/repros/BUG-0047.trace.json SOAK_EXPECT_FAIL=1 npx playwright test --project=soak --grep "Trace replay". The essential pair is `table.create` followed by any `sheet.move` that renumbers the table's sheet; the hide only makes the move land somewhere interesting. Unit-level: `sheets::tables_remap_tests::{a_move_carries_the_table_and_re_stamps_its_sheet_index, a_copy_shifts_everything_at_or_above_the_insertion_point, every_structural_command_re_keys_the_table_store}`.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: One store outside the shared helper. §3bn's sweep asked 'is this store keyed by sheet index, and does the helper reach it' and `tables` answered the first question yes and the second no -- it has its own inline re-key in `delete_sheet`, so it looked handled. Nothing asked the two commands that do not delete anything.

fix.diffSummary: New `remap_tables_store(state, effect, remap)` re-keys the store and re-stamps the `sheet_index` each `Table` carries -- both halves, because a key that moved without the field is the same divergence one layer down. `move_sheet` and `copy_sheet` call it with the very remap closures they already pass to `remap_sheet_keyed_stores`; `delete_sheet` keeps its inline pass, which also has to drop the deleted sheet's names out of `table_names`. A source census (`every_structural_command_re_keys_the_table_store`) checks all three by name, because 'it is a sheet-keyed store' is exactly the reasoning that missed it. Lock order: the call sites already hold `sheet_names`, and taking `tables` under it is the canonical direction the BUG-0045 census enforces.

source.runId: sheet-surface sweep, 2026-08-13 — found by asking BUG-0046's question of the DELETE side

violation.message: DELETING A SHEET CAN LEAVE A WORKBOOK WITH NO VISIBLE SHEET, AND CAN LEAVE THE ACTIVE SHEET ON A HIDDEN ONE. `hide_sheet` has always refused to hide the last VISIBLE sheet; `delete_sheet` only ever checked that at least one SHEET remained (`sheet_names.len() <= 1`). Hide Sheet1, delete Sheet2, and that guard is satisfied while the workbook is left with a single HIDDEN sheet: no tab to click, and an active index naming a sheet the user cannot look at. Excel's wording is exactly the distinction it was missing -- "a workbook must contain at least one visible worksheet". Separately, the index arithmetic that picks the post-delete active sheet is pure bookkeeping, so deleting the sheet beside a hidden one lands the user ON the hidden one even when other visible sheets exist.

repro.description: TWO ACTIONS, from the sheet tab context menu. (1) Right-click Sheet1 > Hide. (2) Right-click Sheet2 > Delete. Before: the delete succeeds and the workbook has one sheet, hidden -- the tab strip is empty and the grid is showing a sheet with no tab. After: the delete is refused with "Cannot delete the last visible sheet". The second half: with three sheets, hide Sheet2, then delete Sheet3 -- before, the active index lands on the hidden Sheet2; after, it walks on to a visible one. Unit-level: `sheets::hidden_active_sheet_tests::{a_delete_that_would_leave_no_visible_sheet_is_counted_as_zero, the_landing_sheet_skips_a_hidden_preference, delete_sheet_asks_both_questions}`.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: "At least one sheet" and "at least one VISIBLE sheet" are different tests, and only one of the two commands that can violate the rule was making the right one. The asymmetry survived because `delete_sheet` takes eight `State<T>` arguments and cannot be driven from a unit test, so the rule was never asked of it.

fix.diffSummary: Two pure functions with their own unit tier -- `visible_sheets_after_removing` (the refusal) and `nearest_visible_sheet` (the landing) -- plus `sheet_is_visible`, which reads a SHORT `sheet_visibility` as visible exactly as `build_sheet_list` does. `delete_sheet` calls both, and a source census (`delete_sheet_asks_both_questions`) fails the build if either call goes away, because the command itself cannot be tested directly. Non-vacuity partners pin that the landing walk is a no-op when the preferred sheet is already visible, and that a short visibility vector does not make a workbook undeletable.

source.runId: soak walk seed 1786446166374 (200 actions), on the build that had just fixed BUG-0047

violation.message: THE UNDO ORACLE REPORTS A FALSE PRODUCT DEFECT WHEN A SHEET IS ADDED WHILE THE UNDO HISTORY IS EMPTY. Measured: "Undoing 22 steps did not restore the checkpoint state. 2 differences; first: sheetNames[2]: \"<absent>\" -> \"Sheet3\"" -- and both digest differences were that one EMPTY sheet. The walk had ADDED Sheet3 inside the checkpoint window; adding a sheet is not undoable (Excel parity, BUG-0005), so no number of undo steps returns to the checkpoint and the window is not decidable. The oracle decided it anyway. `stepsBackToBaseline` asks whether a wholesale clear DISCARDED anything (`clearedTotal`, a count of TRANSACTIONS), and a structure change made while the stack is already empty discards nothing -- so the counter does not move, the oracle sees no clear, winds the history back and reports the sheet the walk added as an undo defect. This is the exact false alarm BUG-0005's fix removed for the non-empty case, on the one case it left standing; it is a harness defect, and its cost is a triage cycle plus a lost walk each time it fires.

repro.description: Any walk that (a) reaches a checkpoint with an empty or freshly-cleared undo stack, (b) pushes some ordinary transactions, and (c) adds/deletes/renames/moves/copies a sheet in the same window. Seed 1786446166374 at 200 actions does it at the checkpoint after step 125. Deterministic unit-level reproduction: `undoHistoryHorizon.test.ts::says so when the clear discarded NOTHING because the stack was empty` -- baseline {clearedTotal: 4, clearsTotal: 1}, now {clearedTotal: 4, clearsTotal: 2}: `clearedTotal` has not moved and the window must still be undecidable. Its partner covers the non-empty-baseline branch. Sabotage-checked: reverting the decision to `cleared > 0` fails exactly those two.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The counter answered a question next to the one that was being asked. `cleared_total` was introduced to tell "a structure change ended the history" from "the cap dropped it" and "the walk undid past it", and it does -- as long as the history had something in it. The fact the caller actually needs is whether a clear HAPPENED, which is not the same number.

fix.diffSummary: `UndoStack` gains `clears_total`, incremented on EVERY `clear()` regardless of what it discarded, alongside the transaction-counting `cleared_total` -- kept separate so `no_phantom_clear_on_a_pristine_workbook` keeps meaning what it says. `get_undo_state` reports it as `clearsTotal`; `stepsBackToBaseline` decides on `clears > 0` and uses `cleared` only to say how much was lost ("1 clear(s), 0 transaction(s) discarded"). Two new cases in `undoHistoryHorizon.test.ts` cover both branches (empty and non-empty baseline) with `clearedTotal` deliberately unchanged, and they fail when the decision is reverted.

source.runId: soak walk seed 90070001, 250 actions, SOAK_CATEGORY_WEIGHTS=sheet:10, on the build carrying the BUG-0045/0046/0047/0049 fixes

violation.message: SHEET VISIBILITY (AND TAB COLOUR) ARE PERSISTED MUTATIONS WITH NO UNDO ENTRY AND NO HISTORY INVALIDATION. Measured: "Undoing 26 steps did not restore the checkpoint state. 1 differences; first: sheets[1].visibility: \"visible\" -> \"hidden\"" -- the sheet was VISIBLE at the checkpoint, the walk hid it inside the window, and undoing the whole window left it hidden. `hide_sheet`, `unhide_sheet` and `set_tab_color` all construct `DocumentEffect::mutates` (the state IS saved into the .cala), take no `undo_stack`, record nothing, and -- unlike the five structural commands -- do not call `invalidate_undo_history_for_sheet_structure` either. THE DEFECT IS REAL UNDER EITHER PARITY READING, and only the fix differs: if Excel undoes a sheet hide (see the evidence note below, which could not settle it from any source), the commands owe an undo entry that restores `sheet_visibility` / `tab_colors`; if it does not, they owe the history invalidation the other sheet commands make, so the oracle declines the window instead of deciding it. What is NOT defensible is the current third state, where the history stays intact across a change undo cannot reverse.

repro.description: THREE ACTIONS. (1) Type a value into Sheet1!A1. (2) Right-click Sheet2's tab and choose Hide. (3) Press Ctrl+Z. The cell edit is undone and Sheet2 stays hidden, with no indication that anything was skipped -- and pressing Ctrl+Z again walks further back through a history that no longer describes the workbook. Same shape for Unhide and for a tab colour. Walk-level: E2E_MANUAL=1 SOAK_SEED=90070001 SOAK_ACTIONS=250 SOAK_CATEGORY_WEIGHTS="sheet:10" SOAK_ORACLE_EVERY=25 npx playwright test --project=soak --grep "random walk" -- fails at the checkpoint after step 125. NOT SUPPRESSED: no `KNOWN_ISSUES` entry was added, so sheet-weighted walks will keep reporting it until it is decided.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED, and the OWNER CALL is decided in favour of an undo ENTRY. The two candidates were 'record a CustomRestore' and 'end the history the way the five structural sheet commands do', and what settles it is that the argument FOR ending the history does not reach these three. Read `invalidate_undo_history_for_sheet_structure`'s own doc: the five end the history because an undo entry names its sheet by INDEX and those five RENUMBER every index (or, for a rename, rewrite every formula that spells the name), so a queued entry silently comes to describe a different sheet. Hiding a sheet renumbers nothing and rewrites nothing -- it assigns one element of a parallel Vec in place -- so every queued entry still describes exactly the sheet it was recorded on, and the hazard the invalidation exists to prevent is ABSENT. With the structural argument gone what remains is an asymmetry of cost: ending the history destroys every undo step the user had accumulated, recording an entry costs a few bytes. `hide_sheet_inner` already takes that same cheap direction one line over for the dirty flag ('a false positive, which is the cheap direction').
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/src-tauri/src/sheets.rs (hide_sheet_inner, unhide_sheet, set_tab_color) — either a `CustomRestore` payload for `sheet_visibility` / `tab_colors` plus its apply arm in undo_commands.rs, or a call to `invalidate_undo_history_for_sheet_structure`. OWNER CALL: which one is Excel parity.

fix.diffSummary: A new `"sheet_tab_state"` CustomRestore kind carries `{ visibility, tab_colors, active_sheet }` -- whole vectors (their LENGTH is state: `ensure_visibility_len` pads them lazily and `build_sheet_list` reads them by index, so a partial restore could leave the list disagreeing with itself), each field `Option` so 'this change did not touch it' is expressible, exactly like `UserHiddenSnapshot`. `hide_sheet_inner`, `unhide_sheet_inner` and `set_tab_color_inner` record it; the latter two are NEW `_inner` splits, added for the same reason `hide_sheet_inner` exists (a `State<T>` command has no unit tier). Every recording happens with NO other state lock held -- `record_custom_restore` takes `undo_stack`, which the crate's canonical order puts ahead of the grid locks -- and only when something actually changed, so a no-op hide/unhide/recolour and a REFUSED hide burn no undo step. Registry row: domain `Sheets` (the translator fans it out to "sheets:refresh" + SHEET_CHANGED, which is what makes the tab strip re-read), `defer: true` -- not a preference: undoing the hide of the ACTIVE sheet puts the user back through `sheets::activate_sheet`, which takes grid/grids/widths/heights/merges, all of which `apply_changes` still holds during the inline phase. `active_sheet` is recorded ONLY by hide (the only one that moves the user) and the restore refuses to follow it onto a sheet that is out of range or hidden, under the same rules as `activation_target`. 15 unit tests in `sheet_tab_state_undo_tests.rs` (undo/redo of all three, the standing-point follow and its non-active control, the hidden-target refusal, three no-op cases, a refused hide) plus a source census that every command recording persisted tab state names the kind, with a synthetic-source self-test proving the detector fires in both directions and that the brace matcher stops at the right function. `restore_registry_tests` (which fired on the new kind and had to be taught it) pins the domain and the defer flag. PROVED LIVE from a cold app through the REAL tab context menu and REAL Ctrl+Z (`sheet-tab-state-undo.spec.ts`): the hidden tab's absence is asserted FIRST so the probe is shown able to report the broken answer, then the tab returns, the backend and the rendered strip agree on the active index, and the formula bar reads a mark that only exists on the restored sheet. Paired control: undoing the hide of a NON-active sheet restores it and moves nobody.

bugs.evidenceNote: EXCEL'S ANSWER IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE, and this note says so rather than manufacturing a confirmation (2026-08-15 Excel-parity evidence pass). Microsoft Support, Microsoft Learn, Microsoft Q&A and the established secondary literature (Ablebits, tips.net, DavidRingstrom, MrExcel) were searched: NO source states either that Excel undoes a sheet hide or that it does not. Microsoft's own 'Undo, redo, or repeat an action' does not mention sheet operations at all. What IS corroborated is the surrounding family: DELETING a worksheet clears the undo stack (unanimous across independent sources), as does running a macro (first-party). THE FILING'S ORIGINAL EVIDENCE WAS WEAK AND HAS BEEN REPLACED: 'the Undo button is available after Format > Hide & Unhide > Hide Sheet' does not show that Ctrl+Z will undo the HIDE -- the button stays enabled for the PREVIOUS action whenever the stack was neither cleared nor appended to, which is precisely the ambiguous middle case. WHAT CARRIES THE READING IS THE MECHANISM, not a document. The operations documented to clear the stack are those that change a sheet's EXISTENCE or IDENTITY (delete; arguably insert/rename/move): prior undo records name sheets, and once a sheet is destroyed those records are unreplayable, so Excel discards the stack. Hiding is not in that class -- `Worksheet.Visible` is a property of a sheet that CONTINUES TO EXIST and stays referenceable by formulas (Microsoft's 'Hide or Unhide worksheets' stresses that hidden sheets' data 'can still be referenced from other worksheets and workbooks'). No prior undo record is invalidated by a hide. On the mechanism it belongs with ordinary undoable formatting, like tab colour. Confidence that Excel specifically undoes Format > Hide & Unhide > Hide Sheet: LOW-MODERATE -- one notch BELOW the filing's original 'moderate', deliberately lowered rather than raised. A trap for whoever revisits this: thebricks.com's 'How to Undo Hide in Excel' claims Ctrl+Z recovers a DELETED worksheet. That is false and contradicts Microsoft and every established secondary source; it is AI-generated SEO filler and ranks highly on this exact query. OWNER DECISION 2026-08-15, taken knowingly under that uncertainty and under the standing tiebreaker 'as similar to Excel as possible': KEEP THE SHIPPED FIX, NO CODE CHANGE. The argument does not depend on the unanswered question. The shipped undoable `sheet_tab_state` CustomRestore is EXACT PARITY if Excel undoes hide, and a HARMLESS SUPERSET if it does not (Ctrl+Z does slightly more than Excel, loses no user work, surprises nobody). The alternative fix -- invalidating the undo history on every hide -- is strictly worse under uncertainty: it DESTROYS user-recoverable history to model a behaviour nobody has confirmed. Only the pre-fix third state (history intact across a change undo cannot reverse) was broken under every reading, and that is what the fix removed. ONE CONSEQUENCE TO KEEP VISIBLE (§22b): the invariant walker's undo round-trip oracle decided 0 round-trips in 5 of 6 recent seed runs because walks hit workbook-structure actions that clear the stack. Hide NOT clearing the stack is what keeps hide-heavy walks decidable. Moving hide into the invalidating family would thin that oracle's evidence further.

source.runId: invariant walk seed 90080002, INVARIANT_CATEGORY_WEIGHTS=sheet:6,chart:4,table:4, on the build carrying the BUG-0045/0046/0047/0048/0049 fixes

violation.message: THE "TABLE DESIGN" CONTEXTUAL TAB SURVIVES THE DELETE OF THE LAST TABLE WHEN A SHEET HAS BEEN RENAMED IN BETWEEN. Measured: 'Contextual tab "Table Design" is visible but at least one table must exist. Found: slicers=0, charts=0, tables=0, pivots=0, timelines=0, sparklines=0'. The backend has NO tables and the ribbon still offers a tab whose every button addresses an object that no longer exists — the same end state BUG-0026 and the `syncDesignTabToTables` fix (soak seed 20260810) were about, reached through a door those fixes do not cover. The shrinker kept the rename: removing it makes the trace pass, so it is load-bearing and not incidental.

repro.description: FOUR ACTIONS, confirmed by the shrinker (30 replays, 22 clean passes, verdict=confirmed): `table.create` -> `sheet.rename {tabIndex: 0}` -> `table.select-into` -> `table.delete`. Replay: E2E_MANUAL=1 SOAK_TRACE=tests/regression/repros/BUG-0051.trace.json SOAK_EXPECT_FAIL=1 npx playwright test --project=soak --grep "Trace replay". NOTE ON REACHABILITY: renaming sheet 0 only became generatable in this pass — the walker's `sheet.rename` picked `pickInt(rng, 1, n-1)` and could never rename the first sheet, which is the one everything else refers to.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: ESTABLISHED, and it is NEITHER of the two filed candidates -- no probe was needed, the source says it. `deleteTableAsync` DOES succeed and DOES refresh its own cache; what it never does is announce the `objects` domain. The only thing that re-derives the contextual tab is `syncDesignTabToTables`, which runs on TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED, which is dispatched by the `objects` domain and by nothing else in the delete path. `announceObjectCascade` in the Table store named only ["slicer", "ribbonFilter"]; TWO CALLERS papered over it by emitting TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED BY HAND after awaiting the store (TableDesignTab's Delete and Convert-to-Range buttons), so the defect was invisible from the screen a human uses and reproducible from every other route -- a script, an MCP tool, the E2E walker. WHY THE CENSUS THAT EXISTS FOR THIS DID NOT CATCH IT: the two halves of `cascadeAnnouncementCensus.test.ts` contradicted each other. Its cascade half runs off `requiredDomainsFor`, which DELETES the owner's own domain from the required set on the reasoning that a route re-reading its own cache needs no announcement for itself -- and `objects` IS the Table's own domain. Its selection half, meanwhile, recorded in its own `why` that the tab 'is re-derived ... on TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED, which the `objects` domain dispatches'. One half excused exactly what the other half depended on. AND THE RENAME: the shrinker was right that removing `sheet.rename` made the trace pass, but it is not load-bearing to the DEFECT -- it was load-bearing to the SETUP. The walker's `table.create` used a raw `create_table` invoke, which leaves the frontend cache empty, so `table.select-into` could not register the tab at all; the rename fired SHEET_CHANGED, whose Table handler calls `refreshCache()`, and that -- nothing about renaming -- is what made the tab appear so it could then survive.
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/extensions/Table/lib/tableStore.ts (deleteTableAsync) + app/extensions/Table/index.ts (the SHEET_CHANGED handler, which refreshes the cache without re-deriving the tab) + app/extensions/Table/handlers/selectionHandler.ts

fix.diffSummary: The STORE announces its own domain change: `announceObjectCascade` becomes `announceTableObjectChange` and names ["objects", "slicer", "ribbonFilter"], so the delete and the convert-to-range make the identical announcement an out-of-band MCP table delete already made. The two hand-written TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED emits in TableDesignTab are DELETED -- they were a second source of truth for 'the table list changed' that only the button path had. THE CENSUS IS REPAIRED SO THE CLASS CANNOT RECUR: `SelectionOwner` gains `reconcileDomain` (the refresh domain whose fan-out reaches the reconciliation) and a mandatory `reconcileDomainWhy` for the null case, and a new rule `unannouncedReconciliations` requires EVERY delete route for that kind to announce it -- own domain or not, which is precisely the check `auditRoutes` structurally cannot make. Non-vacuity is asserted (exactly one owner exercises the rule today) and a synthetic-source teeth case proves the detector fires, that the fixed shape is accepted, that `ownDomain` + a self-refresh does NOT excuse it, and that a null domain with no reason is reported. The new rule immediately found a SECOND, INDEPENDENT instance -- but it was a false report: `announceObjectCascade` in `scriptHost/host.ts` reaches "objects" through a SECOND hop (`announceObjectsChanged`) that the analyser's one-hop rule did not follow. `domainsAnnounced` now follows announcement helpers transitively, which keeps the closure at 'the announcement helpers this route reaches' rather than the whole module. HARNESS: `table.create` in the walker goes through `createTableAsync` and emits TABLE_CREATED, the way Insert > Table does. The raw invoke it replaces left the frontend not knowing a table existed, which made the walk blind to the whole contextual-tab surface unless an unrelated action happened to refresh the cache. PROVED LIVE from a cold app: the ribbon is asserted to be SHOWING 'Table Design' before the delete (so 'it is gone' cannot pass vacuously), the backend is asserted to hold zero tables after it, and the rendered ribbon no longer offers the tab. TEETH: with the fix sabotaged on the running build and the WebView reloaded, the same live test reports `["Home", "Page Layout", "Controls", "Table Design"]` with zero tables; the file was then restored byte-identically (sha256 8ac813074b0b42914c0044001e22801efa3fa1940d88d30402d40199c10dc2bf) and it passes again. The committed 4-action trace `repros/BUG-0051.trace.json` now replays clean.

source.runId: live per-animation-frame sampling in app/e2e/journeys/sheet-tab-state-undo.spec.ts, written to attack BUG-0043's atomicity claim rather than re-read it

violation.message: A SHEET SWITCH IS NOT ATOMIC ON SCREEN: for a two-frame window the tab strip paints the NEW sheet as active while the canvas is still painting the OLD sheet's cells. Measured per animation frame, with the strip's own painted font-weight and a canvas `getImageData` probe of a cell that has ink on one sheet and not the other: undo-of-an-off-sheet-edit 21-71 ms, an ORDINARY TAB CLICK 60-67 ms, across three runs on the same build. It is therefore NOT undo's defect -- `applyRestoreToTheView` deliberately reuses the tab click's channel and measures no worse than it, usually better -- but a property of every sheet switch in the app. `followBackendSheetActivation` dispatches sheet:beforeSwitch -> the grid sheet context -> sheet:normalSwitch with no `await` between them, so the tab strip repaints on the next frame; the canvas cannot repaint until `refreshCells()` has completed a backend round trip.

repro.description: TWO ACTIONS, no scripting. (1) On Sheet2, type something into D1 so the two sheets are visually distinguishable. (2) Click Sheet1's tab, then click Sheet2's tab while sampling. For ~60 ms the Sheet2 tab is bold and the grid below it still shows Sheet1. Automated: `E2E_MANUAL=1 npx playwright test --project=journey e2e/journeys/sheet-tab-state-undo.spec.ts --grep BUG-0043`, which PRINTS both windows ('[BUG-0043] torn window: tab click N ms, undo M ms') and asserts only that undo is no worse than the click plus 50 ms, and that both settle. Raising that to the absolute claim -- no torn frame at all -- fails today, which is how this was found.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The switch is atomic in STATE and sequential in PAINT. The tab strip derives from the grid sheet context and re-renders synchronously with it; the canvas has to fetch the new sheet's cells before it can draw them. Closing it means either fetching the target sheet's viewport BEFORE the context swap and committing both in one batch, or suppressing the canvas paint until the fetch lands (which trades a wrong sheet for a stale one -- no better). The first is a change to the ONE switch path every tab click, script, MCP tool and undo goes through, and the register's standing warning about that path is that the last time it had two hydration paths, the second was mount-only and painted sheet 1's panes on sheet 2.
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/src/core/components/Spreadsheet/useSpreadsheetSelection.ts (followBackendSheetActivation) and whatever consumes `sheet:normalSwitch` to refetch the viewport. NOT undo-specific: fixing it in applyRestoreToTheView alone would make undo differ from the tab click, which is the split BUG-0043 closed.

fix.diffSummary: FIXED 2026-08-14, by the register's own prescription -- fetch the target sheet's viewport BEFORE the context swap and commit both in one batch -- and the measurement found the tear had TWO mechanisms, not one. (1) THE CANVAS HALF: every switch initiator (SheetTabs' click/add/delete/applySheetsResult and applyRestoreToTheView for undo/redo) now awaits `primeSheetSwitch()` AFTER the backend switch and BEFORE the first dispatch; the prime runs GridCanvas's own registered prefetcher (same calculateFetchRange, same getViewportCells+getSpillRanges) into a one-shot handoff slot (`app/src/core/lib/sheetSwitchPrefetch.ts`, exposed to Shell via @api), and the EXISTING `sheet:normalSwitch` handler -- no second channel, no second hydration path -- takes the payload and commits it synchronously inside the dispatch turn; a `useLayoutEffect` then paints the canvas before the browser paints, so React commits strip and cells in ONE flush. The dispatch sequence itself still contains no `await` (the §13 atomicity discipline; the prime sits strictly before the first dispatch), a same-sheet undo primes nothing, and a missing/failed prime degrades to the old fetch-after-swap path, never to a wrong paint. A sheet-epoch guard in fetchCells discards any viewport response that straddled a switch (the backend answers for whichever sheet is active when it SERVES the call) and re-fetches via the existing deferral machinery. (2) THE STRIP HALF, which the prime alone exposed at 33 ms on undo: the strip's bold weight rendered from SheetTabs' LOCAL activeIndex, which a backend-initiated switch only reaches through the 'Syncing activeIndex with Redux' useEffect -- one flush AFTER the canvas painted. `paintedActiveIndex` now renders the highlight from the grid sheet context, making followBackendSheetActivation's standing comment ('the tab strip has no state of its own... it syncs its highlight from this') true of the pixels; local activeIndex remains for behaviour only. MEASURED with the committed probe, cold app, consistent bundle: before 60-67 ms (click) / 21-71 ms (undo); after 0 ms / 0 ms across five consecutive runs, and the spec now asserts the ABSOLUTE claim (tornWindowMs === 0 for both gestures) it could not before. Switch latency unmoved: landed-at 90-156 ms (click) / 52-83 ms (undo) vs the pre-fix canvas catch-up at ~98 ms. TEETH: with the prime sabotaged to a no-op on the running build, the raised test fails with 'tab click 64 ms' and samples showing the strip at t=112 ms over ink at t=191 ms -- the filed symptom exactly; restored byte-identically (sha256 a6b85099f95e07ebd43a6b1c0d8eba42484ad8f4139e3a961e955b60906873b7) and green again. 10 unit tests pin the handoff slot (exactly-once take, foreign-sheet refusal, staleness, disposal ownership, renderSignal bracketing). The atomicity unit suite (undoSheetActivation) passes unchanged -- the event sequence and detail shapes are untouched. CAUTION FOR FUTURE MEASUREMENT: under `tauri dev`, HMR cycles that reload sheetSwitchPrefetch.ts can split its module state across stale importer instances (prime writes into one, take reads another), which resurrects a ~30 ms tear that does NOT exist on a cold bundle -- measure this bug only on a verified cold launch.

violation.message: A ROW/COLUMN DELETE THAT FULLY COVERS A PIVOT REGION DELETES THE PIVOT WITHOUT THE CASCADE, WITHOUT AN UNDO RESTORE AND WITHOUT AN ANNOUNCEMENT. `shift_pivot_regions_for_row_delete` / `_col_delete` (app/src-tauri/src/commands/structure.rs, the two `pivot_tables.remove(&pid)` sites) remove the pivot RAW. Compare `delete_pivot_table` (pivot/commands.rs), which (1) runs `object_deps::cascade_deleted_sources` so the slicers, timeline slicers and ribbon-filter targets bound to the pivot die with it, (2) records `pivot_delete` + the cascade restores on the undo stack, and (3) cleans `views` and `active_pivot_id`. The structural path does NONE of these: slicers/timelines survive pointing at a dead pivot id (the exact orphan §3bt's cascade exists to prevent), `pivot_state.views` keeps the dead entry, undoing the row delete restores the pivot's CELLS (via the structural snapshot / engine RestoreSnapshot, which carry cells only) but not the pivot object -- a region that looks like a pivot and answers to nothing -- and no announcement reaches the frontend stores. The object_deps census does not see it because these sites are not a delete COMMAND; the same reasoning that hid `tables` from §3bn's sweep (BUG-0047: 'it has its own re-key, so it looked handled').

repro.description: FOUR STEPS, no scripting needed for the backend half. (1) Create a pivot whose destination occupies, say, rows 10-15. (2) Bind a slicer to it. (3) Select rows 8-20 (whole rows) and Delete Sheet Rows. (4) Observe: get_pivot_tables no longer lists the pivot; the slicer still lists it as its source (orphan); Ctrl+Z brings the ROWS back with the pivot's rendered cells but `get_pivot_at_cell` finds nothing -- the pivot object is gone for good. The FRONTEND ghost-tab half (Analyze/Design tabs surviving under a stationary cursor when the rows are deleted by a script's api.deleteRows) was fixed 2026-08-14 by `reconcileActivePivotAfterShift` in the Pivot selection handler, pinned by activePivotReconciliation.test.ts; the backend halves are what stay open.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The structural shift helpers pre-date the object-dependency cascade and were never onboarded: they hold `protected_regions` + `pivot_tables` for their whole pass, so the cascade (which takes the slicer/timeline/ribbon locks) cannot run inline -- it has to collect the removed pivot ids and run after the drops, the way `delete_pivot_table` runs it FIRST for the same lock-discipline reason. The undo half needs the removed pivots recorded as `pivot_delete` restores inside the row-delete's own transaction (cascade restores first, then the pivot, then the rows -- reverse-replay order), and the frontend told via the `pivot`+`slicer`+`ribbonFilter` domains. `delete_rows`/`delete_columns` already thread pivot_state and ribbon_filter_state; slicer_state and timeline_state would need to join the signatures (delete_rows_impl exists over plain references, so the behaviour is unit-testable).
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/src-tauri/src/commands/structure.rs (shift_pivot_regions_for_row_delete / _col_delete: return removed pivot ids; delete_rows_impl / delete_columns_impl: cascade + undo-record + announce after locks drop)

bugs.notes: Deliberately NOT suppressed anywhere: no KNOWN_ISSUES entry, no walker exclusion. A walk that deletes rows across a pivot with a slicer bound to it should fail loudly on the orphan. Filed open rather than fixed in-pass because the fix threads two more State handles through two structural commands and reorders undo recording in a lock-heavy area this program has deadlocked in three times -- it deserves its own pass with the app-lib suite run against it.

source.runId: surfaced by the stale-fixme sweep: re-enabling regression-scenarios.spec.ts 'inserting a row expands formula references' failed on a verified-clean cold app; mechanism isolated by a CDP probe (scratchpad probe-insert-shift.mjs transcript in the register, section 17d)

violation.message: A ROW INSERTED INSIDE A FORMULA'S RANGE NEVER JOINS THAT FORMULA'S DEPENDENCY EDGES, so writing into the inserted row recalculates NOTHING. Measured on a clean workbook: A900=10, A901=20, A902=30, A903=SUM(A900:A902)=60. insert_rows at 900 shifts everything correctly and re-points the formula to =SUM(A900:A903) - the D8 re-pointing works. Then update_cell A901=15: the SUM's display STAYS 60 (expected 75). Control 1: writing 25 over the shifted 20 at A902 (a cell the range covered BEFORE the insert) recalculates to 80 - and that 80 = 10+15+25+30 proves the engine's value store has the 15; only the EDGE is missing. Control 2: a fresh =SUM(A900:A903) entered afterwards computes 80 immediately. So insert_rows re-points the AST and shifts the EXISTING edges but registers no edges for the cells the range GREW over; every formula whose range was expanded across an insert is deaf to the inserted cells until some originally-covered cell changes.

repro.description: FOUR STEPS on a cold app. (1) A840=10, A841=20, A842=30, A843=SUM(A840:A842). (2) insert_rows at 841. (3) update_cell into the inserted A841 = 15. (4) Read A844's display: stays at its pre-write value instead of 75. Automated: E2E_MANUAL=1 npx playwright test --project=functional e2e/tests/regression-scenarios.spec.ts --grep 'inserting a row expands' - re-enabled 2026-08-14 and DELIBERATELY LEFT FAILING (no fixme, no suppression); its first assertion (range expansion to SUM(A840:A843)) passes, its second (recalc on write to the inserted row) is this bug.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The D8 family, one edge over: D8 shipped re-pointing + re-evaluating the formulas structural edits MOVE, but the dependency-map maintenance for a RANGE that grew across the inserted rows registers edges only for the shifted copies of edges that already existed - the inserted cells were never inside the old range, so no edge is shifted into place for them, and nothing walks the re-pointed AST to register the widened span. The fix direction is to re-register (normalize_cross_sheet_refs-aware, one shared helper) the dependents of every formula whose range a structural insert widened - or simply re-register the re-pointed formula's dependencies wholesale after the rewrite, which is what entering the same formula fresh does (control 2 proves that path is correct).
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/src-tauri/src/commands/structure.rs (insert_rows/insert_columns formula re-pointing) + the dependency-map registration it should re-run per rewritten formula

bugs.notes: Found because the stale-suppression sweep re-enabled a fixme whose test had ALSO been written with a broken probe (getCellLiveValue reads the formula bar, which shows a formula cell's formula text, never its value) - the probe was fixed first, and the test then failed for this real reason. The sibling stress-tests fixme ('changing the root propagates through entire chain') had ONLY the probe defect and is green after the same one-line probe fix, live from a cold app.

source.runId: first invariant walk generated from the new floating-range catalog actions (fr.create et al., added 2026-08-14); the poisoned session then failed seed 90010001's BOTH tests at step 1 with the same errors

violation.message: THE WALKER RESET NEVER TEARS DOWN FLOATING RANGES, AND THE STALE FRONTEND STORE POISONS EVERY LATER WALK IN THE SESSION. deepResetForWalk tears down slicers/charts/sparklines/pivots/tables through their own APIs and relies on new_file for the rest -- but resetToNewWorkbook invokes new_file RAW and never emits AFTER_NEW (the product's File > New does a full window.location.reload(), so the product never sees this state). new_file clears the backend floating-range rows and tells the FloatingRange extension nothing: its store keeps the dead rows, the overlay keeps their regions, and on the next redraw frRenderer fetches cells for ids the backend no longer has -- '[FloatingRange] Failed to fetch cells for <uuid>: No floating range with id <uuid>' x3, tripping no-console-errors at step 1 of WHATEVER walk runs next. Measured: seed 1786456498740's walk 1 created 3 FRs (the new fr.create cap) and passed; its rapid-fire walk then failed at step 1 fr.create, and seed 90010001 -- run next in the same app session, generating NO fr actions at all -- failed both tests at step 1 (table.create / sparkline.create) on the same three stale uuids. BUG-0004's exact class (reset leaves frontend object stores unnotified), recreated for the newest object family.

repro.description: PRE-FIX, one invocation: E2E_MANUAL=1 INVARIANT_SEED=1786456498740 npx playwright test --project=invariant. Walk 1 creates floating ranges and passes; the rapid-fire walk fails at step 1 with the stale-id console errors, and any seed run afterwards in the same session fails at step 1 too. tests/regression/repros/BUG-0056.trace.json is the bundle's 1-action minimized trace (fr.create) -- NOTE it only fails in a session already poisoned across the reset boundary; on a clean session it replays green, because the defect IS the state that survives the reset, not the action.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: reset.ts's own header states the rule -- 'new_file leaves ... frontend object stores not notified, so walks explicitly tear down all objects through their own APIs first' -- and the FloatingRange extension (landed 2026-08-13) was never added to that teardown list. The product is unaffected: every product route to a new/opened document either reloads the window (File > New) or emits AFTER_NEW/AFTER_OPEN (file-api), both of which resync the store.

fix.diffSummary: deepResetForWalk tears floating ranges down through the ANNOUNCED @api wrapper (listFloatingRanges + deleteFloatingRange, the same route the product's menus use), then unconditionally resets and reloads the extension's store (resetFloatingRangeStore + loadFloatingRangesFromBackend + syncFloatingRangeRegions) so a session ALREADY poisoned by an earlier raw new_file is healed even when the backend has nothing left to delete. Verified live on the poisoned session itself: re-running seeds 1786456498740 and 90010001 immediately after the fix, without restarting the app, went from '1 failed / both failed at step 1' to green.

bugs.notes: Found by the FIRST walk ever generated from the new floating-range catalog actions -- the coverage added this pass (fr.create/setCell/resize/rename/refFromGrid/delete, snapshot axis, frChange effectiveness accounting, and the undo-oracle rule that FR creation makes a window undecidable). The failure was in the harness, not the product; the product-side lifecycle was proven by the floating-range journey before this.

source.runId: the rapid-fire invariant walk (derived seed 1786456498741) on the same run that exposed BUG-0056: fr.create at step 1, fr.delete at step 18, no-console-errors tripped by a fetch for the freshly deleted row

violation.message: A BACKEND-INITIATED FLOATING-RANGE DELETE LEAVES A REPAINT WINDOW THAT RENDERS -- AND FETCHES -- THE DELETED ROW, LOGGING console.error FOR A BENIGN RACE. The @api wrapper's deleteFloatingRange (and a script's api.deleteFloatingRange through the broker -- both routes confirmed in source) deletes the backend row, announces MUTATION_REFRESH['floatingRanges'], and emits CELLS_UPDATED. The FloatingRange extension prunes its store in an ASYNC reload (reloadForBackendChange awaits a backend list), but the CELLS_UPDATED handler has already invalidated caches and requested an overlay redraw -- so the overlay renders the store's still-present row, frRenderer fetches its cells, the backend answers 'No floating range with id <uuid>', and frRenderer.ts logged console.error. The extension's OWN delete path (menus, keyboard, provider seam) prunes the store synchronously before any repaint, which is why the product UI never showed it; a restricted script deleting an on-screen FR hits it every time. Severity: transient one-repaint ghost + console noise; self-heals when the reload lands.

repro.description: Walk-level, pre-fix: E2E_MANUAL=1 INVARIANT_SEED=1786456498740 npx playwright test --project=invariant --grep 'rapid create-delete' (with the BUG-0056 reset fix in place, so the failure left is this one) -- fails no-console-errors on the id fr.delete removed at step 18. Product-level: run a script that calls api.deleteFloatingRange on a floating range currently on screen and watch the console.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The announce-then-reload architecture makes a stale-render window unavoidable for backend-initiated deletes; the defect is that the renderer treats a fetch failure inside that window as an error. The distinction that matters is not the failure but its PERSISTENCE: a row gone from the store by the time the dust settles lost a delete race (silent); a row still cached is a real store/backend inconsistency (loud -- that loud path is what caught BUG-0056 and must not be weakened).

fix.diffSummary: fetchFrCells DEFERS the verdict on a failed fetch (1 s) instead of softening it: if the row has left the store by then, the fetch lost a delete race -- prune its cache silently and redraw; if the row is STILL in the store, console.error exactly as before, so a persistent stale store (BUG-0056's class) keeps failing walks loudly, one settle later. Two unit cases pin both branches (fake timers; the loud branch asserts the error still names the id). Verified live: the rapid-fire walk on seed 1786456498740 that failed on this exact race is green after the fix, with fr.create/fr.delete exercised.

bugs.notes: Found by the walker's SECOND-ever fr walk, ten minutes after BUG-0056 -- the two are the same architecture examined from opposite sides: 0056 is the store never told about a wipe (harness reset), 0057 is the store told asynchronously about a delete (product routes). The deferred verdict serves both: silence for the benign race, unchanged loudness for real inconsistency.

source.runId: first mixed floating+sheet soak (SOAK_CATEGORY_WEIGHTS=floating:5,sheet:5, 150 actions) -- the first walk to combine floating-range lifecycle with sheet structure; failed recalc-consistency at the checkpoint after step 75; shrinker-confirmed at 17 actions over 30 replays

violation.message: A CROSS-SHEET DEPENDENT ON A NON-ACTIVE USER SHEET GOES STALE WHEN A FLOATING-RANGE CELL (OR ANY OFF-SHEET-WRITTEN CELL) CHANGES. Measured on the minimized trace: two grid cells hold ='Float1'!A1+4 on two different sheets; a script-path write rewrites Float1!A1 while a THIRD sheet is active; full recalculation then changes exactly one cell -- 'sheet 1 cell 60:48: 46 -> 4' -- and the post-F9 probe proves F9's value is the correct one (Float1!A1 = 'Sheet1 (2)'!B2*2 = 0, so +4 = 4). The dependent on the ACTIVE sheet updated; its twin on the non-active sheet held the pre-write value. MECHANISM (read from source, then pinned by a unit test): `recalc_after_off_sheet_write` (app/src-tauri/src/commands/data.rs) re-evaluates the WRITTEN sheets, every OBJECT-backed sheet, and the ACTIVE sheet, twice -- and never any other user sheet. The cross-sheet dependents map is not consulted at all, so a registered edge into a non-active, non-written user sheet is simply outside the pass's scope. Every off-sheet write route funnels here: floating-range cell writes, a script's update_cell_on_sheets/clear_range_on_sheets, the QuickJS bulk path.

repro.description: tests/regression/repros/BUG-0058.trace.json (17 actions, shrinker-confirmed over 30 replays). Replay: E2E_MANUAL=1 SOAK_TRACE=tests/regression/repros/BUG-0058.trace.json SOAK_EXPECT_FAIL=1 npx playwright test --project=soak --grep 'Trace replay' (pre-fix). Unit-level, no app: floating_range_recalc_tests::a_non_active_sheet_dependent_follows_a_floating_range_write -- three sheets, an FR dependent registered on Sheet1, a second-hop dependent on Sheet2, the write made while Sheet3 is active.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED from source: recalc_after_off_sheet_write's sheet set is written+object+active, a hand-fixed scope that predates cross-sheet edges reaching arbitrary user sheets. GAP A made the edges exist; nothing made this pass walk them. The class is the standing CLAUDE.md rule ('a command that writes without recalculating dependents'), one function over.

fix.diffSummary: recalc_after_off_sheet_write now extends its recalc set with every sheet holding a cross-sheet DEPENDENT of anything on the written/object sheets, computed to a TRANSITIVE fixpoint over sheet names (a repaired dependent can feed a formula on yet another sheet). Lock use is strictly sequential -- snapshot sheet_names, drop; lock the dependents map, collect, drop -- so no nesting is added to the crate's lock graph (the three-deadlocks history is why that is stated in the code). source.runId: watched-flake verification (the 20d follow-up pass): full app-lib suite x3 on the final tree -- run 3 of 3 failed 'the wedge must be cleared' (1632/1633). Second strike under the 20c watch rule; first strike was 1-of-3 full runs on 2026-08-13.

violation.message: SCRIPT-BATCH RECLAIM DESTROYS ITS OWN HEALING RECORD, AND CONNECTION TEARDOWN STRANDS THE BATCH INTERLOCK. reclaim_expired_script_batches (bi/model_editor.rs) removed EVERY expired entry from the process-global script_batch_registry() and only then attempted rollback_model_batch against the CALLER's BiState -- so a rollback that fails (connection not resolvable by that caller) left `in_batch` set in the global model_undo_store with the registry record already gone: nothing can ever reclaim it again. That is the PERMANENT form of the exact wedge the deadline exists to heal -- every later batch on that ModelKey refuses to open and record_model_undo silently suppresses every later edit's undo snapshot; ModelKey outlives both connections and documents, so a reconnect or a reopened workbook inherits the wedge. Reachable in production two ways: (1) bi_delete_connection removed a connection with a batch open (trusted OR script) and never released it; (2) reset_bi_connections (File > New / Open) drained all connections while a batch was open, leaving both globals set. Manifested in the test binary as the watched flake: many BiStates run concurrently against the same globals, and a sibling test's reclaim stole the freshly-expired zombie batch of an_abandoned_script_batch_is_reclaimed_and_rolled_back in the window between the test back-dating the deadline and its own healing edit; the thief's rollback failed against the wrong BiState ('Connection not found'), the record was gone, and the zombie's model stayed wedged -> 'the wedge must be cleared' at model_editor.rs:9103.

repro.description: Deterministic: bi::model_editor::tests::reclaim_leaves_batches_whose_connection_it_cannot_resolve pins the exact interleaving (two BiStates; B's reclaim runs while A's expired batch is on record -- pre-fix it steals and strands, post-fix it must not touch it). Stochastic pre-fix: full app-lib suite at default parallelism (12 threads) failed ~1 in 3 runs; NOT cold-I/O -- the 2026-08-14 strike was on the third (warm) consecutive run, and it is not wall-clock/tokio-timing either: the deadline is back-dated a full second, the window is scheduling-order between threads sharing the global registry.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED from source. Three defects, one root: the reclaim consumed the registry record before knowing the rollback could succeed; rollback resolves the batch's connection_id in the caller's BiState; and neither bi_delete_connection nor reset_bi_connections released a live batch while a rollback was still possible. The 20c characterisation ('load-sensitive test isolation, not product behaviour') was HALF right: the trigger is test-binary concurrency, but the record-then-heal gap it exposes is a real production wedge via connection delete / document reset.

filesChanged: app/src-tauri/src/bi/model_editor.rs (reclaim_expired_script_batches now takes ONLY batches whose connection lives in the calling BiState -- removing an entry it cannot roll back is destroying the last healing record; on a rollback that still fails, clear_batch_interlock() heals the in_batch flag instead of logging and stranding it; new prepare_connection_delete() gate: reclaims expired script batches, REFUSES the delete while a live script batch owns the model (same rationale + bound as guard_no_live_script_batch), and rolls back a trusted batch left open on the model's last connection; new forget_batches_for_model_key() for document reset; + 4 pinning tests)
app/src-tauri/src/bi/commands.rs (bi_delete_connection runs prepare_connection_delete before removing the connection; reset_bi_connections forgets batch state per torn-down connection's model key)
fix.diffSummary: The reclaim can no longer steal what it cannot heal, a failed rollback clears the interlock instead of stranding it, and the two connection-teardown paths release batch state while release is still possible. Semantics preserved: a reclaimed batch is still rolled back (never committed); when no engine remains to reinstall into, the pre-batch snapshot stays as one undoable step. Deleting a connection while a LIVE script batch owns the model is now refused with the same bounded error the trusted end/cancel paths give.

violation.message: A DATE NUMBER FORMAT APPLIED THROUGH THE FORMAT CELLS DIALOG RENDERS THE FORMAT STRING ITSELF, NOT A DATE. Measured live: type 45000, Ctrl+1 > Date > '2024-01-15 (ISO)' > OK -- the cell displays the literal text 'yyyy-mm-dd' (backend display AND rendered pixels agree; crop saved). MECHANISM (read from source, then pinned by unit tests): the dialog stores its date presets LOWERCASE ('yyyy-mm-dd', styles.rs parse_number_format), while core/engine/src/number_format.rs::format_date_number was a hand-rolled .replace chain that only knew the UPPERCASE spellings YYYY/YY/MM/DD/M/D -- any other spelling fell through every replace untouched and the format string became the display. The engine's own presets::date_iso() uses 'YYYY-MM-DD', which is why nothing in-repo ever hit it. Same class one level down: xlsx builtin numFmt 15-17 ('D-MMM-YY') produced digit salad (MMM is not a token the chain knew), datetime combos ('M/D/YYYY HH:mm') left the time half raw, and lowercase 'hh:mm' rendered 13:00 as '01:00' (h was unconditionally 12-hour; Excel's rule is 24-hour unless AM/PM is present). SECOND DEFECT found while pinning the fix: the full custom-format engine (custom_format.rs), whose lexer is case-insensitive and was the delegation target, DROPPED '/' and '.' in date sections -- '/' lexes as FractionSeparator and '.' as DecimalPoint, and format_datetime_section rendered neither -- so 'MM/DD/YYYY' came out '01152024'.

repro.description: Live: cold app, type 45000 into any cell, Ctrl+1 > Date > ISO > OK -- pre-fix the cell shows 'yyyy-mm-dd'. Unit, no app: number_format::tests::date_format_lowercase_dialog_spelling_formats_a_date (45000 + Date{'yyyy-mm-dd'} must be '2023-03-15'), date_format_never_echoes_the_format_string, date_format_xlsx_builtin_month_names, time_format_h_is_24_hour_without_am_pm; custom_format::tests::test_date_format_slash_and_dot_separators_are_literal. All fail pre-fix.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED from source: two date formatters existed -- a token-replace toy in number_format.rs (uppercase-only, no month names, no datetime combos, 12-hour always) and the real case-insensitive engine in custom_format.rs -- and the dialog's lowercase presets only ever reached the toy. One formatter now: Date/Time delegate to custom_format, which also had its date-section '/' and '.' literals restored.

fix.diffSummary: format_date_number and format_time_number now delegate to custom_format::format_custom_value -- the case-insensitive, full-token engine (month/day names, datetime combos, elapsed [h], AM/PM-driven 12/24h) -- instead of an uppercase-only .replace chain; their dead helpers (chrono_lite_date, is_leap_year, the token chain) are gone. format_datetime_section renders FractionSeparator as literal '/' and DecimalPoint as literal '.' in date/time context ('m/d/yyyy', 'dd.mm.yyyy', 'mm:ss.0'). Pinned by 5 new unit tests across the two files; full core workspace green (engine 551 passing incl. 20 number_format + 66 custom_format). Verified live post-fix on a cold isolated app: dialog Date ISO on 45000 renders '2023-03-15' (pixels + backend), dialog Time renders '13:30:00', every ribbon route unchanged.

source.runId: full functional pass on the post-BUG-0060 tree (this pass): 549 passed / 1 failed / 4 upheld fixmes of 554 collected, 38.4m -- the one failure was mcp-create-named-range.spec.ts at the MCP handshake, ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8787, 1.2s into test 265 of 554

violation.message: MCP START CLAIMS SUCCESS BEFORE THE SERVER CAN ACCEPT, AND A BIND FAILURE IS INVISIBLE. mcp_start (app/src-tauri/src/mcp/mod.rs) set running=true, returned 'MCP server started on port N', and only THEN -- on a freshly spawned thread that first creates a whole Tokio runtime -- bound the TCP listener. A client following the documented start -> status -> connect sequence can beat the bind and get ECONNREFUSED from a server that mcp_status reports as running:true with a valid bearer token. Under a loaded machine (test 265 of a 554-test ordered run) the E2E spec lost exactly that race; the run's own backend log shows the spec's cleanup mcp_stop ('Server stop requested', line 8267) landing BETWEEN 'Server starting' (8266) and 'Server listening' (8268), after the fetch had already been refused -- the newborn server then shut down having served nothing. Worse: an actual bind failure (port in use) was only a background log line -- the command had already returned success and `running` silently flapped back to false. A real user pasting the MCP config into Claude Desktop hits the same refused connection with no error surfaced anywhere.

repro.description: Stochastic in-suite: full --project=functional, the first MCP spec in alpha order fails its handshake when the server thread loses the race (passes isolated -- 1/1 cold, 1.6m). Deterministic contract pin: mcp::bind_tests::a_successful_bind_accepts_before_any_accept_loop_and_a_conflict_is_an_err (a bound listener accepts with NO accept loop running; a port conflict is an Err naming the port).

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED from source and from the run's interleaved backend log: the bind happened asynchronously after the success reply, so 'started' and running:true never meant 'accepting'. The 1.2s in-suite failure, the green isolated replay, and the 8266/8267/8268 log interleaving are all the same mechanism.

filesChanged: app/src-tauri/src/mcp/mod.rs (bind_mcp_listener(): the listener is bound -- and listening, kernel backlog live -- SYNCHRONOUSLY inside mcp_start before running/token/cancel state is touched; the bound socket is handed to the server thread and converted with TcpListener::from_std; a bind failure is now the command's own Err naming the port; + bind_tests contract test)
fix.diffSummary: Success from mcp_start (and running:true from mcp_status) now means the port accepts connections at that instant -- the kernel backlog holds connections arriving before the accept loop spins up, so the race is structurally gone rather than narrowed. Port conflicts became caller-visible errors. No protocol or security-model change: token issuance, origin/host hardening and shutdown are untouched.

source.runId: Excel-parity pass on the overflow marker (open-decisions-2026-08.md §21c item 3), 2026-08-15: source review of app/src/core/lib/gridRenderer/rendering/cells.ts against Microsoft's ##### and text-spill documentation, each finding then reproduced by a test

violation.message: A NEGATIVE value under a Date or Time format renders a PLAUSIBLE LIE instead of Excel's width-independent '####'. MEASURED, not read: core/engine/src/number_format.rs probe `negative_serials_under_date_and_time_formats_render_a_plausible_lie` prints -1.0 as Date(YYYY-MM-DD) -> "1900-01-01" and -0.5 as Time(HH:MM:SS) -> "12:00:00". Both are ordinary-looking values that a user cannot tell from real ones -- a subtraction that came out backwards reads as the first of January 1900 rather than as a refusal. Excel lists "formulas that return dates and times as negative values" as a distinct cause of '#####' and its remedy is NOT "widen the column" but "verify that dates and times are positive values": the refusal is SEMANTIC and width-independent, because a serial below zero has no representation in the 1900 date system. Mechanism: format_datetime_section (core/engine/src/custom_format.rs:1536) takes `days = value.floor()`, and for `days < 1` falls back to `(1900, 1, 1)` while the time half uses `value.fract().abs()` -- so the sign that made the value impossible is discarded before any string exists. WHY THE 2026-08-15 PARITY PASS COULD NOT CLOSE IT: every other rung of Excel's ladder is decidable from `CellData.display` plus `StyleData.numberFormat`, which is why that pass shipped entirely inside the renderer. This rung is not: `CellData` carries only the formatted display string, so by the time the renderer sees "1900-01-01" the negativity is gone and NO renderer-side rule can recover it. Not a missing check -- missing data.

repro.description: Format a cell as Date (any pattern) and put a negative number in it -- e.g. =-1, or =A1-B1 where B1 is the later date. Calcula shows 1900-01-01 at every column width; Excel shows ##### at every column width and clears it only when the value becomes positive. Same with a Time format and =-0.5 (Calcula: 12:00:00). Unit-level: the engine probe named in the violation, which RECORDS today's answer rather than asserting Excel's.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED from source and from a measured probe. Two independent halves: (1) the engine formats an unrepresentable value instead of refusing it, and (2) the CellData transport carries no value type, so the renderer cannot re-derive the refusal. Fixing (1) alone would put '####' into `display`, which then travels into copy/paste, CSV export and the formula bar -- the marker is a RENDERING outcome, not a value, and must not become one.

fix.diffSummary: FIXED AS FILED, on the integration pass that owned all three files at once. `OverflowClass { Text | Numeric | Unrepresentable }` added to api_types.rs with struct-level rename_all camelCase, `#[serde(default)]` + `skip_serializing_if` on the Text default so text cells cost nothing on the wire. The decision itself is ONE function, `overflow_class_for(&CellValue, &CellStyle)`, called from ONE place: `format_cell_value_with_color` (lib.rs), the only function in the app holding both the value and the style. Its inner match was split out as `format_cell_value_parts` so the class is stamped once on the way out rather than in each of seven arms -- an arm that forgot would have fallen back to Text (no marker) silently. ALL 56 CellData construction sites across 18 files were made to decide, by the compiler: the field carries no struct-literal default, so `cargo check` enumerated every one. Sites binding `let display = format_cell_value(&x.value, style, &locale)` were rewritten to `let (display, overflow) = format_cell_value_and_class(...)` rather than given a second call, because `format_cell_value(&a.value..)` beside `overflow_class_for(&b.value..)` type-checks perfectly while describing two different cells -- a mismatch that would surface only as a missing '####' in one workbook. Two tuple-destructure sites (commands/utils.rs, commands/data.rs get_viewport_cells) had the class threaded through the tuple so BOTH branches must decide. Renderer side: `classifyCellContent` takes an optional transported class and prefers it over its inference; `fitNumericDisplay` short-circuits to the marker on `unrepresentable` ABOVE the width test, so widening never clears it. THE SECOND HALF THE ENTRY PREDICTED IS ALSO CLOSED: text under an explicitly numeric format now reads as text (it read as numeric if it contained a digit), and digits under the `@` Text format read as text. The engine still renders -1.0 as "1900-01-01" ON PURPOSE -- per this entry's own triage, the marker is a RENDERING outcome and must not enter `display`, where it would travel into copy/paste, CSV export and the formula bar. The engine probe `negative_serials_under_date_and_time_formats_render_a_plausible_lie` still records that and still passes. TEETH PROVEN IN BOTH LANGUAGES, by sabotage on a built tree: replacing the Rust `is_date_or_time && *n < 0.0` guard with `false` turned exactly one of the eight new Rust tests red and left the other seven green; disabling the renderer short-circuit turned exactly two of the new TS tests red. Both restored and re-run green.

source.runId: Excel-parity pass on the overflow marker (open-decisions-2026-08.md §21c item 3), 2026-08-15: source review of app/src/core/lib/gridRenderer/rendering/cells.ts against Microsoft's ##### and text-spill documentation, each finding then reproduced by a test

violation.message: NUMBERS SPILLED ACROSS THEIR EMPTY NEIGHBOURS like text. The spill gate (cells.ts, pre-fix line 1000) read `!shouldWrapEarly && !isMergedMaster && (textAlign === 'left' || textAlign === 'center')` -- alignment only. It never asked Excel's second spill condition, "the cell value is text", so any numeric carrying an EXPLICIT Align Left (or Center) took the text path and ran across its empty neighbours instead of showing '####'. Numbers escaped only by accident: General alignment right-aligns them (cells.ts:935), and 'right' happens not to be in the list. So the defect was invisible until someone left-aligned a numeric column -- an ordinary thing to do to a column of ids or years -- and then a value too wide for its column silently annexed the cells beside it. This is a distinct wrong BEHAVIOUR, not the missing-marker parity gap §21c described: the register recorded only "Calcula ellipsizes; Excel shows ####" and did not mention that Calcula also SPILLS numerics.

violation.message: THE HOME > NUMBER DROPDOWN COULD NOT REPORT ITS OWN RESULT, AND WAS MISSING SIX OF EXCEL'S ELEVEN ENTRIES. Two defects in one control. (3) THE REGION: format codes cannot express five of Excel's eleven entries, because Excel writes Short Date / Long Date / Time as [$-x-sysdate] / [$-x-systime] handles and takes Currency / Accounting from the OS currency pattern. source.runId: reading the Scientific row of the new dropdown against Excel's 0.00E+00, then against the engine's own test, which asserted the wrong string

violation.message: SCIENTIFIC NOTATION HAD THE WRONG SHAPE IN BOTH ENGINES, AND IGNORED THE LOCALE. Excel's Scientific preset is the format code 0.00E+00: a signed exponent, zero-padded to the placeholder count, with the locale's decimal separator. (1) The TYPED path (NumberFormat::Scientific) handed the value to Rust's {:e}, which prints '1.23e3', and only upper-cased the e -- so 1234.5678 displayed as '1.23E3' where Excel shows '1,23E+03' on sv-SE, missing the sign, the zero padding AND the decimal comma. The engine's own test asserted '1.23E3', pinning the defect. (2) The CUSTOM path (a '0.00E+00' code) counted digit placeholders across the WHOLE section, so the exponent's two zeros were folded into the mantissa: 1234 rendered as '1.2340E+3' -- four mantissa decimals and a one-digit exponent, both wrong -- and its test asserted only that the output contained 'E+', which that string does. Two surfaces, two different wrong answers for one user intent.

repro.description: sv-SE: 1234,5678 formatted Scientific rendered '1.23E3'; the same value under the custom code 0.00E+00 rendered '1.2340E+3'. Both now render '1,23E+03'. Pins: test_format_scientific, scientific_uses_the_locale_decimal_separator (core/engine/src/number_format.rs); test_scientific_notation, scientific_sections_split_mantissa_from_exponent_width, scientific_sections_localize_the_mantissa (core/engine/src/custom_format.rs).

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED from source. Rust's {:e} is not Excel's E+00, and count_digit_placeholders has no notion of the E boundary.

source.runId: implementing Excel's Long Date / Time dropdown entries: there was no long-date and no time pattern anywhere in the app, and the month names the pattern needs were English-only

violation.message: MONTH AND WEEKDAY NAMES WERE ENGLISH IN EVERY LOCALE, AND NO LONG-DATE OR TIME PATTERN EXISTED AT ALL. mmm / mmmm / mmmmm / ddd / dddd are LANGUAGE tokens -- Excel renders them in the system locale, so a Swedish machine shows 'den 15 januari 2024'. The custom-format engine resolved them through four English-only free functions with no locale parameter, so every format carrying a month or weekday name rendered in English on all eighteen supported locales. Separately, engine::LocaleSettings carried only a SHORT date pattern: Excel's Long Date and Time entries are the [$-x-sysdate] / [$-x-systime] handles, and neither pattern existed in the product in any language, so those two dropdown entries could only have shipped a hard-coded US pattern.

Pins: calendar_names_are_localized_per_language, calendar_tables_are_complete_and_out_of_range_is_safe, every_supported_locale_carries_a_long_date_and_a_time_pattern, swedish_long_date_and_time_match_the_os_patterns, us_long_date_and_time_match_the_os_patterns (core/engine/src/locale.rs); month_and_day_names_follow_the_locale_not_the_format_string, swedish_long_date_renders_the_os_pattern, us_long_date_renders_the_os_pattern, one_letter_month_token_never_slices_mid_codepoint (core/engine/src/custom_format.rs).

Fixed in the same change (chars().next()) and pinned across en-US/sv-SE/ru-RU/ja-JP/pl-PL. AMBIGUITY LEFT OPEN: the tables are a fixed per-locale-id approximation of the OS patterns; Excel reads Windows' actual regional settings (GetLocaleInfoEx LOCALE_SLONGDATE/STIMEFORMAT/SCURRENCY), so a user who customises their short date in Windows sees that in Excel and the table's default here.
