source.runId: Integration pass over the three concurrent §21c Excel-parity passes, 2026-08-15: checking the seam the brief named -- 'the dropdown and the dialog share format definitions' -- by running the ribbon's own sv-SE display names through the dialog's resolver, not by reading either one.

violation.message: THE RIBBON CAN NOW APPLY FORMATS THE FORMAT CELLS DIALOG CANNOT REPORT. MEASURED, not read: feeding the eleven display names `get_ribbon_number_formats` resolves on sv-SE through the dialog's own `normalizeToPresetValue` returns null for three of them -- `Date (YYYY-MM-DD)` (Short Date), `Date ("den "d mmmm yyyy)` (Long Date) and `Currency ( kr, 2 decimals)` (Currency). The dialog lands on the right CATEGORY (its prefix table is unaffected) and then highlights NOTHING, so a user who applied Short Date from the ribbon opens Format Cells and cannot see which format the cell carries. MECHANISM, and it is the same one twice: `DISPLAY_NAME_TO_PRESET` (app/extensions/BuiltIn/FormatCellsDialog/utils/numberFormats.ts) is a HAND-WRITTEN TypeScript mirror of a Rust serializer's output, and the §21c item-1 pass added display names it does not contain. `Date (YYYY-MM-DD)` misses on CASE alone (the locale table spells the pattern uppercase; the dialog's own `date_iso` preset spells the same pattern lowercase, and the engine's date formatter is case-insensitive, so these are the SAME format failing to compare equal). `Currency ( kr, 2 decimals)` misses on the sv-SE currency symbol's LEADING SPACE (" kr" vs "kr"). Long Date genuinely has no dialog row at all. This is the defect BUG-0065 and BUG-0069 were each an instance of -- a surface that cannot report its own result -- reappearing through a route the item-1 pass opened. That pass deliberately avoided the trap on the ribbon side by asking the backend for the mapping; the dialog was left inverting it in TypeScript. NOT DATA CORRUPTION, and the entry says so rather than inflating it: the store still holds the display name, Rust's `try_parse_display_name` round-trips all three losslessly, and pressing OK preserves the format. What is lost is the dialog's ability to TELL THE USER what is applied. It is also unbounded in the direction it was heading: hard-coding the three sv-SE names would leave the same hole open for the other 17 locale arms, each with its own date pattern and currency symbol.

repro.description: On a sv-SE document: select a cell, pick Short Date (or Currency) from Home > Number, then open Format Cells > Number. The Date (or Currency) category is selected and no row is highlighted. Unit-level: normalizeToPresetValue('Date (YYYY-MM-DD)') === null while normalizeToPresetValue('Date (yyyy-mm-dd)') === 'date_iso' -- the same pattern.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED by measurement. A second source of truth for the backend's display-name vocabulary, living in TypeScript, drifting the first time the Rust side gains a name.

fix.diffSummary: Fixed in the direction that closes the class, not the three instances. (1) The dialog now RESOLVES ribbon display names through the backend, exactly as the ribbon does: `NumberTab` fetches `getRibbonNumberFormats()` alongside the locale it already fetched, and `normalizeToPresetValue` takes that resolved list and consults it FIRST. No display name was hard-coded, so the other 17 locale arms are covered by construction rather than by a table someone has to remember to extend. (2) The five ribbon presets with no dialog row -- Currency, Accounting, Short Date, Long Date, Time -- are now ROWS in their categories, sourced from that same backend response (label from the preset, example from its `sample`). This is also the Excel shape: Excel's Format Cells Date list leads with the locale-responsive Short/Long Date entries, and its Currency list leads with the regional symbol. (3) The static `DISPLAY_NAME_TO_PRESET` map stays as the OFFLINE fallback for the dialog's own presets (date_iso/date_us/...), which the ribbon list does not contain, and its lookup was made case-insensitive so `Date (YYYY-MM-DD)` and `Date (yyyy-mm-dd)` -- the same pattern to a case-insensitive engine -- stop being two different formats to the dialog. A test spells the whole seam out: every one of the eleven display names the ribbon resolves must map to a preset the dialog can HIGHLIGHT, so the next entry added to either side without the other fails here rather than in a user's dialog.

validatedBy: app/extensions/BuiltIn/FormatCellsDialog/__tests__/ribbonFormatSeam.test.ts

source.runId: Integration pass, 2026-08-15 golden recapture: found while VERIFYING a recapture rather than while making one. The recaptured goldens passed the run that wrote them and failed the next clean run of the same project with the same filter.

violation.message: THREE GOLDENS IN comments-notes.spec.ts GAVE THREE ANSWERS FROM ONE BUILD, AND THE VARIABLE IS A TABLE ANOTHER SPEC LEFT IN THE SHARED WORKBOOK -- NOT THE SELECTION. The filed cause (a repaint race between the selection and the annotation refresh) is REFUTED by measurement, and the refutation is the cheapest part to check: the frame carries the selection's own evidence. The capture parks the selection in the SAME COLUMN as the range (parkSelectionAwayFrom uses parkCol = min(a.col,b.col)), so the clip's top 4 px are the selected-column header highlight #E3ECF7. In the failing cold run those 4 rows are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the golden -- 284/284 pixels, 256 of them the highlight -- in both -cell-with-indicator goldens. The selection was in the same place in both pictures. Replaying the exact capture sequence 8 times in one session gave 8 byte-identical frames (sha 38c2aa112ed3). There is no race. WHAT THE PIXELS ACTUALLY SAY: every differing pixel is Excel table chrome. Expected #4472C4 -> actual white, 829 px; expected #D9E2F3 -> white, 264 px; plus 186 px where the golden's caption is WHITE BOLD on blue and the actual's is dark on white. #4472C4/#D9E2F3 exist in exactly one place in the tree: HEADER_BG and BAND_EVEN_BG in extensions/Table/lib/tableStyleInterceptor.ts. Bounding boxes confirm it -- the comments diff starts at y=5 (below the header band), and the notes diff is confined to x[0..3], the 4 px of padding that shows W1's right edge. THE SOURCE: tables.spec.ts's 'rename a table' builds a table over V1:W2 (startCol 21, endCol 22) -- inside comments-notes.spec.ts's declared W-X ground -- and never deletes it. Measured after one full cold functional run, get_all_tables returned SalesData r0-1 c21-22, Table1 r0-3 c17-19 and TotalsTest r6-9 c17-18: three tables, three tests, no cleanup. A table is neither cell state (clear_range_with_options cannot reach it) nor a floating object (the residue guard could not see it); its colours are repainted every frame from the DEFINITION by a style interceptor. WHY ONE BUILD GAVE THREE ANSWERS: 'tables' sorts AFTER 'comments-notes', so the residue can only reach the capture on the SECOND or later run against one app process. Reproduced exactly, on one build, one machine: cold ordered run -> all 3 fail (1363 / 52 / 1338 px); the file alone on an app that had just completed a full run -> 6 passed, 1 failed, which is the ledger's own observation (c) reproduced to the test; and `--update-snapshots` on a warm app wrote the contamination as truth. The third golden (indicators, W6) needs a table reaching row 5, which one full run does not produce -- so that file encodes a workbook MORE contaminated than the ordered suite can even reach.

repro.description: cd app; launch a COLD app; E2E_MANUAL=1 npx playwright test --project=functional tests/comments-notes.spec.ts --reporter=./e2e/collectionGuard.ts,list -> 3 failed / 4 passed. Then run the whole --project=functional once (which runs tables.spec.ts) and repeat the single-file command WITHOUT restarting the app -> 6 passed / 1 failed. Same build, same machine, two answers. `get_all_tables` after the full run lists SalesData over V1:W2.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: Cross-spec, cross-RUN residue: a table left in the shared workbook by a spec that sorts later, repainted by Table's style interceptor over another spec's photographed cells. Not a repaint race and not the selection.

fix.diffSummary: Fixed at the cause, then defended, then guarded, then re-recorded. (1) CAUSE: tables.spec.ts's 'rename a table' moves from V1:W2 into its own R-T ground (R17:S18), and a test.afterAll now deletes EVERY table the file creates and clears its cells -- the charts.spec.ts shape, including the app:table-definitions-updated event without which the chrome keeps painting from the extension's own cache after the backend has forgotten the table. (2) DEFENCE: comments-notes.spec.ts reclaims its own ground in beforeEach (deletes any table overlapping W1:X10, clears formats there), so the golden is a function of the test even if a future spec squats. (3) GUARD, which is worth more than either: zz-workbook-residue.spec.ts gains 'no spec left a table in the backend'. Tables were the one residue class with no guard -- floating objects, charts and open panels each had one -- which is exactly why this was invisible for as long as it was. (4) The general half of the original filing was right and is fixed too: takeGridRegionScreenshot ran waitForGridStable BEFORE the park and then dispatched up to three navigate events, each followed by a FLAT sleep, so the last thing before the shutter was a sleep. Comparison mode retries and hides that; --update-snapshots takes one frame and writes it. It now stabilises AFTER the park, before the shutter. VERIFIED, and never by the run that wrote the goldens: recaptured on a cold app, then TWO further cold runs (fresh app.exe each, PID changed each time) both 7/7 with the golden bytes unchanged (04887c89f178 / 090d396df34b / c57d60ff6d69). The property that was broken -- repeat runs against one app -- was then measured directly: cold 7/7, warm 7/7, warm 7/7.

source.runId: Integration pass, 2026-08-15: verifying the scenario-project golden recapture.

violation.message: A CHART FROM ONE SCENARIO IS IN FRAME IN ANOTHER SCENARIO'S GOLDEN. `scenario-budget-model-title` captures the budget-model scenario's title row; the verify runs photograph the 'Monthly Sales' bar chart from the monthly-report scenario sitting over columns E..H of the budget sheet. Measured: 173,986 differing pixels, glyph-dark pixels 728 -> 19,161, glyph centroid +208px. That is not the 2026-08-15 parity work -- the parity signature in this same file is a ONE-pixel glyph row shift plus the ribbon's lit toggle moving from x=427 to x=460, and both are present as well and account for a few thousand of those pixels, not 174,000. REPRODUCED TWICE on two consecutive clean runs, so it is not a one-off. THE PRE-PASS GOLDEN HAS NO CHART, so the contamination is not baked into the old baseline -- it appears in what the suite produces NOW. Same family as BUG-0074 and found the same way: `--update-snapshots` wrote a chart-free frame and the comparison runs then rejected it, so the recapture was not self-validating. The mechanism differs though, and that is why this is a separate entry: BUG-0074 is a repaint RACE inside one spec, this is an OBJECT that outlives the scenario that created it. `e2e/walker/reset.ts` tears objects down for walks (the BUG-0004/BUG-0035 discipline); the scenario harness evidently does not do the equivalent between scenarios.

repro.description: cd app; cold app on 9222; E2E_MANUAL=1 npx playwright test --project=scenario --reporter=./e2e/collectionGuard.ts,dot  -> 'Scenario: budget-model > 06 title with merged cells and bold' fails; the -actual.png shows a 'Monthly Sales' chart the budget scenario never creates.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading: a chart that the FRONTEND store never learned about survives the reset's teardown, and is then loaded INTO that store by the reset's own table teardown, 500ms before new_file empties the backend. The store is what paints. The product is clean on both halves of the same question and both were measured: new_file clears state.charts (live: get_charts 1 -> 0), and the product's File > New / File > Open both window.location.reload() after the backend switch, so no frontend store can survive a document boundary the product can take.

fix.diffSummary:
THE CAUSAL CHAIN, MEASURED END TO END ON 2026-08-15 with an in-page instrument (timestamps are from one run): +0ms backend=1 store=0 (the residue a raw save_chart leaves); +10251ms charts:refresh (the reset's TABLE teardown announces the objects domain -- ObjectKind::Table -> UiDomain::Objects -- and the Shell translator fans that out to charts:refresh); +10331ms backend=1 store=1 (the extension reloads its store from a backend that STILL HOLDS the outgoing document's chart); +10794ms backend=0 store=1 (new_file cleared the backend, nothing re-syncs the store). From there a chart with no document behind it paints over the next scenario and was photographed by scenario-budget-model-title. REPRODUCED AND EXTINGUISHED AT WILL: with both fixes removed the failure returns at EXACTLY 173,986 differing pixels -- the filed number, to the pixel -- and with them in place the run is green. 

THREE CHANGES. (1) ROOT CAUSE, monthly-report.scenario.ts: the chart is created through the product's chartStore.createChart (what Insert > Chart calls), not a raw save_chart invoke -- the same lesson the walker's chart.create learned as BUG-0031, one directory over. A new assertion pins that the backend and the store AGREE after the create, so the shortcut cannot come back silently. (2) DEFENCE, walker/reset.ts: the chart teardown now also enumerates the BACKEND's list (the store is not a census of the document), and -- the half that closes the CLASS rather than the trigger -- a new resyncChartStoreToBackend() runs AFTER new_file and ASSERTS the store reached zero, throwing a sentence that names the state if it cannot. Proved necessary and sufficient in isolation: with the backend enumeration still disabled and monthly-report still store-blind, the re-sync alone makes the run green. (3) TEETH, soak/walker-action-effects.spec.ts: a regression test that builds the precondition deliberately (a table, then a raw save_chart) and asserts both stores are empty after the reset. It fails when either half of the fix is removed. 

VERIFIED THE WAY THIS PROGRAMME REQUIRES -- by runs that did not write anything: scenario 24/24 on a cold app, 24/24 again on a second cold app, and 24/24 warm in between (the second consecutive run is the one that used to fail). The golden was NOT recaptured and needed no recapture: it is correct as committed, and the diff was the phantom chart, not a stale baseline. Also green after the change: soak/walker-action-effects 6/6, invariant 2/2, journeys/cascade-announcement-live 2/2, soak/synthetic-click-drag 3/3, tsc -p e2e, check:line-endings.

source.runId: Ownership pass on the unfiled 'default-style repaint' reproduction that TWO independent agents hit and neither attributed (open-decisions §24's stale-style-cache note and §27i's method note). Reproduced from the discriminator, then measured A/B on one live binary.

violation.message: FORMATTING A CELL THROUGH ANY ROUTE THAT DOES NOT HAND-DISPATCH `styles:refresh` PAINTS THE DOCUMENT DEFAULT, NOT THE CELL'S OWN STYLE. Ctrl+B on a red cell turned it WHITE and left it unbolded, while `get_style` reported bold + the colour. MEASURED LIVE, one app, one binary, one document, the fix stripped for one page only via `page.route` (another session was running a suite against the same Vite server, so the tree could not be reverted on disk): HEAD  before Ctrl+B styleIndex 47 bold=false, painted 2277 fill px / 784 white px; HEAD  after  Ctrl+B styleIndex 48 bold=TRUE,  painted 0 fill px / 3052 white px (of 3248) -- the cell reverted to the default style. FIXED before Ctrl+B styleIndex 48 bold=false, painted 2277 fill px / 784 white px; FIXED after  Ctrl+B styleIndex 49 bold=TRUE,  painted 2184 fill px / 784 white px -- the fill survives and the glyphs cover 93 px more, which is the bold. MECHANISM: the renderer resolves a cell with `getStyleFromCache(styleCache, cell.styleIndex)` (app/src/core/lib/gridRenderer/styles/styleUtils.ts:33), and that lookup FALLS BACK to index 0 -- the document default -- for an index the cache does not hold. `apply_formatting` MINTS an index (`get_or_create`, commands/styles.rs), and the cache is refreshed by exactly ONE event: `styles:refresh`. `grid:refresh` refetches CELLS only. So every route that refreshed cells without hand-dispatching `styles:refresh` painted the default. THE BACKEND WAS ALREADY HANDING OVER THE CURE AND IT WAS BEING THROWN AWAY: `FormattingResult.styles` is documented in api_types.rs as 'New or updated styles that the frontend should cache', collected from `used_style_indices`; the only frontend reference to it was `console.log(..., result.styles.length)`. PRODUCT ROUTES AFFECTED (not a probe artifact): (1) Core's own keyboard shortcuts -- Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I / Ctrl+U / Ctrl+5 and Ctrl+2/3/4, plus the seven Ctrl+Shift number-format shortcuts -- `useGridKeyboard` -> `handleCommand` -> `applyFormattingToSelection` (useSpreadsheetSelection.ts:1230), which calls `canvas.refreshCells()` + `redraw()` and announces nothing; (2) the script host's `applyRangeFormat` for the ACTIVE sheet (api/scriptHost/host.ts:7791) -- `afterCellDataChange` schedules `grid:refresh` only, while the OFF-sheet arm correctly emits the `styles` mutation domain; (3) MCP `format_range` (mcp/tools.rs:388) mints in Rust and emits only `grid:refresh`; (4) every direct-invoke route in the e2e harness (`setNumberFormatDirect`, alignment.spec, workflow-invoice.spec). The ribbon was correct only because `useHomeTabState.applyFormat` dispatches `styles:refresh` BY HAND, and the Reports extension had already hit the same wall and patched it at ITS call site with the comment 'the style cache must refetch too or the report renders unstyled'. WHY 106,931 UNIT TESTS AND 550 FUNCTIONAL TESTS MISSED IT: every formatting test reads the format back from the BACKEND (`get_cell` -> `get_style`), which was always right. The only assertions that could have seen it are pixels, and every visual formatting golden applies its format through the RIBBON. The walker drives Ctrl+B (actionCatalog.ts:824) but its oracles compare state, not paint. NOT VISIBLE FOR EVERY FORMAT, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED CASUAL CHECKING: a format that changes only the DISPLAY STRING (a number format on a cell wide enough to fit) paints identically under the default style, because `display` comes from the backend. Measured: replaying core-visual.spec.ts's number-format block through the direct route and then repairing the cache changed 0 of 20,592 pixels. It becomes visible the moment the style decides how the cell is DRAWN -- fill, font, colour, alignment, borders, or the overflow ladder. §27i's own probe hit the ladder: an explicitly Number-formatted cell in a 60px column painted `1,23E+08` (General's scientific rung) instead of `########`. Re-measured after the fix on the same probe: `#####` vs `2E+08`, two different pictures, as Excel has it.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: NOT a hypothesis -- measured in both directions. One cache with one refresh event, and the refresh wired to CALL SITES instead of to the IPC wrapper. Identical in shape to the outline / hyperlink / validation / annotation defect this tree already fixed (see the header of app/src/api/__tests__/refreshAnnouncements.test.ts, 'a refresh event wired to one caller is how the ribbon path stayed correct while the script path silently left the cache -- and therefore the painted grid -- describing a document that no longer existed'). The lookup's silent fallback to index 0 is what makes the failure a plausible-looking wrong answer instead of a blank cell or a crash.

fix.diffSummary: TWO mechanisms, because the class has two directions. (1) PRIME, at the one door: `applyFormatting` / `applyBorderPreset` in tauri-api emit `AppEvents.STYLE_ENTRIES_UPDATED` carrying `FormattingResult.styles`, and `useSpreadsheetStyles` merges the entries into the cache. Emitting from the WRAPPER cannot be routed around -- there is no other door to the command -- and it costs NO IPC, because the backend already returns exactly the indices it used or created. It also lands BEFORE the repaint, so no frame is ever painted with the wrong style (a heal alone would flash the default first, which a screenshot can photograph). (2) HEAL, for the mints that never touch a frontend wrapper (MCP, .calp pulls, backend recalculations, and the e2e direct-invoke helpers): on `grid:refresh` and on `sheet:normalSwitch` the cache compares its size against `get_style_count()` -- a scalar IPC beside the viewport cell fetch those events already pay for -- and re-reads the registry in full only when the two disagree. `!==` rather than `>`: a document replaced under the frontend can leave the registry SHORTER, and a cache holding entries the backend no longer has is just as wrong. Coalesced with an in-flight guard so a burst of refreshes costs one probe. PINNED by app/src/core/components/Spreadsheet/__tests__/formatStyleCachePrime.test.tsx (6 cases), which mounts the REAL `useSpreadsheetStyles` + `useSpreadsheetSelection` against the REAL tauri-api (only Tauri's `invoke` is doubled, by a fake registry that dedupes like `get_or_create`), drives a real Ctrl+B keydown on the grid container, and asserts the RENDERER's own question -- `getStyleFromCache(cache, cell.styleIndex).bold`. PROVED BY SABOTAGE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: disabling the prime turns exactly the two prime cases red ('expected false to be true') and leaves the heal cases green; disabling the heal turns exactly the heal case red. Two of the six are cost assertions -- a format costs no `get_all_styles`, and a quiet `grid:refresh` costs the scalar probe and no full re-read.

repro.description: LIVE: launch an isolated app (own WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER, CDP 9223). Give A4 a background colour no other style has, force one `styles:refresh` so the cache holds it, then press Ctrl+B on the grid container (WebView2 swallows the real accelerator -- dispatch the keydown on [data-focus-container='spreadsheet'], as e2e/helpers/grid.ts does). Before the fix the cell turns WHITE and unbolded while get_style reports bold + the colour. A FRESH style matters: `get_or_create` dedupes, so re-applying a format the registry already holds returns an index the cache already has and the defect hides -- that is how an earlier attempt at this measurement came out green on the unfixed build. UNIT: `npx vitest run src/core/components/Spreadsheet/__tests__/formatStyleCachePrime.test.tsx`. Instruments (untracked, app/e2e/results/): style-repaint-ab.mjs (the A/B, which strips the fix for ONE page with `page.route` so a shared dev server is not disturbed), style-repaint-probe.mjs (§27i's own probe re-run), golden-impact-probe.mjs (the changed-pixels-vs-goldens measurement). HARNESS NOTE (open-decisions §28k): the FIRST run of this probe silently migrated onto ANOTHER session's app -- its own instance died and that session's pinned app took the freed CDP port, so `connectOverCDP` attached to theirs and the probe wrote cells and reloaded the page inside their document. The numbers above are from a re-run behind an OWNERSHIP GATE (app/e2e/results/cdp-owner.ps1: resolve the PID listening on the port, refuse anything whose --user-data-dir is not this probe's), checked at start AND end. A CDP port is not an identity.

source.runId: BUG-0074 diagnosis: reading every reset the suite performs, then invoking them against the live backend instead of trusting the source.

violation.message: FIVE RESIDUE CLEANUPS -- INCLUDING THE SUITE'S OWN resetGrid -- HAD NEVER RUN, BECAUSE THEY SPELL AN ENUM VARIANT IN A CASING serde REJECTS. ClearApplyTo (app/src-tauri/src/api_types.rs) carries #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")], so the wire vocabulary is all|contents|formats|hyperlinks|removeHyperlinks|resetContents. Measured live against the running backend on CDP 9223: "All" -> REJECTED `unknown variant`, "all" -> ACCEPTED; same for Formats/formats and Contents/contents. Every one of the five call sites wraps the invoke in .catch(() => {}) because 'the command may not exist', so the rejection was swallowed and the clear silently did not happen: e2e/helpers/screenshots.ts resetGrid (the suite's reset -- its used-range + formatting clear never ran, leaving Ctrl+A + Delete as the whole of it), and the test.afterAll cleanups in animation.spec.ts, charts.spec.ts, dimensions.spec.ts and edge-cases.spec.ts. Those four were written specifically to close the cross-spec residue class recorded as sections 3a/3b of the register -- so the register's own remediation for that class was, in fact, unenforced. The cost is measurable: on one cold app, one build, the ordered functional run went from 27 failures to 20 when the five were corrected, with 8 tests fixed (all 5 comments-notes, clipboard copy/paste, and both dimensions tests) and the two whole-grid evaluate-formula goldens revealed as photographs of edge-cases.spec.ts's uncleaned AE-column residue.

repro.description: In the running app: invoke('clear_range_with_options', { params: { ..., applyTo: 'All' } }) rejects with `unknown variant \`All\``; the same call with 'all' resolves. Then grep the e2e tree for applyTo: "All".

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: A hand-written TypeScript spelling of a Rust serde vocabulary, with a catch-all around the call that turns a rejected command into silence.

fix.diffSummary: All five call sites corrected to the accepted lower-case spelling, and the class closed rather than the five instances: e2e/__tests__/clearApplyToVocabulary.test.ts PARSES the variants out of the Rust enum, camelCases them the way serde does, and fails the build naming file and line for any applyTo literal in the e2e tree that the backend would reject. It was proved to fail before it was trusted (it flagged its own failure-message template on the first run, and then dimensions.spec.ts:48 when one site was deliberately reverted). CONSEQUENCE, attributed rather than absorbed: the two whole-grid evaluate-formula goldens changed, because they had been photographing residue their owner's afterAll was written to remove. Attribution is one-directional and exact -- 3,379 ink pixels present in the golden are absent now and ZERO new ink appears, all of it in the column band that resolves to AE after the spec's own navigateTo('AI1') scroll, which is edge-cases.spec.ts's declared AE1:AH200 ground. grid-evaluate-formula-init was already 112,174 px wrong on a cold app before this pass and is 2,498 px after it. Both were re-recorded in the ordered cold run and verified by two further cold runs.

source.runId: BUG-0074 diagnosis: the isolated app's parked selection reset itself twice while nothing was driving it.

violation.message: THE APP UNDER TEST IS ON THE EDITOR'S HOT-RELOAD CHANNEL, AND A SOURCE SAVE RESETS THE GRID MID-RUN WITH NOTHING ABLE TO OBSERVE IT. The E2E app is a `tauri dev` build served by Vite, which pushes to whatever is connected. Measured 2026-08-15 while another agent saved app/src/core/lib/events.ts: Vite pushed `hmr update` for ~170 modules and `page reload (circular import invalidate)` for several; React fast-refresh remounted the provider tree, so GridProvider's useReducer restarted from getInitialState() and the selection snapped from row 6 col 22 back to A1 with scrollX 286 -> 0, about 2.5 s after the harness had parked it. THE PART THAT MAKES IT A BUG RATHER THAN AN ANNOYANCE: there is no navigation. performance.timeOrigin is unchanged and a window marker installed before the update survives it, so neither the page nor Playwright can tell the app was reset underneath a capture -- the resulting golden is a photograph of the editor and is indistinguishable from a product change. Cutting the channel made the same state hold still for 10 s and the same capture come back byte-identical 8 times out of 8. This is a standing hazard on a machine where more than one agent works, which is how this program is run.

repro.description: With an E2E app running against the Vite dev server, park the selection (dispatch app:navigate-to-cell {row:6,col:22,select:true}) and poll __CALCULA_GRID_STATE__.selection while saving any file under app/src. The selection returns to 0,0 and viewport.scrollX to 0 with no framenavigated event and with window markers intact.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The E2E launchers start a normal dev server; nothing tells Vite that this instance is under test and must not be hot-reloaded.

fix.diffSummary: Both launchers now set CALCULA_E2E=1 on the `tauri dev` child, and vite.config.ts resolves `server.hmr` to false under it -- so an E2E instance has no hot-reload channel while interactive development is untouched. Pinned by e2e/__tests__/hmrDisabledForE2E.test.ts, which checks BOTH halves (the config reads the flag and resolves to false; each launcher still sets it), because a guard that only checks one half is gone the first time the other drifts. Proved to fail before the change: the test reported 'vite.config.ts does not mention CALCULA_E2E' and 'global-setup.ts spawns tauri dev without CALCULA_E2E'. During diagnosis the same effect was obtained from the harness side by routing the websocket away, which is what made the 8-of-8 identical replay possible.

source.runId: BUG-0074 verification: running the fixed file a second time against one app process.

violation.message: comments-notes.spec.ts COULD NOT RUN TWICE AGAINST ONE APP, AND THE SECOND RUN'S FAILURES WERE NOT SCREENSHOTS. Measured after the BUG-0074 fix: a second run of the file on the same app process failed FOUR tests, none of them a pixel comparison. add_comment and add_note refuse a cell that already carries one, so expect(result.success).toBe(true) failed at W1, W2, W3 and X1 against the annotations the FIRST run left. Annotations are a residue class of their own: they are not cell state (clear_range_with_options does not touch them) and not floating objects (the residue guard cannot see them), so nothing in the suite has ever removed one. Same family as BUG-0074 -- a spec that creates state and does not remove it -- but the state is the file's OWN, which is why it shows up as a failed assertion rather than a changed picture.

repro.description: cd app; cold app; run tests/comments-notes.spec.ts twice WITHOUT restarting the app. Before the fix the second run reports 4 failed / 3 passed, all on expect(result.success).toBe(true).

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The spec creates comments and notes and never deletes them.

fix.diffSummary: A test.afterAll deletes every comment and note in W1:X10 -- the ground the file's header claims -- and clears the cells, then announces app:annotations-changed so Review's indicator cache stops painting triangles for annotations the backend has already forgotten. DELIBERATELY NOT a beforeEach: the notes-cell-with-indicator golden clips X1 with 4 px of padding, and those pixels contain 15 px of the COMMENT triangle that test 1 puts on W1. That cross-test dependency is real and documented; wiping annotations between tests would have deleted it from the golden silently. The file's tests may depend on each other; the RUN may not depend on the previous run. Verified: cold 7/7, then warm 7/7 and warm 7/7 against the same app.

source.runId: Close-out pass. Found by reading BUG-0076's own fix for the CLASS rather than the instance: `announceStyleEntries`'s comment claimed 'there is no other door to the command', so every other command returning the same FormattingResult was checked.

violation.message: A NAMED STYLE APPLIED THROUGH `@api` PAINTS THE DOCUMENT DEFAULT. BUG-0076 primed the frontend style cache from `FormattingResult.styles` at the `applyFormatting` / `applyBorderPreset` wrappers in `src/core/lib/tauri-api.ts`, and that function's own comment asserted there was 'no other door to the command'. True of `apply_formatting`; FALSE of the style cache. `apply_named_style` and `apply_named_style_range` return the SAME `FormattingResult` with the same `styles` array, their wrappers live in `src/api/backend.ts`, and both are exported through `@api` (`src/api/index.ts`, `src/api/lib.ts`) for extensions to call. Neither announced anything, so an extension that applies a named style mints a registry index the cache does not hold and `getStyleFromCache` falls back to index 0 -- the document default. MEASURED at the unit tier on the real hooks (`formatStyleCachePrime.test.tsx`, real `tauri-api`, fake backend with a real dedup registry): after `applyNamedStyleRange('Accent1', 0,0,0,0)` with no `grid:refresh`, the renderer's own lookup returned backgroundColor '#ffffff' while the backend reported '#00A650'. SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: no LIVE reproduction was achieved. Every caller in the tree today happens to compensate -- the ScriptNotebook host hand-dispatches `styles:refresh` (a third local patch of this same class, after `useHomeTabState` and `Reports/lib/reportRefresh.ts`), and the script host's `afterCellDataChange` schedules `grid:refresh`, which fires BUG-0076's count-based heal. A staged live probe (`e2e/results/named-style-prime2.mjs`, three stages, with a primed-door control) found both doors painting the fill, because the heal had already covered the index. The defect is therefore reachable by any NEW `@api` caller and by no current one.

repro.description: vitest run src/core/components/Spreadsheet/__tests__/formatStyleCachePrime.test.tsx -- the case 'a NAMED style primes the cache too'. Before the fix: AssertionError, expected '#ffffff' to be '#00A650'. The case deliberately dispatches no `grid:refresh`, because that event triggers the heal and would mask which DOOR announced.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The prime was attached to two of the four wrappers that receive a FormattingResult, and the comment recording that decision named the COMMAND rather than the style cache, so the remaining doors were never looked for.

fix.diffSummary: `announceStyleEntries` is EXPORTED and both named-style wrappers in src/api/backend.ts call it, so every wrapper that receives a FormattingResult announces through one function. Its doc comment is corrected: the claim was about `apply_formatting`, not about the style cache, and the class is the DOOR rather than the command. Pinned by a new case in formatStyleCachePrime.test.tsx that models `apply_named_style_range` on named_styles_cmd.rs (rewrites the cells' style index wholesale, returns cells + styles) and asserts the renderer's own `getStyleFromCache` lookup. Red before (paints #ffffff), green after; 7/7.

source.runId: Close-out pass, running the `invariant` project -- one of the three projects the previous pass never ran. Found by reading the walker's OWN warning as arithmetic instead of as luck.

violation.message: THE INVARIANT PROJECT'S SAVE/RELOAD ORACLE COULD NOT RUN ON ANY SEED. `OracleBattery` fires the save/reload round-trip when `checkpointCount % saveReloadEvery === 0` and defaults `saveReloadEvery` to 4. `state-consistency.spec.ts` runs 75 actions at a cadence of 25 (3 checkpoints) and a rapid-fire walk of 50 at 25 (2 checkpoints). 3 % 4 and 2 % 4 are never 0, so the oracle had NEVER executed in that project -- not 'did not fire this run', but could not, by arithmetic, on any seed or any weighting. Every run printed its own '[WARNING] the save/reload round-trip never ran -- persistence was not exercised' and then reported '2 passed', so the warning read like bad luck. MEASURED on two cold runs before the fix (seeds 20260811 and 20260815): 'save/reload round-trip: 0 run(s)' on all four walks. This is the exact failure mode the collection guard exists for, one layer down: a suite reporting a clean pass for coverage it structurally did not have.

repro.description: cd app; INVARIANT_SEED=20260811 npm run e2e:invariant. Before the fix the coverage line reads 'recalc consistency: 3 run(s); save/reload round-trip: 0 run(s)' on the main walk and '2 run(s) ... 0 run(s)' on the rapid-fire walk, and the run passes. After: '1 run(s)' on both.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The walk length, the checkpoint cadence and the oracle cadence live in three files and nothing had ever compared them. The default was chosen for the soak project (150/25 = 6 checkpoints, where it does fire) and inherited by a project whose walks are half that length.

fix.diffSummary: Two halves, and the second is worth more than the first. (1) Both invariant walks now STATE their cadence -- SAVE_RELOAD_EVERY_MAIN=3, SAVE_RELOAD_EVERY_RAPID=2 -- so persistence is exercised exactly once per walk (more often would cost the undo oracle its baseline, which save/reload resets). (2) `WalkRunner.run` now REFUSES a walk whose cadence cannot come due: `plannedCheckpointCount` (an UPPER bound, so a wall-clock budget can only make it over-count) is compared against `saveReloadEvery` by `describeUnreachableSaveReloadCadence`, which names all three numbers and prescribes the three legal fixes -- including `saveReloadEvery: 0` to say 'this walk deliberately does not exercise persistence'. A guard that cannot run is not a guard that passed. Pinned by oracleCadenceReachable.test.ts (10 cases: the arithmetic, the boundary at exactly one checkpoint short, the 0-means-opt-out case, and the real spec's configuration READ OUT OF ITS SOURCE plus an assertion that both batteries state the cadence rather than inheriting the default). Sabotage: setting SAVE_RELOAD_EVERY_MAIN back to 4 turned exactly one case red with the measured sentence; restored byte-identical (sha256) and 10/10.

source.runId: Close-out pass. Struck twice in one session: once at the start of an `invariant` run (which died with exit 127 immediately after '[e2e] CDP ready'), and once on a `soak` run, where it failed ALL 12 tests.

violation.message: A COLD E2E LAUNCH CAN COME UP WITH AN EMPTY #root, AND THE HARNESS REPORTS IT AS N PRODUCT FAILURES. Measured from the failing run's own trace: the page had loaded from Vite (frameUrl http://localhost:5173/, the full index.html DOM present, <title>app</title>) and `#root` was EMPTY -- the frontend module never executed, so React never mounted. The backend was alive and had logged its first three lines (AppState created, locale sv-SE detected). Every test then failed identically on `page.waitForSelector("[data-focus-container='spreadsheet']")` after 60s: 12 failed / 1 skipped, including specs with no dependence on the seed. The report contains twelve Playwright TimeoutErrors and NOTHING that says the application never mounted, so the run is indistinguishable at a glance from a product regression -- and the screenshot attachment is a blank white page. NOT REPRODUCIBLE: an immediate cold re-run of the same seed from a verified-zero process table passed 12/1 skipped. Two hypotheses were CHECKED AND ELIMINATED: (a) a leaked app.exe or WebView2 browser process from the previous run -- the process table was zero app.exe, and the 30 surviving msedgewebview2 processes were inspected and all belong to Windows SearchHost, not Calcula; (b) an HTTP failure fetching the module -- the trace's network log is empty because tracing starts after load, so this is UNRESOLVED rather than excluded. Vite's dependency re-optimisation on a cold start is the leading unproven candidate. FOURTH OBSERVATION, AND IT REFRAMES THE ENTRY (measured 2026-08-15 on the app left running for the next session, an ordinary cold launch): the page reached http://localhost:5173/ and then sat with #root EMPTY for approximately 55 SECONDS before React mounted, polled at 5s intervals -- 11 consecutive readings of {root:0, spreadsheet:false} followed by {root:1, spreadsheet:true}. The fixture ceiling is 60s. So the empty-#root state is NOT exotic: it is the ordinary cold-start condition while Vite transforms the module graph for the first time, and the three failures are that transform running just past a ceiling it normally clears by ~5 seconds. That also explains why every re-run passed (Vite's cache was warm) and why it struck the FIRST project run after an idle period. What remains unproven is whether the overrun is purely transform time or a stall.

repro.description:
REPRODUCIBLE, and the original 'not reproducible on demand' was measured wrongly: the re-runs that passed met a dev server that was ALREADY UP, and the cost is paid once per dev-server START, not per launch. To reproduce: kill every app.exe and whatever holds port 5173, launch `yarn tauri dev --config src-tauri/tauri.e2e.conf.json` with the Rust binary already built, and poll the page. 5 of 5 such launches came up with #root EMPTY for 16.8-28.4 seconds after reaching localhost:5173. Cheaper still, with no app at all: start `vite` alone and crawl the module graph over HTTP from /src/main.tsx at concurrency 8 -- 1,420 modules in 37 s cold against 0.4 s on a second traversal of the same server.

THE DOSE-RESPONSE IS THE TELL, and it is what to re-measure if this ever comes back: time from DEV-SERVER READY to mount is a CONSTANT ~38 s regardless of when the browser navigates. Vite idle 10.4 s -> #root empty 28.4 s; idle 22.1 s -> empty 16.8 s; idle 211.8 s -> empty 3.0 s. Idle + window = 38.0-39.5 s across eight launches. A cost triggered by the page could not behave that way.

Two signatures to check BEFORE blaming the product, unchanged and still good: (a) every test failing on the same waitForSelector with a blank-white failure screenshot, and a trace frame-snapshot whose <div id="root"> has no children; (b) window.__calcImport ABSENT, which dates the failure before main.tsx ran its body.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: MEASURED 2026-08-15, no longer a hypothesis. Vite's dev-server file watcher is `chokidar.watch(root)` with root = `app/`, and `app/src-tauri/` holds an in-repo Cargo `target/` of 100,175 files in 9,118 directories. Chokidar registers a native fs.watch per entry AFTER `server.listen()` has printed "ready in 380 ms" and begun answering HTTP, and that registration blocks the dev server's ONE thread. So the server serves the static index.html instantly and then starves every /src/*.ts request behind the walk: the page sits at http://localhost:5173/ with <div id="root"> present and EMPTY and window.__calcImport absent, which is exactly the state the failing run's trace recorded. A CPU profile of the slow traversal put 74.5% of samples in one stack (_addToNodeFs -> _watchWithNodeFs -> createFsWatchInstance -> node:fs.watch -> native FSWatcher.start). NOT transform time, NOT a deadlock, and NOT the dependency optimizer, which logged "Hash is consistent. Skipping."

fix.diffSummary:
DIAGNOSIS LANDED; the rest is scoped and open. (1) DONE: describeUnmountedApp distinguishes three states -- #root empty ("a HARNESS/STARTUP failure, NOT a product failure; nothing after this is a test result"), #root populated ("the frontend DID mount; that is a product question") and unreadable ("UNKNOWN", because calling an unreadable page empty would be a claim). It dates the failure with window.__calcImport (installed early in main.tsx, so its absence means main.tsx never ran its body) and carries a console tail collected from the fixture onward, saying so explicitly when there is none. Five cases pin the wording, as appGoneMessage.test.ts does for the app-gone arm. This turns N identical waitForSelector timeouts -- 18 of them in the visual project, where it reads as the entire golden corpus breaking -- into one named cause. (2) OPEN, and now the LEADING fix given the ~55s measurement: raise the first-mount ceiling well clear of a cold Vite transform (the current 60s has ~5s of margin), and/or warm the dev server before the first fixture waits. Deliberately not done in this pass: it changes the timeout that bounds every project and deserves its own measured baseline of cold mount times rather than one sample. (3) OPEN: capture the Vite request log from global-setup so an overrun can be told from a stall -- Playwright's trace starts after load and its network log is empty. (4) A retry stays LAST: a retry that hides the state deletes the evidence (2) and (3) need.

=== ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-15 (second pass) ===
IT STILL REPRODUCED, and far more often than 'not reproducible on demand' suggested: 5 of 5 cold launches of the real app with the Rust binary already built came up with #root EMPTY for 26.1 / 26.3 / 27.9 / 28.4 / 16.8 SECONDS after the page reached localhost:5173. It is the ORDINARY cold-start condition, not an exotic one. The single launch that did NOT show it is the one where cargo recompiled for 3m20s first, giving the dev server 200 s of idle in which to finish its watcher walk before the WebView navigated -- mount then took 3.0 s. That contrast is the whole mechanism.

MEASURED against the dev server ALONE (no cargo, no app.exe, no WebView2, so CPU contention is excluded), crawling the 1,420-module graph over HTTP the way the browser does, order-controlled:
  watcher default        1,420 modules in 37.0 s / 37.4 s / 62 s / >120 s
                         (one run served THREE modules in 120 seconds)
  ignoring src-tauri     1,420 modules in  3.4 s /  3.3 s /  3.7 s
  chokidar watched       9,720 dirs / 113,460 entries  ->  545 / 3,443
  SECOND traversal       0.4-0.6 s in BOTH  <- the transform is never the cost, which is why every immediate re-run 'passed': it met a server that was already up.

The 37-120 s spread brackets the ~55 s fourth observation exactly, and shows the window is UNBOUNDED rather than a fixed ~55 s -- so raising the fixture ceiling was never going to be a fix, only a bigger number to overrun.

FIX: `server.watch.ignored` in app/vite.config.ts excludes **/src-tauri/**, e2e/results, the *-snapshots golden corpora, test-results and dist. Nothing there is a frontend module; src-tauri is Rust and Tauri's own dev watcher owns it. === THE HARNESS GUARD LANDED 2026-08-15 (third pass, open-decisions §32) ===
The residual the root-cause pass left open -- "(a) the harness guard that fails the RUN instead of N product tests" -- is DONE. A BARRIER in global-setup (app/e2e/startupBarrier.ts) connects over the same CDP the fixtures use, reads the page once a second, and refuses the run before the first test, so a never-mounted launch now reports ZERO test results instead of 12 or 18 product-looking failures. The decision and every sentence live in app/e2e/startupGuard.ts, which imports nothing from Playwright and is unit-tested (33 cases on a virtual clock); the mid-run half writes a marker that the EXISTING collection-guard reporter reads in onEnd, so there is one first-position reporter, one assertCollectionGuardPresent handshake protecting both duties, and no second reporting channel. Escape hatch STARTUP_GUARD=off, loud. Six named failures: never-mounted-stalled, dev-server-not-answering, never-mounted-cap, no-page, wrong-origin, no-tauri-bridge (the documented tauri.e2e.conf.json symptom, which fires in 0.0s).
THE BOUND IS NOT A MOUNT DEADLINE, deliberately. It is a quiet window whose budget is chosen by document.readyState: 45s when the document is COMPLETE and the resource count is frozen (nothing outstanding, so nothing is coming -- BUG-0082's exact signature), 300s while the document is still LOADING (the page is blamed on the dev server, not the frontend), and a 900s absolute cap as an anti-hang backstop. That split is measured: on the pre-watcher-fix tree the page went 218 SECONDS with nothing changing -- two resources at 12.4s, the next at 230.9s -- while blocked on one /src/main.tsx request, and a stall window over network activity alone would have failed that healthy-if-pathological launch at 57s. readyState was "interactive" throughout that silence and "complete" in the dead state.
PROVED BOTH WAYS, LIVE: --project=visual (the project this bug turned into "18 of 18 failed") against a genuinely dead launch -> exit 1, ZERO tests reported, one named failure, zero test lines in the log; the same project against a healthy app -> "[startup-guard] the frontend mounted after 0.0s" and 18/18 passed, exit 0. Also fired at 45.5s against a controlled never-mounting stub and at 0.0s against a stub with window.__TAURI__ undefined. Sabotage-checked: const stalled=false fails exactly the firing case, const stalled=true fails the four patience cases, and removing one assertAppMounted call or flipping the fixture's <=0 fails the wiring pins.
FOUND WHILE MEASURING, AND STILL UNEXPLAINED: with app/node_modules/.vite deleted on the pre-fix tree, the page reached readyState complete with 250 resources loaded and #root empty, and stayed that way for TEN MINUTES. A reload with console listeners attached caught "Warning: Invalid hook call" plus "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useReducer')" in <GridProvider> -- a SECOND React instance, i.e. a mid-flight dependency re-optimisation whose full-reload could not be delivered because CALCULA_E2E=1 disables HMR. That is a different failure from the starved watcher: it makes an ARRIVED page render nothing, and waiting never recovers it. The same recipe after the watcher fix mounted in 7.8s, so it may need a long serve window to reproduce. Repro recipe and console signature are in the guard's own failure message.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-15 (integration pass, open-decisions §34) ===
Both items this entry left open are now resolved, and the entry is CLOSED.

The two live outcomes come from the SAME command on the SAME project, so the sabotage is demonstrably load-bearing rather than a no-op.
(b) 'raising the first-mount ceiling should be re-decided against the NEW baseline' -- DECIDED: no change. Re-measured after the watcher fix, cold mount is now 2.0-4.1 s (four cold auto-launches this pass: 4.1 s, 2.2 s, 2.0 s, 2.0 s) against a 60 s fixture ceiling. The ~55 s sample that made a raise look urgent was a symptom of the starved watcher, and the margin is now ~15x. Raising a ceiling to accommodate a defect that no longer exists would only delay the next real detection.
REPRODUCTION EVIDENCE, which is the honest answer to 'is it gone': across this pass every cold launch that was supposed to mount, mounted -- and none of them approached the old window. The only unmounted launches were the two deliberately sabotaged ones.

Measured by exhaustive search: zero matches for componentDidCatch / getDerivedStateFromError / ErrorBoundary / react-error-boundary across all of app/src and app/extensions. There are FIVE React roots (main.tsx plus chartSpecEditorMain, objectScriptMain, modelEditorMain, packageInspectorMain), and all five HTML shells are `
` and nothing else -- no fallback content, no

repro.description: Make any component in the initial tree throw (e.g. `throw new Error('x')` at the top of App's render) and start the app. Before the fix: a white window, forever, with nothing on screen. After the fix: a named failure panel with the error, the component stack, a Reload button and a Copy details button.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: No root error boundary was ever added; the HTML shells carry no fallback content either, so there are two independent routes to a blank window and neither had anything in it.

fix.diffSummary:
A RootErrorBoundary now sits above every one of the five React roots, OUTSIDE StrictMode and above every provider (a boundary nested under the thing that threw catches nothing). It renders a named failure panel -- which window failed, the error, the stack, the component stack -- with Reload and Copy details.

IT IMPORTS REACT AND NOTHING ELSE, on purpose: no styled-components, no theme, no store, no @api. Every one of those is a plausible CAUSE of the error being caught, and a fallback that renders through the broken subsystem is not a fallback. All styling is inline literals.

Two test tiers. Behaviour: a throwing child leaves the container NON-empty and names both the surface and the message; the injected reporting hook is called; a reporting hook that ITSELF throws does not replace the original failure with its own. Census: the entry points are ENUMERATED FROM DISK (every app/src/*.tsx containing createRoot) and each must wrap its root and name its surface -- because the fix is one wrapper element per file and a sixth window added later would otherwise ship blank with every test still green. The census has a non-vacuity case (it must find at least 5) and was verified with teeth: unwrapping packageInspectorMain turns it red.

SCOPED, NOT DONE -- the OTHER route to a blank window. A React boundary cannot catch a failure BEFORE React runs: a module-level throw, or a bundle that never loads, leaves #root empty with the boundary never constructed. The bounded fix is fallback content in the five HTML shells plus a boot watchdog that reveals it if #root is still empty after N seconds. It is NOT done here because it collides with the E2E startup guard landing in the same pass: that guard reads `#root.childElementCount > 0` as proof that the frontend mounted, and a watchdog that injects children into #root would make it report a startup failure as a product question. Doing it needs a marker both sides agree on (e.g. `data-calc-boot-failed` on #root) and should be settled with the guard's owner.

Also NOT done and deliberately so: window.onerror / unhandledrejection reporting. Those do not blank the window, which is the failure this entry is about.

PENDING: proof in the live app. The boundary is proven under jsdom (11 cases). It has not yet been shown catching a real throw in a running Tauri window, because the E2E app and port 5173 were held by a concurrent pass throughout.

=== LIVE PROOF OBTAINED 2026-08-15 (integration pass, open-decisions §33c) ===
The PENDING item -- 'it has not yet been shown catching a real throw in a running Tauri window, because the E2E app and port 5173 were held by a concurrent pass throughout' -- is DONE, and the status moves from fixed-pending-live-proof to fixed.
A deliberate `throw new Error(...)` at the top of App's render, launched cold as an ordinary E2E auto-launch: the boundary caught it and rendered the named panel, and the harness read its text back verbatim -- 'Calcula could not start', 'error: Error: SABOTAGE-0084: deliberate boot-time throw', component stack 'at App (http://localhost:5173/src/shell/App.tsx:8:9)' / 'at RootErrorBoundary (.../RootErrorBoundary.tsx:69:8)'. Before this fix that window was blank and silent. Sabotage reverted; App.tsx verified byte-identical to its backup afterwards.

It had NOT -- the register contained zero occurrences of 'BUG-0083' and zero of 'RootErrorBoundary', because two agents appended to the same 1.2 MB file concurrently and one whole-file write landed on top of the other. source.runId: Integration pass over BUG-0082 (E2E startup guard) and BUG-0083 (root error boundary), which were built concurrently by two separate efforts and landed together. Found by checking the COMBINATION rather than either report -- both touched the same signal and neither owned it.

violation.message: THE STARTUP GUARD READ A CRASHED BOOT AS A HEALTHY MOUNT, so BUG-0082's misreporting came back through BUG-0083's front door. The guard's ONLY mount signal was `#root.childElementCount > 0`, chosen when the only two states were 'React rendered the app' and 'React never ran'. BUG-0083 then added a `RootErrorBoundary` above all five React roots whose failure panel is ITSELF a child of `#root`. So after both fixes, an app that throws during first render satisfies the mount check: the barrier prints 'the frontend mounted after Xs', lets the run proceed, and every spec then times out on `[data-focus-container='spreadsheet']` -- N product-looking failures for ONE systemic fact, which is precisely the reporting failure BUG-0082 exists to delete. The same signal is read a second time in `e2e/fixtures.ts` for the mid-run case, where it was worse than useless: `rootChildCount > 0` selected the arm that says 'the frontend DID mount and the spreadsheet container specifically is missing -- that is a product question, not a startup one', sending the reader to hunt a missing container while the page was displaying the stack trace of the actual throw. Neither report claimed this was handled; BUG-0083's own fix note flagged the collision ('#root.childElementCount > 0 has a second meaning now') and left it to the guard's owner, and the guard shipped before that note existed. It was nobody's defect and therefore nobody's fix.

repro.description:
Make any component in the initial tree throw (BUG-0083's own repro), then run any project. BEFORE: `[startup-guard] the frontend mounted after 0.4s`, the run proceeds, and every spec fails on the spreadsheet selector -- 18 of 18 in `visual`, reading as a total product collapse. AFTER: the run ends in global-setup with kind `boot-error`, ZERO tests reported, and the panel's own text (surface, error, both stacks) printed in the failure message.

Unit-level: `waitForMount` over a probe with `rootChildCount: 1, bootErrorText: 'boom'` must return `{ok: false, kind: 'boot-error'}`, not `{ok: true}`.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: MEASURED, not hypothesised. Two correct fixes, built in parallel, sharing one signal that only one of them knew the meaning of. `#root` having children meant 'the app is up' until the moment a boundary was allowed to render into `#root`, and nothing re-derived the meaning because neither change looked like it touched the other. The general shape is worth keeping: a boolean whose definition is owned by one module and whose truth conditions are set by another.

fix.diffSummary:
`StartupProbe` gains `bootErrorText: string | null`, read from `[data-testid='root-error-boundary']` -- the marker BUG-0083's panel already carried, so no product change was needed. A new `MountFailureKind` of `boot-error` is checked INSIDE the mounted branch of `waitForMount` and BEFORE the Tauri-bridge check, because a crash early enough to precede the bridge would otherwise be reported as a launcher misconfiguration and send the reader to the wrong file.

THE VERDICT SENTENCE IS NO LONGER SHARED, and that is the substance of the fix rather than a detail of it. Every other arm ends 'this is a HARNESS/STARTUP failure, NOT a product failure -- re-launch and re-run'. For `boot-error` both halves of that are false: it IS the product, and re-running cannot help a deterministic boot throw. Printing the standard footer over a real crash would have exonerated the code that broke -- the same lie as BUG-0082's, pointed the other way. The arm instead says 'this IS a product failure, but it is ONE failure, reported once' and prints what the boundary reported.

`fixtures.ts` gets the matching fourth arm for the mid-run case, and -- the part that actually matters there -- is now EXCLUDED from writing the startup marker when a boundary is on screen, because that marker triggers the banner asserting the failures are not product failures.

Teeth verified by three sabotages, each producing a targeted red and no other: disabling the boot-error branch failed exactly the two barrier cases; collapsing the verdict split failed exactly the attribution case; disabling the fixtures arm failed exactly the two message cases. Guarded further by source pins in `startupBarrierWired.test.ts` (the barrier must probe for the boundary; its unreadable-page fallback must report `null`, never `""`, which would claim a boundary that reported nothing).

violation.message: THE .XLSX EXPORT WRITES DOCUMENT PROPERTIES AND THE IMPORT THREW THEM AWAY. core/persistence/src/xlsx_writer.rs fills rust_xlsxwriter's DocProperties from Workbook::properties on every save (title, author, subject, description, keywords, category, plus a dcterms:created stamp), and core/persistence/src/xlsx_reader.rs built its Workbook with `properties: crate::WorkbookProperties::default()` -- it never opened docProps/core.xml at all. A one-way loss THROUGH THE APP'S OWN EXPORT: save as .xlsx, reopen the file Calcula itself just wrote, and every document property is blank, with nothing anywhere saying it was dropped. Not a fidelity preference against a foreign producer -- the bytes are present in the file and were written by this code.

repro.description:
Unit: build a Workbook with non-empty `properties`, `save_xlsx` it, `load_xlsx` it back, read `properties`. BEFORE: every field is the empty string. AFTER: every field round-trips. Pinned by `xlsx_writer::tests::document_properties_survive_the_xlsx_round_trip`, which fails with `left: ""` / `right: "Quarterly Report"` when the reader wiring is reverted (verified by sabotage, 2026-08-15).

Product route: File > Save As > .xlsx on a workbook with document properties set, then File > Open on that same .xlsx -- the properties are gone.

triage.rootCause: The reader was written before the writer grew document properties and was never revisited. `parse_xlsx_styles` already opened the archive and already parsed non-style parts out of it (sheet visibility, workbookPr/@date1904), so the archive pass that could have read docProps existed the whole time -- the part was simply never read.

fix.diffSummary: docProps/core.xml is parsed with quick-xml by LOCAL NAME (dc:title, dc:subject, dc:creator -> author, cp:keywords, dc:description -> description, cp:category, dcterms:created/modified), never by namespace prefix, so a producer that binds the same namespaces to different prefixes is still read. A missing or unreadable part leaves every field the Default empty string and never fails the load: document metadata is advisory and must not cost a user their cells. The element names are taken from what the writer (rust_xlsxwriter/src/core.rs) actually emits rather than from the Calcula field names, because the two disagree in two places (author <- dc:creator, description <- dc:description via set_comment).

source.runId: Targeted reproduction of the SECOND, unexplained BUG-0082 mechanism recorded in open-decisions §32 ("a second React instance from a mid-flight Vite dependency re-optimisation", recorded and never reproduced).

violation.message: THE DEV SERVER SERVES MORE THAN ONE COPY OF REACT TO ONE PAGE, AND UNDER E2E IT CAN NEVER REPAIR IT. Vite pre-bundles dependencies into node_modules/.vite/deps_temp_<hash>/ and RENAMES that directory onto deps/. Measured on this tree by clearing the cache and running the optimiser in a loop: 3 of 10 runs FAILED with `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rename '...\.vite\deps_temp_78efe380' -> '...\.vite\deps'`, each leaving a deps_temp_* behind. A failed rename leaves no usable deps/, so the server discovers dependencies request-by-request WHILE THE PAGE IS LOADING and serves /node_modules/.vite/deps/react.js?v=<hash> under more than one hash. Different URL = different module instance, so hooks are registered against one React dispatcher and read through another: `Warning: Invalid hook call` + `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useReducer')` in <GridProvider> -- the exact console lines §32 recorded and could not explain. Vite's own repair is a `full-reload` over the HMR channel, and CALCULA_E2E=1 disables HMR deliberately (a stray fast-refresh resets GridProvider's useReducer mid-capture), so the page stays dead at readyState=complete with an empty #root indefinitely, and the harness reports it as N product failures. Measured rate: 4 of 11 cold-cache launches served react.js under FOUR hashes in a single page load. Contributing cause on this machine: app/node_modules sits inside the Dropbox-synced tree and, unlike app/src-tauri/target and core/target, carried NO com.dropbox.ignored marker, so Dropbox held handles on the freshly written bundles -- 3/10 failures with it synced, 1/12 with it ignored.

repro.description:
rm -rf app/node_modules/.vite/deps*, start the dev server with CALCULA_E2E=1, then crawl the module graph over HTTP exactly as the browser does and count the distinct `?v=` hashes per dep (no browser needed -- app/e2e/depOptimizer.ts crawlModuleGraph does this). BEFORE: 4 of 11 launches produced 2-4 hashes for react.js, 18-30 refused requests, and the server log showing two `optimized dependencies changed. reloading` lines nobody could receive. AFTER (with scripts/ensure-dep-cache.mjs run first): 0 of 8 launches duplicated anything; two of the eight hit the EBUSY and the retry cleared it.

Faster reproduction of the underlying event: clear the cache and run `npx vite optimize --force` in a loop -- 3 of 10 fail with EBUSY on the rename.

triage.rootCause: A directory rename that only usually succeeds was load-bearing for module identity. Nothing in the harness required the dependency cache to be COMPLETE before the app loaded a module, so the optimiser's discovery rounds raced the page's own crawl; and the one mechanism Vite has for recovering from that race (a full-reload over HMR) is switched off for E2E on purpose. Neither half is wrong alone -- together they make an unrecoverable state reachable at ~36% of cold-cache launches.

filesChanged: app/scripts/ensure-dep-cache.mjs (NEW: complete the optimisation before any server exists, retrying the transient EBUSY; wired as npm predev, which Tauri's beforeDevCommand runs, so it covers interactive dev, the E2E auto-launch and the manual launcher from one place)
app/scripts/dropbox-ignore.mjs (NEW: mark the long-lived build trees com.dropbox.ignored; app/node_modules was the one that was missing)
app/e2e/depOptimizer.ts (NEW: parseDepVersion / collectDuplicateDepVersions / crawlModuleGraph + re-export of the repair)
app/e2e/pageState.ts (probe reports depUrls from the page's own resource timings)
app/e2e/startupGuard.ts (new MountFailureKind `duplicate-deps`, decided FIRST and without waiting out a stall window)
app/e2e/global-setup.ts (note recording why the repair is NOT run from here)
fix.diffSummary:
PREVENTION plus DETECTION, because prevention can be skipped. Prevention: ensureDepCache() reads the cache off disk, deletes the deps_temp_* a failed rename leaves behind, and runs `vite optimize --force` with bounded retries until deps/ holds its bundles AND a parseable _metadata.json -- exit status alone is not the answer, since the measured failures exited non-zero AND left an empty directory. It runs from predev, i.e. before a dev server exists, so every discovery round happens while nothing depends on the result. It NEVER fails the command: a machine where the rename can never succeed still gets its run, and gets the EBUSY printed verbatim. Detection: the startup probe reports every /node_modules/.vite/deps/*?v=* URL from performance.getEntriesByType('resource'), and the barrier fails the run by name -- immediately, not after the 45s stall window, because two copies of React are terminal -- printing the duplicated deps and the one-command remedy. It fires even when the page APPEARS to have mounted, since every spec after that would be running against an incoherent module graph.

NOT a retry of the thing that failed (BUG-0082's fix note keeps retries last): nothing is re-run and no evidence is discarded, a DIFFERENT step is completed first, before the step that would fail is asked to start.

violation.message: THE ENTIRE E2E HARNESS WAS OUTSIDE THE TYPE GATE. `npm run check-types` compiled tsconfig.check.json -- src/, extensions/, scripts/ -- and NOT ONE of the 212 TypeScript files under app/e2e/. Playwright and vitest both transpile with esbuild, which strips types WITHOUT checking them, so a type error anywhere in the harness (fixtures, helpers, the collection guard, the app-died marker, the startup barrier) was invisible until it threw at runtime -- inside a run whose entire purpose is to say whether the PRODUCT is broken. The same shape as every other defect this programme has paid for: an instrument that can stop working and say nothing.

source.runId: Owned pass on the undo round-trip oracle. The register (31k item 2) had recorded 10 walks / 32 checkpoints / 0 decided and left the cause as 'structure actions clear the stack (Excel parity)'.

violation.message: THE UNDO ROUND-TRIP ORACLE COULD NOT DECIDE. It captured its baseline at the start of a 25-action window and only asked at the END of the window whether that baseline was still reachable -- so ONE history-ending action anywhere in the window forfeited all 25 actions' worth of evidence. Measured live with the fix switched off (12 walks, seeds 20260815001-007, `invariant` project): 5 of 28 checkpoints decided, and 6 of 11 completed walks decided ZERO, while every one of them reported '[OK] Walk passed'. Undo is where this programme found a sheet's whole cell map replaced by another sheet's snapshot, an undo stack outliving its document across File > Open, and undo recalculating no dependents at all -- and the instrument aimed at that surface was structurally unable to fire over it.

repro.description: Set AB_NO_UNDO_REBASE=1 (the A/B switch used to measure this, since removed) and run `npx playwright test --project=invariant` on seeds 20260815004 and 20260815006: both walks report 'undo round-trip: 0 decided ... 3 undecided' and, before the meta-assertion landed, still printed '[OK] Walk passed'. The generator-level measurement is in app/e2e/__tests__/undoOracleDecidability.test.ts: 6 of 120 windows in the invariant project's own shape contain no history-ending action.

triage.rootCause: The window was fixed at the checkpoint cadence, and a window-killer is common: five structural sheet commands END the undo history (Excel parity, correct), fr.rename/fr.delete are a sheet rename and a sheet delete, fr.create is neither undoable nor history-ending (so the created object survives every undo), and the walker's own `undo` action can pop past the baseline. The stated cause -- sheet structure -- is real but is the MINORITY one: in the generator census 276 of 370 window-killers (75%) are floating-range actions, which landed on 2026-08-13, after the observation the register attributed to sheets.
