fix.diffSummary: The walker re-captures the undo baseline the MOMENT it becomes unreachable, measured after every action from `get_undo_state` plus the snapshot's floating-range ids, instead of discovering 25 actions later that the window died at action 2. The verdict is not relaxed: the baseline digest is captured at the rebase point and the round trip pops exactly the ids above it, so a decided window is a genuinely replayable one. The action that forced each rebase is recorded and checked against the set of actions ENTITLED to end the history, because a rebase would otherwise absorb 'an ordinary cell edit cleared the undo stack' in silence. And a walk that decides zero round-trips now FAILS with `undo-evidence-missing` rather than printing a warning under '[OK] Walk passed'.
validatedBy: LIVE A/B on the same 6 seeds, `invariant` project, 12 walks each way. BEFORE (rebase off): 5 of 28 checkpoints decided, 174 transactions wound back, 6 of 11 completed walks decided ZERO. AFTER (rebase on): 25 of 28 decided, 514 transactions, 0 walks with zero evidence -- and one NEW failure, filed as BUG-0090.

FINAL verification run after BUG-0090's fix, same 6 seeds, 12 walks: all 12 pass, 27 of 30 checkpoints decided, 546 transactions wound back, 1 with nothing to undo, 2 undecided, 85 mid-window rebases and NONE by an action that had no business ending the history.
the meta-assertion fired on the BEFORE half -- 4 walks failed `undo-evidence-missing` where the old code printed the same fact as a warning under '[OK] Walk passed'. That is its sabotage proof.
cost, matched pair (seed 20260815002 main walk): 66s before, 68s after -- one `get_undo_state` per action plus 7 digests.
app/e2e/__tests__/undoOracleDecidability.test.ts (generator decidability, with a detector that fires)
app/e2e/__tests__/oracleCoverage.test.ts (undoEvidenceFailure on/off/disabled, rebase census, unexpected-ender warning)
app/e2e/__tests__/undoHistoryHorizon.test.ts (undoBaselineUnreachableReason agrees with the checkpoint's own verdict, in its precedence)

source.runId: The FIRST window the newly-decidable undo oracle ever judged. Before the rebase it was undecided and reported nothing.

violation.message: Undoing 22 steps did not restore the checkpoint state. 1 differences; first: activeSheet: 2 -> 0

repro.description: invariant seed 20260815001: sheet.copy, sheet.add (baseline re-captured here, activeSheet 2), structure.insert-row, sheet.switch {tabIndex: 0}, then 22 ordinary transactions on Sheet1. Winding all 22 back restores every cell, style and object -- exactly ONE digest difference in the whole workbook, `activeSheet: 2 -> 0`, which is the walk's own sheet switch.

triage.rootCause: A HARNESS false positive, not a product defect, and false BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by degree. `activate_sheet` is `DocumentEffect::deliberately_clean(CleanReason::Navigation)` and records no undo entry -- looking at a workbook must not dirty it -- so a sheet switch inside a window is invisible to the history and no number of undo steps can put the view back. Undo does move the active sheet, to the sheet the undone change happened on, which is Excel's behaviour and deliberate (`undo_commands::activation_target`). So a perfectly correct product fails this comparison every time a window contains a sheet switch, and the undo diff profile was comparing it.

fix.diffSummary: `activeSheet` is excluded from the UNDO profile and still compared under saveReload, where it is real document state (`workbook.active_sheet` is persisted, so a save/open that lost it is a defect). What is lost is stated rather than glossed: undo's own activation behaviour is covered at a tighter tier by app/src-tauri/src/undo_sheet_activation_tests.rs (undo, redo, hidden target, every per-sheet store, the dependency maps), and frontend/backend disagreement about which sheet is active is still caught per action by the cheap invariants.
validatedBy: app/e2e/__tests__/digestDiffProfiles.test.ts, including the self-test that a real cell difference is still reported and that saveReload still compares activeSheet
invariant seed 20260815001 re-run green after the change (see the final verification run)

source.runId: Found while wiring the per-action rebase into WalkRunner.run -- the two checkpoint call sites had to be reconciled.

violation.message: THE WALK RAN ITS ENTIRE ORACLE BATTERY TWICE AT THE SAME STEP. The in-loop checkpoint fires on `step % cadence === 0 || isLastStep`, and the 'final off-cadence checkpoint' after the loop fired on `step % cadence !== 0` -- both true at the last step of any walk whose length is not a multiple of the cadence. A 40-action walk at cadence 25 therefore ran three checkpoints, not two: digests, the undo round-trip and the save/reload round-trip, a second time, over a state nothing had touched in between. It also made `plannedCheckpointCount` UNDER-count, which is the one direction its own docstring promises it never goes -- and that number is what `assertCadenceReachable` uses to refuse an unreachable save/reload cadence.

repro.description: Any walk whose `maxActions` is not a multiple of `oracleEveryNActions` (e.g. SOAK_ACTIONS=40, SOAK_ORACLE_EVERY=25) reported one more checkpoint than `plannedCheckpointCount(40, 25) = 2`.

triage.rootCause: Two independent conditions written at different times, neither aware the other could be true at the same step.

filesChanged: app/e2e/__tests__/oracleCadenceReachable.test.ts (pins that the count is now exact)
fix.diffSummary: The final off-cadence checkpoint is skipped when the in-loop one already ran at that step. The shipped projects (75/25, 50/25, 150/25) were all multiples and never hit it, which is why it survived; SOAK_ACTIONS is an env var and the 2026-08-13 soak run that measured '40 actions, two checkpoints' was one setting away from it.
validatedBy: app/e2e/__tests__/oracleCadenceReachable.test.ts
the invariant project's 75/25 and 50/25 walks report 3 and 2 checkpoints, unchanged

source.runId: integration/verification pass (2026-08-16): auditing the image-ingress track's security verdict, whose source assertion scans only the Controls extension -- a SECOND `<input type=file>` lives in ScriptableObjects and was outside every claim made about ingress.

violation.message: AN IMPORTED FILE CHOSE THE PRIVILEGE TIER OF THE CODE IT INSTALLED. `importTemplate` (app/extensions/ScriptableObjects/lib/templateManager.ts) was `JSON.parse(json) as ObjectTemplate` -- a CAST, which validates nothing -- and the parsed object was persisted to %APPDATA%/Calcula/templates/ verbatim, `accessLevel` included. That field is load-bearing, not decorative: `stampFromTemplate` copies it onto the stamped `ObjectScriptDefinition`, and `buildHandleFromDefinition` (app/src/api/scriptHost/broker.ts) converts `accessLevel === "unlocked"` into `tier: "unlocked"`, which in ALLOWLIST terms is whole-workbook reach: api.getCellValue, api.setCellValue, api.updateCellsBatch over 100,000 cells, api.executeCommand. Object scripts run on their object's events, so no further gesture was required to execute it. Worse, the import carries no `provenance`, so `isDistributed` is false and the script lands in the MOST trusted bucket -- ui.html auto-granted, declared-capability ceiling taken from its own source pragmas -- rather than the consent-gated distributed one. The dialog's own empty state invites the user to 'import a .calcula-template file', so the user believes they are choosing a document and are in fact choosing executable code AND the privilege level it runs at. Nothing in the flow states the tier. The rule was already written one file away: `draftToScriptDefinition` (lib/scriptDrafts.ts) forces "restricted" because 'an AI-authored script must never arrive pre-escalated to the unlocked tier; raising it is a separate, deliberate human action in the editor.' The template import door simply never got it.

bugs.repro: Craft a .calcula-template file: valid `name`/`objectType`/`scriptSource`, plus `"accessLevel": "unlocked"`. Script Templates > Import Template... > choose it. Pre-fix: the stored template, and every script stamped from it, is unlocked-tier. Pinned by app/extensions/ScriptableObjects/__tests__/templateImportTier.test.ts.
bugs.triage: Security / transparency. Bounded by the fact that the user must pick the file through a native picker, and capability GRANTS still require consent (only the non-capability api.* surface widens) -- but that surface is read/write of the entire workbook, and the escalation was silent.
bugs.fix: importTemplate now (1) VALIDATES instead of casting -- name, objectType (against a Record keyed by the ScriptableObjectType union, so adding a type is a compile error rather than a silently unstampable template), scriptSource, and the optional description/metadata, throwing TemplateImportError otherwise; and (2) FORCES accessLevel to "restricted" regardless of what the file says, matching draftToScriptDefinition exactly. The id is freshly minted so an imported file cannot choose the identity a capability grant or source hash is keyed to. Locally-created templates (createTemplateFromScript, from the user's own script in trusted UI) still keep their tier -- the boundary drawn is the IMPORT door, not template creation.
bugs.validatedBy: app/extensions/ScriptableObjects/__tests__/templateImportTier.test.ts (17 tests). Sabotage-verified: restoring `accessLevel: raw.accessLevel === "unlocked" ? ...` (the pre-fix behaviour) fails exactly 3 tests including the end-to-end import->stamp consequence; restoring the fix returns 17/17. PLUS the class guard: app/src/api/__tests__/fileIngressSurfaces.test.ts sweeps app/src and app/extensions for every WebView ingress shape (readAsDataURL / readAsArrayBuffer / readAsText / new FileReader / type="file" / showOpenFilePicker) and holds the result against a declared inventory. Sabotage-verified in BOTH directions: adding an undeclared `<input type="file">` to another extension fails 'finds no UNDECLARED ingress surface'; removing the declared one fails 'has no DECLARED entry that no longer exists', so an inventory entry cannot outlive the code it describes.
bugs.evidenceNote: The two assertions that keep this guard aimed read the BROKER and ALLOWLIST SOURCE rather than a reconstruction, so if buildHandleFromDefinition stops deriving tier from accessLevel, or the api.* rows stop being unlocked-tier, the test reports that the premise moved instead of passing vacuously.
bugs.notes: NOT COVERED, stated rather than implied: a file written DIRECTLY into %APPDATA%/Calcula/templates/ never passes through importTemplate. Anything able to write there can already do worse, so the boundary is the import door. Also worth carrying: the image-ingress pass's 'no file input remains' assertion is scoped to app/extensions/Controls only, which is why this second one survived a security review that reported the ingress question settled. ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS, now closed: the image-ingress pass's absence assertion (extensions/Controls/__tests__/imageIngress.test.ts) iterates a HARD-CODED LIST OF SEVEN FILES, all inside app/extensions/Controls. It could not see another extension, and could not see a new file added to Controls either, yet the claim it backed was written repo-wide. The repo-wide sweep measured exactly ONE production ingress surface in app/src + app/extensions -- this one -- so the image track's substance was right and only its scope was overstated.

source.runId: integration/verification pass (2026-08-16): first fresh, unseen seed run through the invariant project after the undo-oracle meta-assertion landed

violation.message: THE NEW UNDO-EVIDENCE META-ASSERTION TURNED THE INVARIANT PROJECT RED ON A SEED NOBODY CHOSE. `state-consistency.spec.ts`'s rapid-fire walk failed with `the undo round-trip oracle DECIDED NOTHING across 2 checkpoint(s): 0 had nothing to undo and 2 were undecidable`, after 11 mid-window baseline rebases. It is structural, not bad luck: that walk runs at `rapidFireProbability: 0.5`, so half its actions are rapid create/delete pairs drawn from exactly the families that END the undo history (10 `fr.*` and 6 `sheet.*` in 50 actions). `WalkRunner` re-captures the baseline after every NON-checkpoint action, so a window only stays dead when the CHECKPOINT'S OWN action is a history-ender -- about 11/50 = 0.22 here. The walk had only 2 checkpoints (50 actions at the main walk's cadence of 25), giving ~0.22^2 = 5% per run of zero undo evidence. The undo track measured 0-of-12 zero-evidence walks on its own six seeds and shipped the per-walk requirement without giving the rapid-fire walk a cadence that could satisfy it.

bugs.repro: INVARIANT_SEED=20260816101 npx playwright test --project=invariant  (the rapid-fire walk derives seed 20260816102). Pre-fix: test 2 fails `undo-evidence-missing` with 2 checkpoints, both undecided.
bugs.triage: Harness. The meta-assertion is correct and stays; what was wrong is that one generated walk was configured so it could not produce the evidence the assertion requires.
bugs.fix: The rapid-fire walk gets its own cadence: `RAPID_ORACLE_EVERY_N_ACTIONS = 5` (was sharing the main walk's 25), giving 10 undo windows instead of 2 and taking P(zero evidence) from ~5e-2 to ~2e-7. `SAVE_RELOAD_EVERY_RAPID` moves 2 -> 10 so the EXPENSIVE oracle still runs exactly once per walk -- save/reload resets the undo stack, so running it more often would spend the very evidence the change exists to produce. The main walk is untouched (it decided 3 of 3 on the same seed, 36 transactions wound back).
bugs.validatedBy: app/e2e/__tests__/oracleCadenceReachable.test.ts: new case `gives the RAPID-FIRE walk a cadence its undo window can survive` asserts the rapid cadence is strictly shorter than the main one and yields >= 8 windows, and the pre-existing save/reload reachability case now reads RAPID_ORACLE_EVERY_N_ACTIONS instead of silently checking the main walk's constant. Sabotage-verified: restoring 25 fails the new case by name. Live: re-run of 4 invariant seeds after the fix.
bugs.evidenceNote: Checkpoint cost was measured from the failing run's own log (7-10s per checkpoint at 25-action windows) before choosing 5, so the extra 8 checkpoints are paid for knowingly; the windows are a fifth as long, so each undo round-trip winds back a fifth as many transactions.
bugs.notes: Found only because this pass ran the invariant project on FRESH seeds rather than the six the undo track used. A per-walk requirement has to be satisfiable by every walk that carries it, not just by the ones it was measured on.

source.runId: same run as BUG-0093 -- observed while watching the failure be minimized

violation.message: THE SHRINKER SPENT ITS WHOLE BUDGET ON A VIOLATION IT COULD NOT POSSIBLY REPRODUCE. When the rapid-fire walk failed `undo-evidence-missing`, `writeFailureBundle` handed the 50-action trace to ddmin, which ran 16+ candidate replays with EVERY ONE reported `-> pass`. It could not have gone otherwise: all three replay paths (`state-consistency`, `soak-walk`, `replay-trace`) construct their OracleBattery with `requireUndoEvidence: false` -- correctly, so a one-action shrink candidate is not judged on undo evidence -- so the verdict being minimized is one the replay function is structurally incapable of returning. ddmin reduced nothing, would have burned up to 30 replays and a 15-minute budget per failing seed, and writes a bundle whose `could not reduce` reads to the next human like a failed reproduction. It is also the wrong question: `undo-evidence-missing` is a property of the walk's CONFIGURATION (cadence vs history-ender density), not of the trace, so no subset of the actions is a smaller reproducer.

bugs.repro: Cause any walk to fail `undo-evidence-missing` (see BUG-0093) with shrinking enabled. Pre-fix: `[shrink] replay N: ... -> pass` repeated until the budget expires.
bugs.triage: Harness. Two individually-correct decisions -- a per-walk undo-evidence requirement, and waiving that requirement on replay paths -- combined into a broken one. The class of defect only an integration pass catches.
bugs.fix: `skipShrinkReason` in app/e2e/walker/failureBundle.ts already existed for exactly this (`page-crashed`, `oracle-infrastructure`); `undo-evidence-missing` is now a third entry, with a reason that states BOTH why minimization is impossible by construction AND why it is the wrong question, and points at `rebaseActions` in the details instead.
bugs.validatedBy: app/e2e/__tests__/shrinkSkip.test.ts (8 tests). Asserts the refusal, the content of the reason, that the two pre-existing refusals survive, and -- the other direction -- that ordinary product violations are still minimized. It also pins the PREMISE by reading all three replay specs for `requireUndoEvidence: false`, and that state-consistency waives it exactly ONCE (on the replay fn, never on the two generated walks). Sabotage-verified: deleting the new arm fails 2 tests by name.
bugs.notes: `skipShrinkReason` was module-private and is now exported so it has a unit tier; no behaviour change beyond the added arm.

source.runId: docs/design distribution+writeback documentation audit (calp group)

violation.message: GATHER.AT IS A WORKING FORMULA FUNCTION THAT NO CATALOG KNOWS ABOUT. `BuiltinFunction::all_catalog_entries()` (core/parser/src/ast.rs:1867) is documented in its own header as "the single source of truth for the function catalog", and it lists four of the five GATHER functions -- GATHER, GATHER.FROM, GATHER.COUNT, GATHER.SUBMITTERS (ast.rs:2412-2415) -- but not GATHER.AT. GATHER.AT is otherwise fully shipped: it lexes/parses (ast.rs:1023), renders back (ast.rs:1572), and evaluates (core/engine/src/evaluator.rs:1987, `fn_gather_at`, with five dedicated evaluator tests). Both consumers of the catalog are therefore wrong about it: `build_full_catalog` (app/src-tauri/src/formula.rs:35) omits it from the function list that drives Insert Function / autocomplete, and `get_function_template` (formula.rs:126) finds no entry and falls through to its `format!("={}()", upper)` fallback, so inserting it yields a bare `=GATHER.AT()` with no argument placeholders while its four siblings get a generated template. Nothing catches this: there is no test asserting the enum and the catalog agree (the only catalog test, `test_get_controlvalue_catalog_entry_and_aliases` in core/parser/src/tests.rs:1684, checks one unrelated function), and the deliberate-hiding mechanism that does exist -- `FunctionMeta::alias()`, ast.rs:2540, which sets `is_alias` so `build_full_catalog` filters the entry out -- was NOT used here, so this is an omission rather than an intentional hide. GATHER.AT is the one GATHER function docs/design/calp-writeback.md singles out as load-bearing ("the primitive that makes per-line-item / tabular consolidation possible"), and it is the only one a user cannot discover.

bugs.repro: 1. Open any workbook. 2. In the formula bar type `=GATHER.` -- autocomplete offers GATHER, GATHER.COUNT, GATHER.FROM and GATHER.SUBMITTERS, but never GATHER.AT. Same absence in the Insert Function dialog's `Writeback` category. 3. Invoke `get_function_template("GATHER.AT")`: it returns `=GATHER.AT()` (the not-found fallback), whereas `get_function_template("GATHER.FROM")` returns a template generated from its syntax string. 4. Confirm the function itself works regardless: `=GATHER.AT("region", ROW(B2), COLUMN(B2))` parses and evaluates normally -- so the function is present in every layer except the catalog. Unit-level: `BuiltinFunction::all_catalog_entries().iter().any(|m| m.name == "GATHER.AT")` is false while `BuiltinFunction::from_name("GATHER.AT")` is `Some(GatherAt)`.
bugs.triage: Product, frontend-visible, backend-rooted. Introduced with the cell-aware GATHER work (roadmap #4 in docs/design/writeback-review-2026-06.md, 2026-06-22), which added the parser variant, the renderer arm and the evaluator implementation plus tests -- the four steps the catalog header names -- and missed the fifth ("add ONE entry here"). The header at ast.rs:1861-1866 spells the checklist out; nothing enforces it. Not data-corrupting: the function computes correctly when typed by hand. The cost is discoverability of the single primitive that makes tabular writeback consolidation possible, plus the missing argument template. Found by documentation audit, not by any suite -- the gap between 'documented as shipped' and 'reachable by a user' is exactly what no existing oracle covers.
bugs.notes: Suggested fix is two parts, and the second is the one that matters: (a) add `FunctionMeta::new("GATHER.AT", "Writeback", "GATHER.AT(region_id, row, col)", "Returns all submitters' values for one writeback input cell (1-based absolute coordinates)")` next to its four siblings at ast.rs:2415; (b) add the exhaustiveness test that does not exist -- every `BuiltinFunction` variant reachable from `from_name` must have a catalog entry or be explicitly `alias()`-marked -- so the next function to skip step five fails the build instead of shipping invisible. Verify the coordinate convention in the syntax string against the `GATHER.AT` note in docs/design/calp-writeback.md (1-based absolute, converted to 0-based internally) before writing it. [FIXED 2026-08-17] Added the FunctionMeta::new("GATHER.AT", "Writeback", ...) entry beside its four GATHER siblings in all_catalog_entries() (core/parser/src/ast.rs). Guarded by THREE tests in core/parser/src/tests.rs, because one was not enough: (1) every_name_from_name_accepts_has_a_catalog_entry scans from_name's arms out of the source text (BuiltinFunction has no variant iterator) and diffs 521 accepted names against the catalog, with a floor assertion so a broken extraction cannot pass as a complete catalog; (2) every_catalog_entry_names_a_function_the_parser_knows covers the reverse direction, a catalog entry that yields #NAME?; (3) every_alias_entry_shadows_a_real_entry_for_the_same_function closes the loophole in (1) -- all_catalog_entries() CONTAINS alias entries but build_full_catalog filters them out, so marking GATHER.AT as an alias would have satisfied the census while leaving the function exactly as invisible. A genuine alias resolves to the same BuiltinFunction variant as some non-alias entry; a primary function marked alias does not. Both sabotages verified: removing the entry reds (1) naming GATHER.AT, downgrading it to alias() reds (3) naming GATHER.AT. NOTE: the ledger repro said from_name returns Some(GatherAt); it returns the bare variant, falling back to Custom(upper).

source.runId: docs/design BI+model documentation audit (2026-08-16): verifying pivot-drillthrough-customization.md section 6 requirement 7 ('fail-safe everywhere') against the shipped dispatch

violation.message: A PIVOT IN script DRILL MODE WHOSE SCRIPT DOES NOT REGISTER onDrillThrough SWALLOWS THE DOUBLE-CLICK ENTIRELY -- no drill, no fallback, no message. The interceptor in app/extensions/Pivot/index.ts (lines 1725-1748) branches on `behavior?.kind === "script" && hasObjectScript("pivot", pivotId)`, emits the app event `pivot:drillThrough`, and RETURNS -- skipping the built-in drillThroughToSheet path. Its own comment states the invariant it is protecting: the hasObjectScript guard exists 'so a double-click is never a silent no-op'. But hasObjectScript (app/src/api/objectScriptBadge.ts:38) only answers 'does this object have a script attached', not 'does that script handle this event'. The handler side is opt-in: the forwarder is installed only when the script calls pivot.onDrillThrough (app/src/api/scriptHost/host.ts:12090, case "pivot.onDrillThrough"), so a pivot script that registers only, say, onRefresh leaves the emitted event with no subscriber. The double-click is consumed by the interceptor (it returns true), so the user gets no drill sheet, no built-in fallback and no toast -- the exact silent no-op the guard was written to prevent, and a violation of requirement 7 of docs/design/pivot-drillthrough-customization.md section 6 ('Consent denied, capability missing, script error, or timeout -> fall back to builtin (or no-op with a toast) ... The drill never breaks the pivot').

bugs.repro: 1. Create a BI-backed pivot with at least one data cell. 2. Attach an object script to that pivot that registers ONLY `pivot.onRefresh(...)` (any body; do not call `pivot.onDrillThrough`). Mount it so hasObjectScript("pivot", pivotId) is true (the presence cache is rebuilt from loadAllObjectScripts()). 3. Open the pivot's 'Drill-through behavior...' dialog and choose the third mode, Script (DrillThroughBehaviorDialog.tsx:325-329), and save -- this persists { kind: "script" } with no query override. 4. Double-click a Data or total cell. EXPECTED (per the design and per the interceptor's own comment): either the script's drill runs, or the built-in drill opens a DrillThrough sheet, or the user is told why nothing happened. ACTUAL: nothing at all happens -- app/extensions/Pivot/index.ts emits `pivot:drillThrough`, no forwarder is subscribed for this instance, the interceptor returns true so the grid does not enter edit mode either, and no error reaches the console. Control: remove the script (or set the behavior back to Built-in) and the same double-click opens the DrillThrough sheet, proving the drill itself is healthy.
bugs.triage: Product, frontend-only, low severity but silent -- which is why it is worth an entry rather than a doc note. The fix is not the guard's existence but its precision: presence-of-a-script is a proxy for handles-this-event, and the two diverge exactly when a pivot script exists for another reason. Options: (a) have the host confirm a live subscriber for `pivot:drillThrough` on this instanceId before taking the script branch (the forwarder registry knows), falling through to drillThroughToSheet otherwise; or (b) keep the branch but arm a short timer that runs the built-in drill (or shows a toast) if the script produced nothing. (a) is the honest one -- it restores the documented 'never breaks the pivot' guarantee structurally instead of by timeout. Note the same file's script-mode branch is also the reason section 4 of the design doc never shipped: the host writes no sheet in script mode at all, by design.
bugs.notes: Found by documentation audit, not by a suite: the BI+model docs pass compared docs/design/pivot-drillthrough-customization.md against the code and found that Layers 1 AND 2 had shipped (the doc still said 'Design -- approved to build'), and that one of its seven security/UX requirements had not. The doc has been corrected in the same pass (new section '9a. As built', which cites this entry's fallback asymmetry). Two stale CODE comments were left in place deliberately, as they are not defects: app/src-tauri/src/pivot/types.rs:1540-1544 still calls Script mode 'a future mode ... planned' directly above the shipped variant, and app/extensions/Pivot/components/DrillThroughBehaviorDialog.tsx:6 says 'A Script mode is planned (Layer 2)' while the same file renders its radio button. Also unbuilt from the same design (section 6, requirement 6, NOT filed as a bug because it is a missing feature rather than a broken guarantee): no pivot paints the shared script badge -- @api drawScriptBadge's only caller in the repo is Controls/Shape/shapeRenderer.ts:617 -- so a pivot whose double-click runs code looks identical to one that does not. [FIXED 2026-08-17] The interceptor asked hasObjectScript (does a script EXIST) and then emitted pivot:drillThrough and RETURNED, skipping the built-in drill. Registering a handler is opt-in, so a script hooking only onRefresh left the event with no subscriber AND the fallback already skipped. Now it asks mountedScriptHasHook(script.id, "pivot.onDrillThrough"), and the four-fact decision lives in a pure module (app/extensions/Pivot/lib/drillDispatch.ts) so it is testable outside the 2200-line activate() closure -- modelled on Controls/lib/buttonClickDiagnosis.ts, the same pattern for the same class of bug on buttons. Every non-script verdict falls through to the built-in drill, and the two cases where a script EXISTS but cannot take the click also toast (error if not mounted, warning if mounted without the hook). NOTE the ledger suggested falling back "when the event has no subscriber" -- that is IMPOSSIBLE: emitAppEvent is a bare window.dispatchEvent and the DOM EventTarget API exposes no subscriber count, so the emitter structurally cannot know. 6 unit tests; reverting to the presence check reds 3 of them.

source.runId: docs/design security+scripting documentation audit (wave3/sandbox/package-manager group)

violation.message: THE SCRIPT-SURFACE TAXONOMY STILL DESCRIBES A RETIRED BEARER-TOKEN AUTHORIZATION MECHANISM THAT NO LONGER EXISTS IN THE CODE. `app/src/api/scriptSurfaces.ts` is the single queryable source of truth backing the Transparency pillar -- it feeds the transparency panel and is the answer to "what can this surface reach and how is it gated". Its `script-library` row is stale in two fields. (1) `gate` (scriptSurfaces.ts:158) ends: "Calls in are authorized by an unguessable host-issued token, which is delegation-transparent but not caller-identifying -- see docs/design/script-package-manager.md §10.4". (2) `containment` (:130) says exported names are routable "through one token-gated entry point". Neither is true any more. The token design was REPLACED by `base.callImport`, which authorizes on caller IDENTITY: the broker row + validator are at allowlist.ts:105 (`vCallImport`), dispatch at host.ts:2645, and the authorization is `authorizeImportCall` (host.ts:2304-2328), which resolves the alias in `scriptImports` (host.ts:2216) -- host state keyed by the CONSUMER's authoritative mount id and written only by trusted linker code -- then caps the call by that caller's own declared capabilities via `requireCallerCoversLibrary` (host.ts:2331). The token machinery is gone, not merely bypassed: `app/src/api/scriptLibraries/linker.ts:38-39` states "There is no bearer token any more. The previous design minted a 128-bit token per (realm, consumer) and baked it into the prelude", and host.ts:2174-2177 records the consequence -- "There is no credential left to leak. Handing a peer the alias string achieves nothing: the peer's own table is consulted, not the sender's." The doc section the row cites, script-package-manager.md §10.3/§10.4, has been marked CLOSED by the 2026-08-16 documentation audit, so the row now points a reader at a section that explicitly says the mechanism it describes was deleted.

bugs.repro: 1. `rg "unguessable host-issued token" app/src/api/scriptSurfaces.ts` -> matches the `script-library` row's `gate` string (line 158). 2. `rg -i token app/src/api/scriptHost/` -> NO matches; `rg -i token app/src/api/scriptLibraries/linker.ts` -> only comments recording that the token was REMOVED (lines 38-39, 308, 627). There is no token issuer, no `__addToken`/`__revokeToken`, and no `__callImport(token, ...)` entry point anywhere in the shipped code. 3. Confirm the replacement is live: `rg "base.callImport" app/src/api/scriptHost/allowlist.ts app/src/api/scriptHost/host.ts` -> allowlist.ts:105 (row + vCallImport) and host.ts:2645 (dispatch). 4. User-visible path: open the script transparency panel / surface inventory for a workbook using a `// @uses` library and read how calls into the library are gated -- it reports bearer-token, delegation-transparent, not caller-identifying. The truth is stronger: the call is refused unless THIS script declared that alias, the name is an `// @export`, and the caller's own declared-capability ceiling covers the library's.
bugs.triage: Documentation-in-code defect, not a functional one -- the ENFORCEMENT is correct and strictly stronger than what the row claims. Filed rather than silently patched because product code is out of scope for a documentation audit pass, and because the fix should be made by whoever owns the surface taxonomy. Severity low and deliberately so: the row UNDERSTATES the security property, so it cannot induce false confidence -- the failure mode is an auditor concluding the system is weaker than it is, or a maintainer 'restoring' a token mechanism to match the documentation. But the module's entire purpose is being the FIRST source of truth for exactly this question, and CLAUDE.md names it as the queryable taxonomy behind the Transparency pillar. A drifted first source of truth is worth more than a drifted doc: every mirror is regenerated from it. Note the shape of the miss -- `base.callImport` landed with its broker row, validator, dispatch, shim and the token's deletion, and updated script-package-manager.md's §10.8 checklist, but not the taxonomy row describing it. Nothing tests the `gate`/`containment` prose against the code, and nothing can: they are free text.
bugs.notes: Fix is two string edits in `app/src/api/scriptSurfaces.ts` (`script-library` row): (a) `gate` (:158) -- replace the trailing token sentence with "Calls in are authorized by CALLER IDENTITY: `base.callImport` resolves the alias against host state keyed by the consumer's mount id (host.ts:2216, authorizeImportCall :2304), refuses undeclared aliases and non-`// @export` names, and caps the call by the caller's own declared capabilities (requireCallerCoversLibrary :2331) -- see docs/design/script-package-manager.md §10.3"; (b) `containment` (:130) -- "one token-gated entry point" -> "one HOST-ONLY entry point (HOST_ONLY_EXPOSED_PREFIX, `public: false`, reachable only via hostCallExposed)". The durable improvement is the harder half: consider whether these prose fields can be anchored the way reach already is. `surface_reach()` / `OP_MANIFEST` in core/script-engine/src/manifest.rs are derived from the live interpreter and diffed both ways by `op_manifest_matches_the_live_interpreter_surface` (:668) plus interpreterReachDrift.test.ts -- which is exactly why the REACH fields did not drift while these did. A cheap first step: assert that any `gate`/`containment` string naming a symbol (`base.callImport`, `__callImport`, `__addToken`) mentions only symbols that still exist in the codebase. That would have caught this on the commit that deleted the token. [FIXED 2026-08-17] Both stale strings in app/src/api/scriptSurfaces.ts rewritten to describe the mechanism that actually runs: library calls are authorized by CALLER IDENTITY (base.callImport takes only an alias; authorizeImportCall resolves it in scriptImports, host state keyed by the calling script id and written only by the linker; then requireCallerCoversLibrary caps by the CALLER's own declared capabilities), and the containment clause now names the HOST-ONLY entry point (HOST_ONLY_EXPOSED_PREFIX + public:false, so callExposed refuses the namespace for every script). Doc citation re-pointed from section 10.4 to 10.3, which is titled "the bearer token is gone, calls are caller-identified". CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY: its :130 for the containment string is wrong, it is :129. AND ITS PROPOSED TEST HAD NO TEETH FOR THIS BUG -- the stale strings name no code symbol at all ("unguessable host-issued token" is pure prose), so a symbol-existence guard is green before AND after. The guard that works asserts the CLAIM: no gate/containment string may say token/bearer, since the only tokens left in the script host are unprotect holds and a rate-limiter bucket, neither a gate nor a containment property. It fails on the pre-fix tree naming both strings (verified by sabotage). The symbol-existence guard was added too, as forward protection for the next drift.

source.runId: journey project run 2026-08-16: 64 tests failed on timeout over 5.4 hours, starting around test 37; investigated 2026-08-16

violation.message:
THE BACKEND STOPPED RETURNING FROM TAURI COMMANDS MID-RUN WHILE EVERY LIVENESS SIGNAL STAYED GREEN. UNREPRODUCED -- filed for attribution, not as a diagnosed defect; see the evidence and the explicit non-claims below.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED. A journey run failed 64 consecutive tests, every one on timeout, never on an assertion. The first failing spec (document-store-leak) contains ZERO Playwright locators -- a grep for locator(/getBy/.click(/.fill(/waitForSelector over its 839 lines returns nothing, so no actionability wait exists that could burn 300 s. Every step goes through page.evaluate, either __TAURI__.core.invoke directly or one of the app own modules imported via __calcImport (:79-91, :94-115). Its 300 s timeouts therefore cannot be explained by a selector, a repaint, or anything in the DOM. Playwright destroys and rebuilds the worker after every failed test, and all 64 rebuilds reported a healthy app. To be precise about WHICH check ran: assertAppMounted runs once per RUN from global-setup (:128, :288), not per rebuild; what re-ran was the worker-scoped sharedPage fixture -- connectWithRetry plus a 60 s waitForSelector on the spreadsheet container (fixtures.ts:244, :316). Same shape, equally blind: CDP accepted a connection and a DOM node was visible, and both remained true throughout. Total cost 5.4 hours; the report showed 64 failures with no indication they were one event.

WHAT WAS RULED OUT, by running it. document-store-leak in isolation: 7/7 pass. Specs 7-8 plus dsl: 13 pass. Specs 1-6 plus dsl: 33 pass. THE FULL JOURNEY PROJECT, unmodified: 156 passed in 27.8 minutes. So it is not that spec, not that ordering, and not deterministic. All three harness death-modes were also excluded because each fails FAST (3 s, instantly, and 60 s respectively), whereas these burned the full 300 s.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The mechanism. A lock-order inversion in the grid locks is the leading candidate on this project's history, but nothing here proves it. Two pieces of evidence that would have decided it were destroyed by design: init_log_file OPENED the app log with .truncate(true) on EVERY app start (fixed 2026-08-17 -- it now rotates; see notes), so four later runs overwrote the only account the backend gave of itself, and results.json is overwritten per run.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD OF GUESSING. Fixing product locks with no reproduction would be speculation. The response makes the next occurrence cheap, attributed and diagnosable: e2e/wedgeGuard.ts probes the backend with a real invoke before every test (double-raced, because page.evaluate has no timeout in Playwright's API), latches after two consecutive unanswered probes, and fails every later test immediately -- turning 5.4 hours into minutes -- while global-teardown prints a banner saying the failures are ONE fact, and archives the app log per run so the evidence survives. Decision logic pinned by app/e2e/__tests__/wedgeGuard.test.ts (8 tests; sabotage measured, not estimated -- latching on the first bad probe reds 5 of 8, and putting the counter back in module memory reds exactly the restart test).

TO CLOSE THIS. A reproduction is still needed -- and the evidence needed to get one now SURVIVES (the log-truncation problem above was fixed 2026-08-17; see notes). The next occurrence will leave e2e/results/app-logs/app-dev-<stamp>.log and an APP-WEDGED.txt naming the test it was first seen before -- start there.

bugs.notes: Product-side follow-up DONE 2026-08-17: init_log_file no longer truncates. It rotates the previous session log to context_manager/history/log-<stamp>.log, retaining the last 10, so the next occurrence of this wedge leaves the backend log intact. Append was rejected deliberately: LOG_SEQ restarts at 0 per process and sort_log_file sorts the whole file by it, so appending would interleave sessions beyond reconstruction. A failed rename takes a uniquely-named file rather than truncating, since a truncating fallback IS the original defect. Pinned by 5 tests in logging.rs rotation_tests, sabotage-checked (disabling rotation reds 3).  — REVIEWED 2026-08-19, STILL OPEN, AND STILL UNDIAGNOSED. That is the finding, not a placeholder: the evidence was re-examined and it does not support a cause, so none has been recorded. WHAT COULD BE ESTABLISHED: the run can be DATED but not diagnosed. `app/e2e/results/mount-timings.log` carries exactly one 5.392-hour gap on 2026-08-16 (14:05:42.348Z -> 19:29:12.791Z), matching the recorded 5.4 hours, and the entry immediately before it ('mounted 2130ms responses=1294 samples=3') shows the app was healthy at run start — so the wedge developed MID-RUN. No backend log, trace, stack or results.json from inside that window survives. THREE CANDIDATES were examined and NONE rose above speculative: (1) a lock-order inversion in a census blind spot — `acquisitions_in` matches only ['.read(', '.write(', '.lock('] and '.lock(' is not a substring of '.lock_pending(', hiding ~76 acquisitions, and real inverted sites exist inside that blind spot — but none is reachable from the first failing spec; (2) async-runtime starvation; (3) stdout backpressure through the harness pipe. Candidate 1 is the seductive one and must NOT be written down as the cause: shipping a lock reorder with no reproduction would earn the sentence 'BUG-0098 fixed by lock-order correction' for a defect that was never diagnosed. WHY 'LEAVE UNTIL IT RECURS' WAS NOT ENOUGH: it is only rational if the NEXT occurrence is diagnostic, and it would not have been. The marker records a verdict word, a test title and a timestamp; the archived app log carries only non-debug lines so it simply goes quiet; the trace photographs the healthy half. The policy committed the project to paying for a second five-hour occurrence and learning nothing. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD — HARNESS ONLY, no product code touched. TWO of the items were not additions at all but live defects in the existing instrumentation, each producing a CONFIDENT FALSEHOOD: (a) `Number(process.env.E2E_WEDGE_BACKEND_MS ?? 5_000)` accepted an EMPTY string (`??` is not triggered by '', and Number('') is 0) and a malformed one (Number('5s') is NaN); setTimeout(fn, 0 | NaN) fires immediately, so a perfectly HEALTHY run would latch as wedged and write the very marker a future reader would trust. Now refused, with a warning naming the ignored value. (b) `global-teardown` archived `results/app-dev.log` on EXISTENCE alone, so under E2E_MANUAL a leftover log from an earlier run could be filed under THIS run's timestamp — the wrong evidence under the right name, for a defect whose entire difficulty is that its evidence was destroyed. Now checked against a run-start stamp published by global-setup. (c) `globalTimeout` of 2 hours added (a journey project passes in ~28 minutes, so 4x margin). The wedge guard latches only for a wedged BACKEND; a renderer-side hang happens ABOVE it and pays full price per test with no latch and no marker. Eight tests in `app/e2e/__tests__/wedgeInstrumentation.test.ts`, sabotage-checked: reverting the parse guard reds the source assertion while the behavioural cases still pass, which is why both halves exist. TO CLOSE THIS: a recurrence that now yields a diagnosable artefact, or a reproduction. Explicitly NOT closeable by a speculative fix.

source.runId: adversarial review of the open-item 1.6 implementation (2026-08-17): 5 lenses, 24 findings raised, 17 refuted, 4 confirmed

violation.message:
BUG-0086 WAS FIXED ONLY FOR THE LOWERCASE SPELLING. A decompression bomb whose base64 tag is capitalised -- data:image/png;BASE64,<4 KB 30000x30000 PNG> -- or whose base64 BODY is percent-escaped -- data:image/png;base64,%69VBORw... -- was classified as a POLICY refusal ("safe on screen, leave inline") and delivered to the WebView decoder, allocating ~3.6 GB of RGBA, exactly as BUG-0086 described.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is the interesting part: the hazard/policy split is only as good as the agreement between the HOST parser and the parser that ACTUALLY RUNS, and the host was STRICTER. decode_image_data_url (core/calcula-format/src/media.rs) required a byte-exact lowercase ";base64" and its hand-rolled decode_base64 returns None at the first "%". The WHATWG data-URL processor WebView2 implements matches the base64 tag ASCII case-insensitively and PERCENT-DECODES the body BEFORE base64-decoding. Every string in that gap took the None arm of judge_inline_image, and that arm treated "could not parse" as "harmless" -- so no byte, dimension or pixel cap ever looked at the payload, while paintableUrl (app/extensions/Controls/Image/imageRenderer.ts:214) hands any non-handle string straight to img.src (:246). The widened exceeds_byte_cap_encoded added by the 1.6 work repeated the same wrong literal, so there were TWO copies of one wrong spelling.

REPRODUCTION: publish a .calp whose controls.json holds src = "data:image/png;BASE64,<base64 of a 30000x30000 single-colour PNG>" and sign it normally. Subscribe and pull (calp_commands.rs:2698). Before the fix: report.refused == 1, the string is materialised verbatim, written into the subscriber own .cala, and decoded by the renderer. The percent-escaped variant needs no case difference at all.

FIXED 2026-08-17, two parts. (1) The host now agrees with the browser: one shared ends_with_base64_tag (case-insensitive) used by both call sites so they cannot drift again, plus percent-decoding of the body. Both are pure widenings of what the host can READ, so they strictly increase inspection coverage. (2) The default is INVERTED: LeaveInline now requires a payload the host could actually read, and an undecodable string declaring a RASTER format is dropped -- "we could not parse it" is not evidence the renderer cannot. SVG keeps its tolerance, being the one declared type this host never decodes by design.

WHY THE SUITE COULD NOT SEE IT: the BUG-0086 regression test builds its fixture with the data_url() helper, which is format!("data:image/png;base64,{}") -- lowercase only. Now covered by a_bomb_spelled_with_an_uppercase_base64_tag_is_dropped, a_bomb_with_a_percent_escaped_base64_body_is_dropped, an_undecodable_raster_declaration_is_dropped_not_tolerated and svg_keeps_its_policy_tolerance_under_the_inverted_default; reverting the three fixes reds 4 tests.

bugs.notes: Sibling of BUG-0086, same harm class, different spelling. As-built record: docs/design/open-item-1-6-calp-media-bound-2026-08-17.md. The generalisable lesson: when a host validates something another engine will parse, the host parser must accept AT LEAST everything that engine accepts, or the difference is a bypass.

source.runId: macro-live-edit.spec.ts test 3 failed on a freshly launched app on 2026-08-18, having also failed at 07:07:35Z and 08:01:02Z in an earlier multi-spec session; instrumented and attributed the same day

violation.message: A TOAST NOTIFICATION IS A CLICK SURFACE OVER THE GRID, SO ANY ON-GRID CONTROL IN THE BOTTOM-RIGHT IS DEAD FOR THE 5 SECONDS THE TOAST LIVES. ToastContainer already sets pointerEvents:'none' on the container, and its comment explains why (a layout box at z-index 9999 over the grid swallows clicks). The fix was applied to the container only: each ToastItem re-enabled pointerEvents:'auto' on its whole 380x~58 box, so the same defect survived at a smaller size. WHAT WAS OBSERVED: the product announces 'Button created at P63'; a click on that button 312 ms later never reaches the grid, and the macro's output cell stays empty for a full 60-second poll. WHY IT WAS HARD TO ATTRIBUTE: the test observed only the cell, and an empty cell is equally consistent with 'the click never arrived', 'the click arrived and the run path broke', and 'the macro ran and wrote nothing'. Two separate investigations reconstructed the geometry from source rather than measuring it and reached opposite conclusions; one computed the toast's top border at y=705.6 against a click at y=705.0 and concluded the toast missed by 0.6 px. WHAT SETTLED IT: instrumenting the spec to ask the PRODUCT instead of arithmetic. hitTestOverlays (app/src/api/gridOverlays.ts:252), the same function the canvas click path consults, returns HIT button id=control-0-62-15 at r62c15 for the click point -- so the click was deliverable -- while document.elementFromPoint at the same page point returns a <div> inside [data-toast]. Blink's point hit test lands in the toast despite the 0.6 px arithmetic. CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT (same spec, same lever, only Toast.tsx changed between rows): before the fix, toast-dismissal OFF = 1 failed / 4 passed and ON = 5 passed; after the fix, toast-dismissal OFF = 5 passed. NOT A REGRESSION from any recent commit: the toast body has been a surface since the container-only fix, and nothing clicked that corner of the grid until this test did.

repro.description: app/e2e/tests/macro-live-edit.spec.ts:1063 -- '3. a linked button runs the LIVE-edited macro (no save, no reopen)', sub-step 'baseline: the button runs the ORIGINAL macro'. The spec anchors its button at P63, the bottom-right of the grid, which is exactly where ToastContainer is positioned (bottom:36, right:16). Any toast on screen at click time eats the click. Reproduces on a freshly launched app; NOT residue.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: ToastItem set pointerEvents:'auto' on the toast body to keep its OK button clickable. Only the OK button needs to be a surface; the rest of the toast is text.

fix.diffSummary: Toast body -> pointerEvents:'none'; the OK button re-enables 'auto' so the toast stays dismissable. New unit test asserts all three layers (body none / OK auto / container none), each sabotage-checked independently: reverting any one reds exactly its own assertion and no other. macro-live-edit.spec.ts additionally gained a delivery probe that asserts hitTestOverlays finds the control BEFORE the outcome poll, and attaches a diagnosis on failure -- so this class can never again cost a day of attribution.
validatedBy: app/src/shell/Toast/__tests__/toastClickThrough.test.tsx
app/e2e/tests/macro-live-edit.spec.ts

bugs.notes: The generalisable lesson is about the TEST, not the toast: an assertion that observes only an end state cannot attribute a failure, and a 60-second poll on an empty cell is the most expensive possible way to learn nothing. Assert DELIVERY separately from OUTCOME whenever a gesture crosses a layer boundary. Note also that the click is dispatched with force:true, which skips Playwright's actionability checks -- a point landing on nothing dispatches into nothing and throws nothing, so the harness will not volunteer this.

source.runId: vba-idioms-wave3.spec.ts:468 'renders edge-only' failed on a freshly launched app on 2026-08-18; diagnosed from the run's own Playwright trace, which stores the sampled pixels

violation.message: EVERY CELL BORDER PAINTED AT HALF ITS NOMINAL WEIGHT, AND VERTICAL ONES SMEARED ACROSS TWO DEVICE PIXELS AT HALF ALPHA. Two stacked defects in app/src/core/lib/gridRenderer/rendering/cells.ts. (1) THE CLIP. The per-cell clip exists to cut overlong TEXT, and the border pass ran inside it. A 'medium' border is 2px centred on the boundary, so the clip discarded the outer half: borders rendered at half weight, wholly inside the cell, instead of straddling the boundary the way Excel draws them. (2) NO DEVICE-PIXEL SNAPPING. drawGridLines has always snapped its hairline (rendering/grid.ts:189-191); drawBorderLine never did. Row boundaries are integral (defaultCellHeight 20) but column boundaries are not (defaultCellWidth 64.29, core/types/types.ts:256), so horizontal borders happened to land on one whole device pixel while vertical ones split across two. WHAT WAS OBSERVED: the test sampled a 5x12 band on the right edge of a red 'medium' outline and got EXACTLY ZERO red pixels, while the TOP edge of the same outline passed its threshold. The trace's stored pixels show every one of the band's 12 rows as 255,255,255 | 255,107,107 | 238,131,131 | 255,255,255 | 255,255,255 -- one red line spread over two pixels at ~58%/42%, against a predicate needing >=64.7% coverage. WHY IT SURFACED ONLY NOW: at dpr 2 the surviving half-stroke is 2 device pixels, so one is always fully covered. The defect is LATENT, not a regression -- it became visible when the machine moved from a 200% display to 100% and the golden corpus followed. A THIRD PROBLEM THE FIX HAD TO SOLVE: once borders straddle the boundary, painting them in place is wrong regardless of the clip. The cell loop is row-major, so a RIGHT or BOTTOM border spilling forward is erased when the neighbour fills its background, while LEFT and TOP borders spill backwards and survive. The ordering is the defect, so the borders are now collected and stroked after every background in the viewport is down.

repro.description: app/e2e/tests/vba-idioms-wave3.spec.ts:468 -- '1. setRangeFormat {bold,textColor,numberFormat,borderOutline} on W61:X63 round-trips and renders edge-only', sub-step 'RENDERED: bold percent display + edge-only red outline'. The RIGHT-edge probe expects >0.15 red and receives exactly 0; the TOP-edge probe on the same outline passes. Requires dpr 1 -- at dpr 2 the assertion passes despite the defect.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The border pass sits inside the per-cell text clip and strokes unsnapped raw coordinates, so half of every stroke is discarded and the remainder lands on a fractional device-pixel boundary on the horizontal axis.

fix.diffSummary: drawBorderLine now derives the device scale from the canvas transform and snaps by PARITY (odd device widths to a pixel centre, even to a pixel edge), matching what grid.ts has always done for the gridline hairline -- a thin border provably lands on the same device pixel as the gridline it replaces. Edge borders are queued during the cell pass and stroked in a single pass afterwards, so a border may straddle its boundary without the next cell's background erasing it. Contested boundaries collapse to ONE stroke (heavier wins, ties to the later cell), which is a deliberate behaviour change: at full weight the two halves are coincident rather than disjoint, so without dedupe a thin grey neighbour would punch a stripe through a thick black border and an rgba border would double-composite. The double-border ornament derives BOTH rules from ONE snapped boundary -- snapping each independently makes Math.round tie the same way and shifts the whole ornament off an already-crisp integral boundary. Diagonals stay inside the per-cell clip and are not snapped, since snapping one axis of a diagonal skews it.
validatedBy: app/src/core/lib/gridRenderer/rendering/cellBorders.test.ts
app/e2e/tests/vba-idioms-wave3.spec.ts
fix.notes: 13 unit tests, four of them sabotage-checked independently: reverting the clip reds T1/T2/T8/T9, removing the dedupe reds T8/T9, snapping the double rules per-rule reds T10, and dropping the snapping reds 6. The live probe that reported 0 now passes.

bugs.notes: Two lessons worth keeping. First, the asymmetry WAS the clue: a defect that shows on one axis and not the other points at the difference between the axes, which here is that column widths are fractional (64.29) and row heights are not (20). Second, the fix was designed twice: an adversarial review caught that naive per-rule snapping REGRESSES the double border on the integral axis, and that removing the clip without deduping creates a new punch-through artefact that exists neither before the fix nor in Excel. Neither was visible from the failing test. See also [related] the same file's headers.ts sibling, which has the same unsnapped fractional-boundary problem and was deliberately NOT changed here because it moves 49 grid-bearing goldens.

source.runId: found by code inspection while fixing the border clip/snapping defect on 2026-08-18; verified independently by reading the render paths, NOT by running the app

violation.message: WITH A FREEZE OR A SPLIT ACTIVE, NO CELL BORDER RENDERS AT ALL. UNVERIFIED AGAINST THE RUNNING APP -- filed for attribution from a code reading, not as a reproduced defect. WHAT WAS OBSERVED (statically): panes are painted by renderZone (app/src/core/lib/gridRenderer/core.ts:230), which calls drawCellTextZone (core.ts:340). That function's body contains no reference to borders at all -- confirmed by scanning its whole body for /border/i, which returns nothing -- whereas the non-frozen painter drawCellText (rendering/cells.ts) draws all six sides. renderZone is the path for BOTH split panes (core.ts:809, 816, 823, 829) and frozen panes (core.ts:880, 886, 893, 900). WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that this has been seen on screen; that it affects the unfrozen path (it does not -- that is the path the sibling entry fixes); that no other code supplies borders for these zones by some route not found. TO CLOSE THIS: freeze a pane over a bordered range in the running app and look, then either fix drawCellTextZone to share the border queue drawCellText now uses, or reclassify. An E2E probe modelled on vba-idioms-wave3.spec.ts:468 with a freeze applied would settle it in one run.

bugs.notes: Deliberately filed WITHOUT triage or fix. The sibling entry's fix does not touch this path, so closing that one must not be read as closing this. Scope was stated honestly in the border fix's own design review rather than being quietly absorbed into it.  — CLOSED 2026-08-19, and it was CONFIRMED before it was fixed. The entry was filed from a code reading with 'never seen on screen' stated as a limit; a unit test now demonstrates it: the same bordered-cell fixture draws 4 border strokes unfrozen and 0 with a freeze active. FIX: the pane painter draws the four edge borders in BOTH of its branches, using an edge resolution EXTRACTED from `drawCellText` (`resolveEdgeBorders`/`strokeEdgeBorders` in cells.ts) rather than copied — a second copy of a formatting rule drifts on the first default change, which this repo has already paid for once with the Macro Recorder's button recipe. TWO BRANCHES, and that mattered: the pane painter handles empty and non-empty cells on separate paths, and a bordered EMPTY cell (the ordinary 'draw a box' case) returned before any border work. The first version of the test used only an empty cell, so sabotaging the content branch PASSED all three cases — the gap was found by the sabotage, not by review. Five tests now, and each branch reds exactly its own two. SIBLING DEFECT FOUND AND FILED SEPARATELY (BUG-0105): the pane painter runs NO style interceptors at all, so CONDITIONAL FORMATTING never reaches a frozen or split pane — not its fills, not its fonts, and so not its borders either. That is strictly bigger than this entry and is NOT fixed here; the empty `{}` passed to resolveEdgeBorders is the honest spelling of 'no CF available at this point', with a comment saying so.

source.runId: found 2026-08-18 by a sweep for open work recorded in NEITHER open-items.md NOR the ledger; every claim below re-verified by hand against the code, not run in the app

violation.message: A TIMELINE SLICER IS NEVER SAVED, HAS NO UNDO ARM, AND LEAKS INTO THE NEXT DOCUMENT. Insert Timeline is a shipped, one-click ribbon button on the PivotTable Analyze tab (app/extensions/Pivot/components/PivotAnalyzeSections.tsx:292-305 -> showDialog('timelineSlicer:insertDialog'); the extension is registered at app/extensions/manifest.ts:215), and TimelineSlicerState (managed at app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:4839) reaches no save path at all. MEASURED with node: /timeline/i occurs ZERO times in app/src-tauri/src/persistence.rs and ZERO times in app/src-tauri/src/calp_commands.rs. THREE CONSEQUENCES, and only the first is named anywhere in the tree: (1) SILENT TOTAL LOSS. The user inserts a timeline, saves, reopens, and it is simply gone. assemble_workbook_for_save never reads the state. (2) NO UNDO RESTORE ARM, so a cascade delete records nothing to bring back (app/src-tauri/src/object_deps.rs:63-67 says so in a comment). (3) CROSS-DOCUMENT LEAK, which nobody has written down anywhere: reset_document_scoped_stores (app/src-tauri/src/persistence.rs:3803-3812) takes AppState, UserFilesState, SlicerState, RibbonFilterState, PaneControlState, ScriptState, PivotState and BiState -- TimelineSlicerState is NOT among them, and it is a separate managed Tauri state. So a timeline from document A survives File > New / Open into document B. That is the same class as the 2026-08-10 document-scoped-state defect, which was closed by adding exactly this function; this store was never enrolled in it. WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the gap is recorded ONLY in code comments (timeline_slicer/commands.rs:85-88, object_deps.rs:63-67) and in the 1.33 MB archive (docs/design/open-decisions-2026-08.md:8573-8576), which the project's own rules say must never be read as live status. docs/design/open-items.md does not mention it. A limitation documented only in a comment is invisible to the open-items list BY CONSTRUCTION.

bugs.notes: Filed OPEN with no triage and no fix, deliberately: consequence (3) is a data-integrity bug that should be fixed immediately and cheaply (enrol TimelineSlicerState in reset_document_scoped_stores, the same one-line enrolment every other document-scoped store has), while (1) needs an owner call this repo's own .cala rules frame precisely: bump format_version to 8, or declare a manifest feature id with an unconditional read. The rule in CLAUDE.md points at the feature id -- an older reader that drops a timeline loses a filter control, which is VISIBLE loss rather than a misread document -- but that is the owner's call and it also needs a .calp carry decision. Do not close this entry when (3) lands; it covers all three. — UPDATE 2026-08-19: PERSISTENCE HAS LANDED (consequence 1); the cross-document leak (3) was fixed 2026-08-18. Timelines now save to a `timeline_slicers.json` section declared by a manifest FEATURE ID with an unconditional read, and NO format_version bump — an older reader drops an unknown section rather than misreading it, verified rather than assumed: `Manifest.features` is a bare `Vec<String>` with no whitelist, nothing in the tree uses `deny_unknown_fields`, and unknown ZIP entries are never enumerated. The store became `Persisted<T>`, which mattered more than expected: SIX of the seven timeline commands did not take `FileState` at all, so even once this was a save source they could not have dirtied the document — the close prompt and AutoRecover both read that one flag. Orphans are pruned on the WRITE side and rows sorted by id, so the load needs no ordering dependency on pivots and a save is byte-stable. `.calp` CARRIES timelines, because the pivot filter they produce already travelled: shipping the effect without the control would pin a subscriber to the publisher's last date range with no way to change it. Dead code removed on the way — `update_timeline_scroll` had ZERO callers and would have persisted a constant 0.0. Two round-trip tests, sabotage-checked: deleting the read-back reds the round trip with 'the timeline did not survive save -> load'. Both censuses caught the new field and forced a decision (`.calp` CARRIED, `.xlsx` REPORTED as 'Timeline slicers'). STILL OPEN: consequence 2, the UNDO ARM. A cascade delete still records nothing, so deleting a timeline is now a loss the user cannot undo — a STRONGER reason to finish it than before, because the object is no longer ephemeral. — CLOSED 2026-08-19: the UNDO ARM has landed, so all three consequences are fixed. Three restore kinds (`timeline_slicer`, `_create`, `_delete`), each recording the SYMMETRIC inverse so redo works — the half that fails silently and is easiest to forget. All six mutating commands now capture: create records its id, delete BINDS the removed object (it was previously discarded, which is why a deleted timeline could not come back) in the SAME transaction as the object-script prune, and the four update_* commands capture the pre-edit clone before any field is written. The cascade records its casualties too, which unblocks four commands that until now destroyed timelines irrecoverably: delete_pivot_table, delete_rows, delete_columns and off_sheet_structural_edit. ORDER is load-bearing there — entries replay in reverse, so the timeline must be recorded BEFORE the caller's pivot entry or undo restores a control pointing at a pivot that does not exist yet; a test asserts that ordering directly. Domains are `MutationDomains::of(Slicer)`, NOT a new domain and never `none()`: ObjectKind::TimelineSlicer already maps to UiDomain::Slicer and the Shell fans it to both refresh events, so `none()` would restore the store and leave the canvas stale — the default_row_height failure exactly. `defer: true`, and the legacy prefix guard needed widening because `starts_with("slicer")` does not match `timeline_slicer`. Four round-trip tests, sabotage-checked: dropping the recorded inverse reds the create/redo case while the other three still pass. KNOWN LIMITATION, deliberately not fixed here: a timeline's selection is also pushed into the pivot by the frontend bridge. In the cascade case both live in one transaction and stay consistent; for an isolated update_timeline_selection, undo restores the timeline while the pivot keeps the old filter until a second Ctrl+Z. The correct fix is one backend transaction writing both, per the Seam Rule — filed separately rather than papered over with a frontend re-apply, which would race the pivot's own restore in the same deferred pass.

source.runId: found 2026-08-18 by a sweep for open work recorded in neither open-items.md nor the ledger; both arms re-verified by hand against the code

violation.message: SORTING AND FILTERING BY CONDITIONAL-FORMATTING ICON ARE SILENT NO-OPS THAT REPORT SUCCESS. Both arms are stubs that return the wrong answer without saying so, and one of them is offered to the user by name in a dialog. (1) SORT: `SortOn::Icon` (app/src-tauri/src/commands/data.rs:5729-5740) carries the comment "Icon sorting not yet implemented - fall back to value comparison" and does exactly that — it sorts by VALUE and returns Ok. The Sorting extension offers it explicitly: app/extensions/Sorting/components/SortLevelRow.tsx:183 renders `<option value="icon">Conditional Formatting Icon</option>`. So a user picks 'Conditional Formatting Icon', the rows reorder (by value), and nothing anywhere says the request was not honoured. A sort that silently sorts by the wrong key is worse than one that refuses. (2) FILTER: `FilterOn::Icon` (app/src-tauri/src/autofilter.rs:884-889) has an EMPTY arm whose comment ends "For now, icon-filtered rows are always shown" — the predicate falls through to true, so the filter hides nothing at all and the sheet looks unfiltered while reporting a filter is applied. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FEATURE: this is the class where the product returns a plausible WRONG answer rather than an error, which is the hardest kind for a user to catch — the rows did move, so the operation looks like it worked. RECORDED NOWHERE until now: neither arm appears in docs/design/open-items.md or the ledger; the only trace was the two code comments quoted above, which are invisible to any status read.

bugs.notes: Two dispositions, and the cheap one should not wait for the expensive one. REFUSING LOUDLY is minutes: make `SortOn::Icon` and `FilterOn::Icon` return an explicit Err (or have the Sorting extension not offer the option) so the user learns the truth immediately. IMPLEMENTING is larger and needs the CF evaluation context at sort/filter time, which is what the filter's own comment says is missing. The owner's call is only on sequencing — whether to ship the refusal now and implement later — not on whether silence is acceptable. — UPDATE 2026-08-18: the REFUSAL half has landed. reject_unimplemented_sort_on (commands/data.rs) refuses at BOTH sort entry points (sort_range and sort_range_off_sheet) and inspects EVERY level, not just the first — a guard reading only fields[0] would have mis-sorted level 2 silently, the same defect one level down. apply_auto_filter_inner refuses an icon criteria before any gate. Five tests in commands/icon_refusal_tests.rs, including two that pin the REACHABILITY claims the guards rest on (filterOn/sortOn still deserialize as "icon" over IPC) so a wire rename retires the guard rather than silently disarming it. Sabotage-checked: disabling the sort guard reds exactly its two tests. THE ENTRY STAYS OPEN — icon sort and icon filter are still not implemented; only the lying is fixed.

source.runId: found 2026-08-19 while fixing BUG-0102; verified by reading the pane painter, not by running the app

violation.message: CONDITIONAL FORMATTING DOES NOT REACH A FROZEN OR SPLIT PANE AT ALL. `renderZone` -> `drawCellTextZone` (app/src/core/lib/gridRenderer/core.ts) paints every cell of every pane INSTEAD of `drawCellText`, and it runs NO style interceptors: a repo-wide grep of core.ts for hasStyleInterceptors/applyStyleInterceptors/useInterceptors returns NOTHING, while `drawCellText` consults them per cell. So the moment a user freezes a pane or splits the window, every conditional-formatting fill, font colour, data bar and icon stops being drawn in that pane — the cell reverts to its static style. STRICTLY BIGGER THAN BUG-0102, which was the same painter missing plain cell BORDERS and is fixed. That fix passes an empty `{}` where the main painter passes the interceptor-resolved style, with a comment saying why — so CF-driven borders are still missing in panes along with everything else CF does. NOT SEEN ON SCREEN. Verified by reading the two painters and by the absence of any interceptor call in the zone path; no app run was made. To confirm: apply a conditional format to a range, freeze a pane above it, and look.

bugs.notes: The fix is not simply 'call the interceptors here too': the main painter resolves an effective style per cell and the zone painter has no equivalent plumbing, so this needs the same extraction treatment BUG-0102's borders got — one resolver both painters share, rather than a second interceptor call site that can drift. Worth checking at the same time whether the pane painter is missing anything else the main one does; borders and CF were both found by reading it, which suggests nobody has diffed the two painters end to end. — CLOSED 2026-08-19, and CONFIRMED before being fixed. The entry was filed from a code reading with 'not seen on screen' stated as a limit. A unit test now demonstrates it at the seam: with a style interceptor registered, the unfrozen grid paints its fill and a frozen pane paints nothing. FIX: one exported resolveEffectiveStyle in cells.ts, called by BOTH painters. The obvious fix — a second applyStyleInterceptors call site in the pane painter — was deliberately rejected: two copies of the seed step drift on the first field added to BaseStyleInfo, and the pane would then be subtly wrong rather than obviously wrong. The main painter was rerouted through the same function, so there is genuinely one copy and not two. The resolved style now drives the pane's background, borders, bold, italic, font size, font family and text colour. The border call that BUG-0102 left as an empty object literal now receives it, which closes the hole that fix explicitly documented. BOTH BRANCHES, and that was the lesson from BUG-0102: the pane painter handles empty and non-empty cells on separate paths, and a conditional format on a BLANK cell is ordinary. Four tests, sabotage-checked independently — disabling interceptors on either branch reds exactly that branch's case and no other. Asserted at the INTERCEPTOR SEAM rather than with a CF fixture: conditional formatting is one consumer of that seam, so the test covers CF and anything else registered through it, and needs no rule engine in a renderer unit test. STILL WORTH DOING, and not done here: nobody has diffed the two painters end to end. Borders (BUG-0102) and interceptors (this) were both found by READING the pane painter, which is weak evidence that they are the last two.

source.runId: found 2026-08-19 while designing icon filtering (BUG-0104); the design flagged it as an incidental risk to its own wire-shape change, and it was then verified by reading the loader

violation.message: A MALFORMED autofilters.json SILENTLY DELETES EVERY AUTOFILTER IN THE WORKBOOK, AND THE NEXT SAVE MAKES THE LOSS PERMANENT. app/src-tauri/src/persistence.rs:3688-3697, on the .cala load path: if the section is present but `serde_json::from_slice::<AutoFilterStorage>` fails, the `else` arm runs `auto_filters.clear()`. No error is returned, nothing is logged, and the user is not told. The document opens looking fine, with every filter gone; saving then writes the empty state back over the file that still had them. THIS IS THE CLASS THE .cala RULES CALL OUT BY NAME: the test for whether a section deserves a version link is whether an older reader would MISHANDLE the document or merely lose something, and 'a stale workbook that comes back looking calculated' is the example of a drop that is a LIE. A silent clear on a PARSE FAILURE is the same lie without even a version mismatch to explain it. NOTE the two arms are not equivalent and only one is wrong: the outer `else` (no autofilters.json at all) clearing is CORRECT -- a document with no filters has none. It is the inner one, where the section EXISTS and could not be read, that destroys data. WHY IT MATTERS NOW: any change to the serialized shape of a filter makes this reachable. BUG-0104's icon-filter work adds a field to FilterCriteria, so a file written by one build and opened by another is exactly the scenario that trips it.

bugs.notes: The fix is small but the DECISION is the owner's: refuse the load with a clear error (safest, and consistent with the reader refusing a format_version it cannot understand), or keep the filters it CAN parse and report the rest, or preserve the raw bytes so a later build can recover them. What must not survive is the silent clear. Whatever is chosen, the same audit should sweep the sibling sections on that load path -- this pattern was found by reading ONE of them, and nothing suggests it is the only one.  — FIXED 2026-08-19, and the chosen remedy is NOT the one first recommended. I proposed refusing the load outright; that is disproportionate — a workbook is not unopenable because a filter is, and this projects own .cala rule says a section an older reader cannot understand may be DROPPED provided the loss is VISIBLE. The sin was the silence, not the loss. So: PER-SHEET RECOVERY plus a report. AutoFilterStorage is keyed by sheet, so the loader now decodes to HashMap<usize, Value> first and then per entry — one corrupt sheet costs only its own filter instead of every filter in the workbook. Whatever is lost is named in a log_warn! AND emitted as a "document:load-warnings" event, because a log line nobody opens is the same silence in a different place. A wholly unreadable section still recovers nothing, but now says so. The outer arm (no section at all) was always correct and is untouched: a document with no filters genuinely has none. Five tests, sabotage-checked — reverting to the whole-section decode reds the source assertion that pins the shape.

source.runId: found 2026-08-19 while designing icon sort/filter (BUG-0104); the design named it as a PREREQUISITE rather than residue, and it was then verified by reading both lookups

violation.message: THE CONDITIONAL-FORMATTING ICON A USER SEES CAN COME FROM A DISABLED RULE. The drawn glyph is a JOIN OF TWO INDEPENDENT LOOKUPS that can disagree: (1) the icon INDEX comes from the backend, which cascades correctly — it skips !enabled, honours stop_if_true, and respects priority; (2) the icon SET (which glyph family) comes from `findMatchingRuleId(row, col, "iconSet")` (app/extensions/ConditionalFormatting/lib/cfStore.ts:254-274), which matches on rule TYPE and geometric range containment ONLY. It does not read `rule.enabled`, does not honour `stop_if_true`, does not consider priority, and returns the FIRST match in array order. CONSEQUENCE: a DISABLED five-icon rule listed before an enabled three-icon rule over the same range makes the renderer draw a five-arrow glyph indexed 0..2 — a picture assembled from two different rules, one of which the user switched off. AND A HARD-CODED FALLBACK: when no rule id resolves, the renderer silently draws `threeTrafficLights1` (iconSetRenderer.ts:60) rather than nothing, so a cell can show traffic lights that no rule asked for. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE PICTURE: 'sort by the icon I can see' has no referent while the displayed icon is not a single value. This is the prerequisite for BUG-0104's icon sorting, not a cosmetic sibling of it — sorting on a glyph the renderer computed from a disabled rule would produce an order the user cannot explain from what is on screen.

bugs.notes: The fix makes the displayed icon ONE value decided in one place: carry the icon SET (and the rule id) on the backend's per-cell evaluation result alongside the index it already returns, so the renderer reads a single resolved answer instead of re-deriving half of it with different rules. That deletes the second lookup rather than patching it, which matters because patching `findMatchingRuleId` to check `enabled` would still leave two implementations of the cascade that can drift. Expect visual-baseline churn on any workbook with overlapping or disabled icon rules — that churn IS the bug becoming visible. — CLOSED 2026-08-19. The icon is now ONE value: the backend carries the resolved icon SET (and the producing rule id) beside the index it already returned, stamped in the loop that applies enabled/priority/stop_if_true, so it is the correctly-cascaded answer by construction. The frontend's second search is DELETED rather than patched: teaching findMatchingRuleId about `enabled` would have left two implementations of the cascade that can drift, which is how this arose. The hard-coded threeTrafficLights1 fallback is gone too — a cell with an index but no resolved set is now SKIPPED, because a wrong glyph is indistinguishable from a right one on screen and that is exactly what let this survive. Also extracted `evaluate_conditional_formats_for`, a pure twin of the Tauri command taking explicit refs and an explicit rule list. The cascade had NO direct unit coverage before this, because the only entry point took State<AppState> and was hard-wired to the active sheet. Four tests now, including the exact defect shape (a disabled FiveArrows rule listed FIRST must not supply the glyph family for an enabled ThreeArrows rule) — sabotage-checked: dropping the carried set reds three of the four. That extraction is also step one of BUG-0104: sort and filter need to resolve icons for a NAMED sheet, not whichever one is on screen. NOT YET DONE, and worth knowing: no visual baseline covers overlapping or disabled icon rules, so the corpus did not move. The churn this fix would cause is the bug becoming visible, and its absence means the corpus never saw the bug either.
